article_content: A 200-year-old sealed Selters stoneware bottle, discovered aboard a recovered shipwreck from the Baltic Sea near Poland, was found to contain a 14% alcohol distillate rather than its original mineral water. Tests indicate the alcohol may be diluted vodka or gin. The bottle was found during exploration of the F-53-31 shipwreck in Gdańsk Bay, near the Polish coast, in June. Researchers believe the bottle dates from 1806 to 1830 and was likely manufactured in Ranschbach, Germany, about 25 miles from the original Selters spring. Selters is a renowned German supplier of carbonated mineral water, which has been sought after for around 1,000 years due to its reputed health benefits. The original springs in the Taunus Mountains dried up in the early 19th century, making the ceramic stoneware bottles rare. Tomasz Bednarz, an underwater archaeologist from the National Maritime Museum, led the recovery effort. The bottle and its contents were sent to the J.S. Hamilton chemical laboratory in Gdynia, where tests determined the alcohol is safe to drink, though it reportedly has an unpleasant smell. In addition to the Selters bottle, the team found fragments of ceramics, a small bowl, some pieces of dinnerware, and stones at a depth of 12.2 metres (40 feet) in Gdańsk Bay. Selters mineral water is still sold today as a luxury product in modern glass bottles, and the water’s quality is said to be similar to that from centuries ago.
translated_content: 一只密封的塞尔特斯陶瓷瓶在波兰附近波罗的海的一处沉船遗址被发现，距今已有200年，瓶内竟不是原始的矿泉水，而是含有14%酒精的蒸馏酒。检测结果显示，这可能是被稀释的伏特加或杜松子酒。 该瓶于六月在格但斯克湾靠近波兰海岸的F-53-31沉船探险中被发现。研究人员认为，该瓶约制造于1806年至1830年，产地或为德国兰施巴赫，距离最初的塞尔特斯水泉约25英里。 塞尔特斯是德国著名的碳酸矿泉水供应商，因其据称具有健康益处，约1000年来受到追捧。塔乌努斯山的原始泉水于19世纪初干涸，这使得陶制经典水瓶变得稀有。 国家海事博物馆的水下考古学家托马什·贝德纳兹带领了此次打捞。瓶子及其内容物被送往格丁尼亚的J.S. Hamilton化学实验室，经检测，酒精可安全饮用，不过气味并不令人愉快。 除了塞尔特斯瓶，团队还在格但斯克湾12.2米（40英尺）深处发现了陶瓷碎片、小碗、部分餐具及石块。 现在，塞尔特斯矿泉水依然以高档产品身份采用现代玻璃瓶出售，据称其品质与数百年前相似。
post_content: 200-year-old Selters bottle found in a Baltic Sea shipwreck had vodka (or gin), not water! Still safe to drink—if you don’t mind the smell. Archaeologists even found more artifacts down there! #HistoryMystery #ShipwreckFind

article_content: China’s state-owned PetroChina has acquired control of 119 petrol and diesel stations in Myanmar, many of which are located close to the India-Myanmar border. The company is reportedly in talks to purchase an additional 53 stations, following the acquisition of over 50 outlets previously owned by a Singapore-based firm. Many of the newly acquired stations are situated near the India-Myanmar border and along the Trilateral Asia Highway. This expansion has potential security implications for India due to the proximity of these assets. Since Myanmar was subjected to Western sanctions after its recent coup, China has increased its investments, especially in Myanmar’s oil, gas, and infrastructure sectors. China views these industries—and the infrastructure connecting Myanmar to the Indian Ocean—as strategically significant. Earlier this year, a Chinese-funded energy project in Myanmar was attacked by anti-junta rebels soon after a Chinese government official visited the country. Last week, the Natogyi Guerrilla Force targeted Chinese-backed oil and gas pipelines in Myanmar’s Mandalay region. These pipelines, stretching 973 kilometers from the Rakhine coast across Magwe, Mandalay, and Shan state into China’s Yunnan province, were built in 2011 and have been operational since July 2013. Other news items include the Indian government’s consideration of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, Apple’s projected ₹1 lakh crore iPhone production goal in India for the current fiscal year, and a family settlement proposal involving Gautam Singhania and Nawaz Modi.

article_content: Pakistan remains hopeful about the Obama administration’s dedication to South Asia and intends to work closely with the U.S. to combat extremism within its territory, according to Foreign Minister Makhdoom Shah Mehmood Qureshi. After meeting U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, Qureshi highlighted strong alignment of interests between the two countries and a mutual willingness to cooperate. "The new American leadership gives us plenty of reasons for optimism. Pakistan is ready to join efforts with the U.S. against all forms of terrorism and extremism," Qureshi remarked on Tuesday. Qureshi is visiting Washington as part of a strategic review focusing on stabilizing Afghanistan and neighboring Pakistan. This initiative is spearheaded by South Asia security expert Bruce Reidel and U.S. Special Envoy Richard Holbrooke. Afghan Foreign Minister Rangin D. Spanta is also participating, and both he and Qureshi are scheduled for meetings with Clinton and Holbrooke. The appointments of Holbrooke and the ongoing discussions show how seriously the new U.S. administration takes the interconnected situations in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Secretary Clinton noted the close cooperation with Pakistan’s government and expressed appreciation for Qureshi’s input. Last week, President Obama announced plans to deploy an extra 17,000 troops to Afghanistan to address the growing insurgency, emphasizing that the fight there is central to broader U.S. efforts against terrorism. The troops are headed to Afghanistan’s southern region, which borders Pakistan and acts as a haven for Taliban fighters. Pakistani officials worry this move might push Taliban militants across the border, further destabilizing their own country. Alongside reviews led by General David Petraeus, Secretary of Defense Robert Gates has acknowledged the original Afghan mission might have been too broad and needs to be more focused. Meanwhile, Pakistan is carrying out its own military campaign against Taliban militants in the Northwest Frontier Province, particularly in Swat Valley where violence has surged and the militants have expanded control. This week, militants extended a cease-fire as part of an agreement with the government to enforce Sharia law—a pact that U.S. and NATO officials fear could entrench extremist influence near Afghanistan’s border. Once a bustling travel destination, Swat Valley has seen widespread violence and civilian displacement, with militants enforcing strict social codes. The federal government, previously with little sway in the region, launched a major offensive last July, prompting shocking retaliatory attacks from the Taliban, including bombings and kidnappings. The Taliban threatened further violence unless troops withdraw. This Tuesday, Taliban leaders prolonged the cease-fire established after signing their agreement with the government, though the deal remains heavily criticized both within Pakistan and internationally. U.S. envoy Holbrooke and NATO have voiced apprehensions that such agreements risk conceding control to militants in Swat.

‘The King's Speech’ transcends its historical roots to deliver a compelling and deeply human drama. The film chronicles the struggle of King George VI (portrayed by Colin Firth) to overcome a debilitating stammer with the help of Lionel Logue (Geoffrey Rush), an unorthodox Australian speech therapist. Set against the looming threat of WWII, the story begins in 1925, as then-Prince Albert faces public embarrassment during a speech at the British Empire Exhibition.

Encouraged by his supportive wife, Queen Elizabeth (Helena Bonham Carter), Albert seeks Logue’s unconventional aid. Their sessions evolve into a transformative friendship, marked by playful yet probing exchanges that reveal the prince’s vulnerability, a stern father (Michael Gambon as George V), and a brother (Guy Pearce as Edward VIII) whose abdication thrusts Albert onto the throne. As Albert becomes King George VI, Logue’s inventive methods prove crucial, enabling the king to confidently deliver the pivotal 1939 radio address rallying Britain against Hitler’s Germany.

Director Tom Hooper, known for acclaimed works like ‘John Adams’ and ‘Elizabeth I,’ invigorates the screenplay by David Seidler, infusing the film with intimacy and urgency. The cast excels: Firth offers a moving and nuanced performance, Rush brings humor and warmth, and Bonham Carter impresses with her subtlety. While the film eschews lavish spectacle for resonant emotion, it succeeds in creating a powerful portrait of courage, friendship, and self-discovery—making it one of the year’s most outstanding films, earning 3½ stars from Rolling Stone’s Peter Travers.

article_content: A recent YouTube video by Sw Yoon shows South Korean women sampling classic American junk foods for the first time, capturing their mix of amusement, surprise, and sometimes outright confusion. They try snacks like Goldfish crackers, salt and vinegar chips, strawberry Poptarts, Cheez-its, Twizzlers, Rice Krispies treats, and War Heads candies. Many of the women express hesitation over the unfamiliar look and taste of these snacks—some even mistake Goldfish crackers for marshmallows or pet food, while Poptarts are described as smelling overly artificial and tasting like toys or candles. Salt and vinegar chips get harsh reviews, with testers put off by their strong smell and sharp flavor. Twizzlers are likened to rubber and many are uncertain about how to eat them, with some almost immediately spitting them out. Cheez-its are better received, with participants suggesting they'd be popular snacks alongside wine or at bars. Chocolate Rice Krispies treats garner the most praise for their familiar sweet flavor. The final challenge, War Heads sour candies, leads to the most dramatic reactions. Most women find them far too sour and can't finish them, with some jokingly accusing the crew of trying to punish them. Humorous and colorful comparisons throughout the video highlight just how different American snack foods can feel to those not used to them.

By Dana Dunne, CEO of eDreams ODIGEO.

The pace of artificial intelligence (AI) development is remarkable, and we are still in the early stages of realizing its potential. According to McKinsey, generative AI could contribute between $2.6 trillion and $4.4 trillion annually to the global economy—a figure that highlights just how much growth lies ahead.

While the economic promise of generative AI is immense, both opportunities and challenges abound. Unlocking these benefits requires a thorough understanding of the technology and thoughtful, agile leadership from business leaders. Generative AI represents a major leap in AI evolution. Its ability to process and analyze massive data sets at unparalleled speeds is set to usher in new levels of workplace productivity.

Perhaps even more transformative is AI’s potential to drive innovation. AI already impacts everyday life, making routine activities more efficient—often in ways we don’t even notice. From powering smartphones and digital banking to enabling retailers’ customer engagement tools, AI shapes many aspects of modern living.

In healthcare, AI-driven research is accelerating discoveries. For example, the use of AI to process clinical trial data enables millions of simulations and speeds the identification of new drug targets, revealing insights that might otherwise take years. With new drug development costs often exceeding $1 billion, AI can save significant resources for pharmaceutical companies, allowing for greater investment in further research and fostering breakthroughs.

The travel industry also stands to benefit. With its extensive data, travel is well-suited for expanded AI applications to enhance services. At eDreams ODIGEO, we have invested in AI for nearly a decade. In 2014, we established an in-house AI team—one of the first in the travel sector—which led to an AI-powered fraud prevention system. AI has been vital to our success in OTA flight bookings, and our generative AI is used for data augmentation, creating personalized itineraries and tailored offers for customers. Looking ahead, travelers can expect even more refined and individually crafted itineraries based on preferences, budgets, and schedules. AI could also help minimize carbon emissions—a growing priority as more travelers care about sustainability.

For businesses to fully leverage AI, a hybrid approach is essential. Rather than replacing staff, AI should complement employees, making their work easier and more creative. At eDreams ODIGEO, AI empowers our talented team by reducing administrative burdens and fostering creativity, such as through brainstorming prompts. This enables employees to focus on high-value, creative work and meaningful customer engagement.

The field of coding is also being transformed. AI enables tech teams to rapidly implement platform updates, improve user interfaces, quickly address issues, and enhance customer experience. In competitive markets, even small improvements in app speed, accuracy, and usability can determine customer loyalty.

To benefit from AI-driven innovation, businesses must diversify their use of the technology; there is no universal solution. Multiple small-scale improvements across administration and operations, blending human skills and AI, drive progress. As automation becomes standard, employees will need new training, and businesses will require specialized staff to oversee AI initiatives. This applies to front-facing services and behind-the-scenes processes such as maintenance, accounting, and HR.

In summary, the accumulation of micro efficiencies from AI across the organization can lead to transformative change, greater innovation, and enhanced customer satisfaction—while ensuring the ongoing success of the business.

人工智能（AI）发展的速度令人惊叹，而我们仍处于释放其全部潜力的早期阶段。麦肯锡（McKinsey）报告称，生成式AI每年可为全球经济带来2.6万亿至4.4万亿美元的增长——这个数据充分说明了其发展空间之大。

虽然生成式AI极具经济潜力，但机遇与挑战同在。要充分释放AI优势，需要企业领导者对技术有深入理解，并采取灵活且有前瞻性的管理。生成式AI是AI发展的重要突破，它能以远超人类的速度处理与分析海量数据，有望开启职场生产力的新时代。

企业要充分利用AI，需采取混合式模式，将AI视为员工助手而非替代品。eDreams ODIGEO拥有出色的人才团队，AI助力他们减负、激发创意，例如通过头脑风暴提示等，使员工能更专注于创意性和客户互动等高价值工作。

AI也正在改变编码领域。技术团队能用AI瞬间完成平台升级、优化界面、快速修复问题，提升客户体验。在竞争激烈的市场中，应用的小幅提升比如速度、准确性和友好度，都是赢得和保留客户的关键。

要抓住AI带来的创新，企业需多元化应用AI，而非只依赖单一方案。通过将人力与AI灵活结合，在企业管理和运营各环节实现微创新。随着自动化推广，员工需培养新技能，技术团队也需引入专业人才管理AI项目。这适用于客服、用户体验乃至维护、财务和人力资源等后台业务。

总之，AI助力各部门实现微创新，推动企业整体转型与创新，提升客户满意度，并保障企业可持续发展。

article_content: A government advisory panel warns that a resurgence of the H1N1 flu virus this fall could lead to up to 90,000 deaths in the U.S., especially affecting children and young adults. The panel urges faster vaccine production with the goal of making initial doses available by September. An estimated 30% to 50% of Americans might be infected with H1N1 during the fall and winter, leading to up to 1.8 million hospitalizations. The President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology outlines a scenario where outbreaks in schools, shortages of antiviral drugs, and infections outpacing vaccine availability could result in 30,000 to 90,000 deaths. Typically, seasonal flu causes up to 40,000 deaths in the U.S. each year, mostly among older adults over 65. This year, the combined impact of seasonal flu and H1N1 may drive influenza-related deaths higher and place added strain on intensive care units, which are often close to full capacity. The report suggests H1N1 could appear again as early as September, coinciding with back-to-school, and peak in mid-October. Vaccine supplies may not be ready until mid-October, and immunity takes weeks to develop after vaccination. This timing gap might reduce the vaccine's immediate effectiveness against the first wave of infections. Dr. Thomas Frieden, CDC director, acknowledges that illness and deaths will occur despite progress with vaccines and testing. The report recommends that agencies prepare for a variety of epidemic scenarios, improve monitoring of flu-like illnesses, protect vulnerable populations—including pregnant women and people with existing medical conditions—and prioritize delivering the vaccine to those at highest risk. Guidelines for businesses and schools have already been issued and are available at flu.gov. The recommended vaccination plan consists of two shots given three weeks apart, with full immunity expected about two weeks after the second dose. The World Health Organization classified H1N1 as a pandemic on June 11, and more than 1,490 people worldwide have died since the virus emerged earlier this year. Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius says any vaccination campaign will be voluntary and final decisions depend on ongoing clinical trial results, which have not yet shown unexpected side effects. Vulnerable groups are pregnant women, healthcare workers, parents of infants under six months, and adults with preexisting health issues like asthma.
translated_content: 一项政府顾问小组警告称，今年秋天H1N1流感病毒可能再次爆发，美国死亡人数或高达9万人，尤其影响儿童和年轻人。该小组敦促加快疫苗生产，目标是在九月前提供首批疫苗。 预计在秋冬期间，30%至50%的美国人可能感染H1N1，住院人数最多或达180万。总统科技顾问委员会指出，如果学校暴发疫情、抗病毒药品短缺、疫苗未能及时覆盖，死亡人数可能在3万至9万之间。 通常每年美国因季节性流感死亡人数最高可达4万人，大多为65岁以上老人。今年，季节性流感叠加H1N1可能导致更多流感死亡病例，并将导致重症监护室负担加重，而这些病房本就在高位运行。 报告称H1N1可能会在九月，与开学季同步，再次出现，并于十月中旬达到高峰。而疫苗供应也许要到十月中旬才能到位，并且在接种后需数周才能产生免疫力。 这种时间差可能会降低疫苗在第一波感染中的即时保护效果。美国疾控中心主任托马斯·弗里登（Thomas Frieden）表示，尽管疫苗和检测取得进展，仍难以避免疫情带来疾病和死亡。 报告建议各级机构针对不同疫情情景制定应对方案，加强对流感类症状的监测，保护包括孕妇和已有健康问题人群等弱势群体，并优先为高风险人群接种疫苗。 针对企业和学校的应对指南已发布，可在flu.gov网站查阅。H1N1疫苗需分两次接种，间隔三周，第二针后约两周方可产生完全免疫力。 世界卫生组织于6月11日将H1N1列为大流行病，今年初以来，全球已有1490多人因感染死亡。美国卫生与公众服务部长凯瑟琳·西贝利厄斯（Kathleen Sebelius）表示，疫苗接种完全自愿，最终是否推广还需等待正在进行的临床试验结果，目前尚未发现异常副作用。孕妇、医护人员、6个月以下婴儿家长、以及有哮喘等基础疾病的成年人都属于高风险人群。

article_content: As 2024 begins, hybrid and remote work continue growing into standard ways of working, signaling a major shift in what 'the office' means. Research from UpWork predicts that by 2025, nearly a quarter (22%) of employees will be working remotely, while AT&T expects hybrid arrangements to be embraced by 81% of employers. With these changes, leaders are under increasing pressure to develop new skills for managing teams in these evolving environments. One major challenge for managers is prioritizing employee wellbeing. As Simon Brisk, co-founder of Click Intelligence, points out, stress management is even more crucial with hybrid teams, since working from home often blurs the separation between personal and work life. Without careful oversight, employees may struggle to maintain work-life boundaries, leading to irritability and a drop in productivity. In fact, while the shift to remote work during the pandemic boosted productivity, it also resulted in burnout for 69% of employees—many of whom ended up working longer hours. To combat these issues, Albert Vaisman, founder of Soxy, advises crafting hybrid policies that include employee input, set clear hours for availability, and establish response time expectations. This structure helps employees avoid the pressure of being constantly online, reduces unnecessary meetings, and protects personal time. Equipping teams with the right technology is another cornerstone of effective hybrid leadership. Tom Humble, CXO and founder of ECD Auto Design, notes that tools like Zoom for meetings, Slack for instant updates, and Trello for managing projects are essential to productive collaboration, no matter where employees are working. When it comes to hiring, Lindsey Bourret, managing director at Mearto, values candidates who have prior experience working remotely. She prioritizes independence and self-motivation, seeing these traits as almost as important as industry expertise. Trust is also foundational. Heavy-handed management and surveillance can erode morale, as Bourret and Kelsey Bishop, CEO of Candor, both stress. Instead, trusting your team and giving them flexibility leads to stronger relationships and greater buy-in. Building genuine connections takes extra effort in remote and hybrid environments, since spontaneous in-person interactions are rarer. However, meaningful relationship-building increases productivity—Gallup research shows that isolation among remote workers can lower productivity by 21%. Bourret recommends one-on-one calls and a personal touch to ensure team members feel supported beyond work tasks. Ultimately, the growth of hybrid and remote work presents new opportunities for career and personal development for both leaders and their teams. By adopting flexible, digital-savvy, and people-first approaches, managers can ensure their teams thrive. As Emery Bowles puts it, success in hybrid management isn't just about new technology—it's about fostering an inclusive culture where communication and flexibility are highly valued.
translated_content: 随着2024年的到来，混合办公和远程办公正逐步成为主流，这也意味着我们对“办公室”的定义正在发生重大变化。根据UpWork的研究，预计到2025年，将有约四分之一（22%）的员工以远程办公为主，而AT&T则预测届时81%的雇主将采用混合办公模式。随着这些变革，领导者需要不断提升技能，以更好地管理处于不断变化环境中的团队。 其中一大挑战就是员工的幸福感。Click Intelligence联合创始人Simon Brisk强调，对于混合团队，压力管理变得更加重要，因为在家工作时，个人生活和工作往往界限模糊。如果不加以关注，员工可能难以实现工作与生活平衡，进而变得急躁、工作效率下降。实际上，虽然疫情期间远程办公带动了生产力提升，但也有69%的员工感到倦怠，许多人工时反而变长。 对于这些问题，Soxy创始人Albert Vaisman建议，制定混合办公政策时要充分听取员工意见，明确规定在线时间和回应时效。这种制度能帮助员工避免“随时在线”的压力，减少不必要的视频会议，保障个人时间。 为团队配备合适的数字工具也是混合型领导力的关键。ECD Auto Design创始人兼CXO Tom Humble指出，Zoom用于会议，Slack实现快速沟通，Trello辅助项目管理，这些工具让团队无论身在何处都能实现高效协作。 在招聘时，Mearto董事总经理Lindsey Bourret非常重视有远程工作经验的人选。她认为独立和自我驱动力几乎与行业经验同等重要。 信任同样至关重要。Bourret和Candor首席执行官Kelsey Bishop都强调，过度监督和监控会削弱团队士气。相反，给予员工信任与灵活度能创造更好的关系与投入感。 在远程或混合办公环境下，要建立真诚的联系需要付出额外努力，因为临时的面对面交流变少了。但关系的维护可以提升生产力——Gallup研究显示，感到孤独的远程员工生产力下降可达21%。Bourret建议多进行一对一沟通，并关心员工生活，帮助他们感受到被支持。 总体来说，混合与远程办公为管理者和团队成员都带来了新的个人和职业成长机会。通过灵活、善用数字工具、以人为本的管理，团队可以更好地成长。正如Emery Bowles所说，混合管理的成功不仅要靠新技术，更在于建立包容与沟通的文化及重视灵活性。

article_content: At the Safe Schools National Summit in Abuja, Nigeria's Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, called for enhanced intelligence operations and proactive strategies to address ongoing school attacks. He emphasized that simply deploying security personnel is insufficient; smarter, intelligence-led approaches are essential to protecting students and staff. Tunji-Ojo highlighted that the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) cannot singlehandedly secure all schools, and collaborative efforts are needed. He urged more investment in surveillance and data analysis to anticipate threats, which would lead to more focused and effective security responses nationwide. He stressed the importance of security agencies staying ahead of criminals by being creative and unpredictable in their strategies. According to the minister, true security relies on being proactive rather than merely reacting after incidents. Furthermore, Tunji-Ojo advocated for a thorough implementation of the Safe Schools programme to help reduce the number of children unable to attend school due to insecurity. He reaffirmed his ministry’s full commitment to making this initiative successful, observing that Nigeria’s challenge is often in execution rather than in ideas. NSCDC Commandant General Ahmed Audi noted that, despite many interventions, school attacks continue, leading to a growing number of out-of-school children. He stated that the summit aims to identify obstacles to the Safe Schools project and better prepare all those involved in keeping schools safe. Representing the Ministry of Education, Director Giginna Ifeyinwa pointed out that many attacks could have been prevented through close cooperation, emergency preparedness, swift responses, and adherence to the Safe School Declaration Guidelines. In summary, speakers at the summit agreed that intelligence-driven collaboration, solid preparation, and continual innovation are vital to securing schools in Nigeria.
translated_content: 在阿布贾举行的安全学校国家峰会上，尼日利亚内政部长奥卢布米·通吉-奥乔呼吁加强情报工作和主动性策略，以应对持续发生的学校袭击。他强调，仅靠部署安保人员远远不够，必须采取更聪明、以情报为导向的方法来保护学生和教职员工的安全。 通吉-奥乔指出，尼日利亚安全与民防团（NSCDC）无法独自承担学校安保任务，必须通过协作共同努力。他主张增加对监控和数据分析的投入，以便提前发现威胁，从而在全国范围内实现更精准、更高效的安保响应。 他强调，安保机构需不断创新，采取出其不意的策略，始终领先于犯罪分子。部长表示，真正的安全在于主动预防，而不仅仅是在事后处理。 此外，通吉-奥乔还呼吁全面落实安全学校项目，以减少因安全原因失学的儿童数量。他重申内政部将全力支持该项目，并指出尼日利亚往往有好的想法，但挑战在于落实。 NSCDC总指挥官艾哈迈德·奥迪指出，尽管多方采取了多种干预措施，学校袭击仍在持续，导致失学儿童不断增加。他表示，峰会旨在找出影响安全学校项目的障碍，并让相关人员更好地做好安全保障工作。 教育部支持服务司司长吉金纳·伊菲因瓦代表教育部长发言时指出，如果相关部门能够更密切合作、加强应急准备并及时响应，并遵守安全学校宣言准则，许多袭击事件是可以预防的。 综上，与会代表一致认为，加强以情报为核心的协作、扎实的准备和持续的创新，是确保尼日利亚学校安全的关键。

article_content: Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel is set to embark on a visit to Japan and Singapore next week to promote the upcoming Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit (VGGS), scheduled for January 2024. According to a tentative itinerary, the CM and his delegation will depart on November 26 and return on December 3. Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation Managing Director Rahul Gupta described the visit as a significant step in the ongoing preparations for VGGS. 'Tentatively, the dates are from November 26 to December 3. The delegation will visit Japan first, followed by Singapore on the final two days,' Gupta said. The Chief Minister will be joined by a high-level delegation, including Chief Secretary Raj Kumar; Additional Chief Secretary (Industries & Mines) S J Haider; Additional Chief Secretary to the CM, Pankaj Joshi; Resident Commissioner Arti Kanwar; and IndextB Managing Director Gaurang Makwana. Industry representatives, including leaders from specific sectors, will also participate—details of which are being finalized, Gupta added. So far, 13 countries—including Australia, Denmark, Japan, South Korea, United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom—have confirmed their partnership for VGGS, according to Gupta.

article_content: As intensive bombing continues, UNICEF and its partners remain present in Gaza, working to save children's lives and protect them from long-term psychological harm. Four-year-old Sileen sits in a hallway outside classrooms at a UNRWA (United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees in the Near East) school now used as an emergency shelter for families displaced by recent hostilities in the Gaza Strip. "I do not like it here, it is crowded. I just want to go home," she said. The conflict in Gaza is exposing children to direct physical danger and severe emotional and psychological distress, UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell told the United Nations Security Council on October 30. Russell emphasized that children in both Israel and the State of Palestine are enduring profound trauma, the effects of which could last a lifetime. She urged the Security Council to remind all parties of their obligations under international law, calling for an immediate ceasefire, full humanitarian access, and the prompt and safe release of all abducted children. "After just over three weeks, the toll is rising rapidly, with grave violations being committed against children," Russell said. "According to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, more than 8,300 Palestinians, including over 3,400 children, have been killed in Gaza, with more than 6,300 children injured. This means that over 420 children are killed or injured in Gaza daily—a statistic that should alarm us all." Recent airstrikes on Jabaliya camp, the largest of Gaza's eight camps for the internally displaced, have further increased the number of casualties. Refugee camps and their inhabitants, including the displaced, are protected under international humanitarian law; all parties must respect and protect them from attacks. Israeli sources report that at least 1,400 people in Israel have been killed and more than 5,431 injured. According to Israeli authorities, 224 Israelis, including at least 20 children, were abducted on October 7. On October 19, Ahmad, aged nine, stood amid the ruins of his house in Rafah, destroyed by an airstrike. UNICEF and its partners continue to push for greater access to deliver essential water, medicine, healthcare, and services. Since the conflict escalated on October 7, only 217 humanitarian aid trucks have entered Gaza as of October 31, while officials estimate at least 100 trucks daily are needed for urgent needs. To date, UNICEF has brought 25 aid trucks into Gaza via the Rafah Crossing, carrying hygiene kits, bottled water for 55,000 people, and medical supplies delivered to Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, supporting an estimated 165,000 people. UNICEF is also pre-positioning more supplies in Egypt and advocating for secure, sustained access for vital aid delivery. On October 30, a plane arrived at Egypt's Al-Arish airport with UNICEF-supported lifesaving supplies for children and families in Gaza. Attacks on civilian infrastructure and ongoing fuel shortages have crippled Gaza’s water and sanitation systems. UNICEF leads the Global WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) Cluster, coordinating with 68 partners to assist water providers in gradually restoring water supply and wastewater services to meet critical needs. UNICEF has distributed 4,500 emergency family kits, leading to clean water production for domestic use that benefits one million people in Deir Al Balah, Khan Younis, and Rafah, including over 560,000 children. Over 22,000 people, about half of them children, have received cash payments—redeemable through mobile agents like grocery stores—to afford basics such as water, food, and hygiene products. UNICEF is also working with partners to support health service delivery in both northern and southern Gaza. Bombardment continues in Gaza City, putting children’s physical and mental health at serious risk. UNICEF is calling for an immediate ceasefire. UNICEF is also providing psychosocial support and child protection services to children affected by the violence. Even before the recent escalation, about 800,000 children (three-quarters of Gaza's child population) were already identified as needing mental health and psychosocial support. Since early October, 625,000 school-aged children in Gaza have lost access to education, and at least 221 schools—over 40 percent of all schools in Gaza—have been damaged by airstrikes. Twelve of Gaza’s 35 hospitals—many now serving as shelters—are out of service, and nearly two-thirds of primary healthcare clinics have shut due to damage. Around 1.4 million people—over half of Gaza’s population—are internally displaced and sheltering in public buildings, hospitals, or with host families. Border closures and limited movement have left civilians with nowhere safe to go. Overcrowding, scarce food and water, and lack of privacy in shelters heighten health and protection concerns, especially for women and children. Families in Gaza are also faced with extensive power outages due to fuel shortages. According to the Palestinian Water Authority, water production is now just 5% of normal daily capacity, forcing people to boil dirty water—raising risks of disease—or drink seawater, which causes severe dehydration. Nesma, a UNICEF staff member remaining in Gaza, reported on October 29 that her daughters, Talia (4) and Zain (7), are desperate for drinkable water and showing signs of severe psychological distress. "It breaks my heart to see children around me struggle for clean water and not find it," she said. "Zain keeps asking for regular (not salty) water." Talia has developed habits of pulling her hair and scratching herself until she bleeds. “Since October 7, my sole mission has been to keep my children alive,” Nesma said. “I can’t worry about their mental health now. As a humanitarian worker and a mother, it’s painful not to meet even their basic needs or those of other Gaza children. When this is over, I want to give them the support and care they need.” UNICEF will continue prioritizing the needs of children and providing essential support to help them recover from intense stress and trauma. However, what children need most is an end to violence. "On behalf of all children trapped in this crisis, we urge the world to do more," Russell told the Security Council. "Whether they are youth at a music festival or Gaza children trying to live their lives, all deserve peace. Children do not start conflicts and are powerless to stop them. We must prioritize their safety and strive for a future where children are healthy, safe, and educated. No child deserves less." UNICEF’s response is focused on meeting immediate protection and humanitarian needs of children in Gaza. Contributions can make a difference—please donate.
translated_content: 随着密集轰炸持续进行，联合国儿童基金会（UNICEF）及其合作伙伴仍坚守在加沙，努力拯救儿童的生命并保护他们免受长期心理伤害。 四岁的塞琳坐在教室外的走廊里，她和家人因近期加沙地带冲突被迫避难于联合国近东巴勒斯坦难民救济和工程处（UNRWA）的一所学校紧急收容所。她说：“我不喜欢这里，这里很挤。我只想回家。” 冲突让加沙的儿童面临直接的身体危险和严重的情绪与心理压力。联合国儿童基金会执行主任凯瑟琳·拉塞尔（Catherine Russell）于10月30日在联合国安理会表示。 拉塞尔强调，以色列和巴勒斯坦地区的儿童都在承受深刻的创伤，其影响可能持续一生。她呼吁安理会提醒各方遵守国际法，立即实现停火、全面开展人道救援行动，同时安全迅速释放所有被绑架儿童。 “仅仅三个多星期，受害人数正在快速上升，儿童正遭受严重侵害。”拉塞尔表示，“据巴勒斯坦卫生部统计，加沙已有8,300多名巴勒斯坦人丧生，其中3,400多名是儿童，另外有6,300多名儿童受伤。换言之，加沙每天有超过420名儿童死亡或受伤——这个数字令人震惊。” 近期对贾巴利亚营地的空袭进一步增加了伤亡人数，该营地是加沙八个流离失所者营地中最大一个。根据国际人道法，难民营及其居民均受保护，各方应尊重并保护他们免遭攻击。 以色列方面报告称，以色列已有至少1,400人死亡、5,431人受伤。以色列当局称，10月7日有224名以色列人被绑架，其中至少 20 人是儿童。 10月19日，9岁的艾哈迈德站在他被空袭摧毁的拉法家中废墟上。 联合国儿童基金会及其合作伙伴正持续争取更多人道救援通道，以便输送急需的水、药品、医疗和各项服务。自10月7日冲突升级以来，截至10月31日，仅有217辆救援卡车获准进入加沙，而官方估计急需的数量应为每天至少100辆。 目前，联合国儿童基金会已通过拉法口岸运送了25辆救援卡车，内容包括卫生包、可供5.5万人饮用的瓶装水和送往汗尤尼斯纳赛尔医院的医疗用品，预计惠及16.5万人。同时，基金会正于埃及预置更多紧急物资，并继续为安全、持续的人道通道而努力。 10月30日，一架载有联合国儿童基金会救命物资的飞机抵达埃及阿里什机场，物资将运往加沙的儿童和家庭。 针对平民基础设施的打击和持续的燃料短缺，已导致加沙水务及卫生系统瘫痪。联合国儿童基金会作为全球WASH（水、环境卫生与健康）合作机制的牵头机构，与68个合作伙伴联合协助水务单位，逐步恢复供水、污水处理，以满足关键救生需求。 基金会发放了4,500套应急家庭包，为代尔巴拉、汗尤尼斯、拉法地区超过100万人（其中56万余名儿童）提供了安全饮用及家用水。 超过22,000人（约一半为儿童）获得可以在杂货店等移动代理网点兑换的现金援助，用于购买水、食品和卫生用品等必需品。基金会还与多方协作，支持加沙南北医疗服务的提供。 加沙城持续遭受轰炸，儿童的身心健康受到严重威胁。联合国儿童基金会呼吁立即停火。 基金会还为受冲突影响的儿童提供心理社会支持及儿童保护服务。 在近期局势升级之前，加沙约80万（占全体儿童数量的四分之三）已被确定为需心理健康和心理社会支持的儿童。自10月初以来，加沙62.5万学龄儿童无法上学；截至目前，至少221所学校——占加沙全部学校的四成以上——已被空袭损毁。 加沙35家医院中有12家（不少现为临时收容所）停止运营，近三分之二的初级医疗诊所因损毁关闭。约140万人（超过本地总人口的一半）被迫在收容所、医院、公共建筑或寄居在他人家中。 边境封闭和行动受限令平民无处安全避难。收容所极度拥挤、食品和饮用水短缺及隐私缺失，特别是对妇女和儿童带来严峻的健康和安全隐患。 加沙家庭还面临由于燃料短缺导致的大面积断电。巴勒斯坦水务局称，目前产水能力仅为正常日常的5%，人们不得不烧煮脏水饮用，导致水源性疾病风险上升，甚至饮用海水，造成严重脱水。 坚守在加沙的联合国儿童基金会工作人员奈斯玛10月29日表示，她的女儿塔莉亚（4岁）和泽因（7岁）迫切渴望饮用水，并出现了严重的心理压力表现。“看到身边的孩子们为了喝上一口干净的水而挣扎却依然无望，我非常心痛。”她说，“泽因不断请求能喝到正常（不咸）的水。”塔莉亚已经开始拔头发并抓挠腿部直至出血。 “自10月7日起，我的人生使命就是让我的女儿们活下去。”奈斯玛说，“此时我已经无暇顾及她们的心理健康。作为一名母亲和人道工作者，当连最基本的生活需求都无法满足时，这种痛苦难以言表，更别说加沙的其他孩子们了。等一切结束后，我想给予她们心理和医疗支持。” 联合国儿童基金会将继续把儿童的需求放在首位，为他们从极度压力和创伤中恢复提供必要援助。然而，孩子们最需要的依然是停止暴力。 “为了所有被困于这场危机的孩子，我们呼吁世界做得更好。”拉塞尔在安理会呼吁，“无论是音乐节上的年轻人，还是在加沙渴望平静生活的孩子们，所有人都值得拥有和平。孩子们不是冲突的制造者，也无力阻止冲突。我们必须把儿童的安全放在最优先位置，创造一个健康、安全、有教育的未来。每个孩子都不应被剥夺这些权利。” 联合国儿童基金会的工作，仍将聚焦于满足加沙儿童紧急的人身保护和人道需求。您的捐助或许能改变他们的命运——欢迎支持。

article_content: Baltimore police officers disarmed a man who claimed he was ordered by the Black Guerrilla Family, a well-known prison gang, to smuggle a loaded handgun into a city police station. Police Commissioner Anthony Batts reported that 29-year-old Jason Armstrong entered the Northeastern District substation around 8 a.m. Tuesday, smelling strongly of marijuana. Officers noticed Armstrong's unusual behavior and searched him, discovering marijuana, cocaine, and a .22-caliber handgun with a round in the chamber. During questioning, Armstrong told officers that the Black Guerrilla Family gang instructed him to bring contraband into the station to test their security measures. At a press conference recorded by WMAR, Commissioner Batts stated, 'An organized gang in Baltimore sent an armed suspect into our building to test our security.' He continued, 'We will not cower or back down. We will not shy away from tough situations. We remain committed to being a constitutional police department.' Batts also emphasized, 'We will not wait for this to happen again. We will hold those responsible for sending him into that police station accountable.' According to WMAR, the Black Guerrilla Family has previously been implicated in schemes to sell drugs from Baltimore Detention Center, including cases where both facility employees and gang members have been indicted. Deputy Police Commissioner Jerry Rodriguez said Armstrong did not act entirely of his own free will, based on Armstrong's own statement. Rodriguez added, 'We have verified as much as possible his gang affiliation and his prior contacts with police. We are aware of incidents that led to this situation.' Late Tuesday, police reported that Armstrong was charged with weapons and narcotics offenses. The FBI had recently issued a memo warning of potential threats against police officers nationwide. This incident follows the December 20 fatal shootings of NYPD Officers Rafael Ramos and Wenjian Liu by Issmaiyl Brinsley, who later took his own life after the attack.

article_content: The Federal Government of Nigeria has started discussions with UAE Ambassador Salem Saeed Alshamsi and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani to gain their support for the national school feeding program. This initiative was announced in Abuja on Wednesday by Dr. Yetunde Adeniji, Senior Special Assistant on School Feeding to President Bola Tinubu, coming just a week after the government's plan to feed 100,000 displaced children in northern Nigeria was unveiled. Dr. Adeniji explained that her delegation spoke with both the UAE ambassador and Governor Sani during the 52nd United Arab Emirates National Day celebrations held in Abuja on Monday, attended by Princess Zara Audu, the APC’s North Central Woman Leader. Governor Sani expressed enthusiasm for the program, noting Kaduna State’s history of leadership in school feeding projects and reaffirmed the state’s commitment to remain highly involved. Ambassador Alshamsi praised the program and acknowledged Dr. Adeniji's initiative in stakeholder engagement. He also commended President Bola Tinubu's administration for its proactive approach to the country’s challenges, highlighting the importance of humanitarian aid. Both Ambassador Alshamsi and Governor Sani reportedly assured their full support for the Federal Government's school feeding programme aimed at assisting vulnerable children.

article_content: George Lucas has decided to abandon plans for a large-scale film studio at Grady Ranch, located north of San Francisco in Marin County. The move comes after years of resistance from local residents and environmentalists, who were concerned about potential increases in traffic, noise, and impacts to the surrounding landscape. The project, proposed by Lucasfilm, involved a 269,000 square foot digital studio complex featuring sound stages, guest accommodations, retail amenities, and even private wine storage—facilities that would have created hundreds of new jobs and boosted local tax revenues. Lucasfilm explained that continued delays and strong neighbor opposition have led to their decision. In a statement, the company said it wants to be considered a 'creative asset' for the community, rather than being labeled as an 'evil empire.' For over 25 years, efforts to gain approval for the Grady Ranch project have faced significant hurdles. Despite receiving unanimous support from the county’s planning commission earlier this year, further appeals and persistent resistance made progress difficult. The company now plans to explore other locations more receptive to development, noting that several cities have already offered attractive incentives. Lucasfilm also intends to sell the Grady Ranch property, potentially for the construction of affordable housing. Cynthia Murray of the North Bay Leadership Council expressed disappointment, saying the decision could make it harder for other companies to invest in Marin. Meanwhile, Liz Dale from the local homeowners association said she understands why Lucasfilm chose to withdraw, emphasizing the importance of aligning any future developments with community needs. Though saddened by the outcome, Lucasfilm representatives believe other communities will recognize the educational and economic value that such creative projects can bring.

article_content: A Scoot flight bound for Perth was forced to return to Singapore on Thursday (Oct 12) after a bomb threat was reported, with fighter jets escorting the plane back. Scoot flight TR16 had departed Changi Airport at 4:11pm, but turned back after authorities were alerted to the threat at about 4:55pm. The aircraft landed safely at Changi Airport at approximately 6:26pm, escorted by Republic of Singapore Air Force (RSAF) fighter jets.

article_content:
Israel and Hamas are set to begin a four-day truce on Friday, marking the first major pause after seven weeks of conflict that have resulted in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement. Under the terms of the agreement, Hamas will release 13 Israeli hostages from Gaza in exchange for an unspecified number of Palestinian prisoners held in Israeli jails, according to Qatari mediators. The truce is scheduled to start at 7:00 am local time (0500 GMT).

Over the four-day period, at least 50 hostages are expected to be freed by Palestinian militant groups in exchange for 150 Palestinian prisoners. More releases might follow if the truce is extended. For Gaza's population of over two million, this agreement offers a respite from ongoing Israeli airstrikes.

The Gaza health ministry, administered by Hamas, claims the war has led to approximately 15,000 deaths and displaced countless others. While these figures are difficult to independently verify, the immense toll on both Palestinian and Israeli families is clear. Civilians continue to pay a heavy price, as highlighted by Gaza residents mourning lost loved ones and facing ongoing hardships.

Qatari officials stated that the first group of hostages to be released would consist of women and children from the same families. Israeli trauma specialists and medics, along with specially trained soldiers, are ready to welcome them upon arrival. The exchange will be overseen by Israeli, Egyptian, and International Red Cross-Red Crescent teams at Rafah, the Egypt-Gaza border crossing.

AFP has confirmed the identities of 210 of around 240 people abducted by Hamas during attacks on military targets, civilian communities, and a music festival on October 7. Among those kidnapped, at least 35 are children, 18 of whom were aged 10 or younger at the time. Israel reports about 1,200 fatalities, mostly civilians, from the October 7 attacks.

Little is known publicly about the hostages’ current conditions. Moty Cristal, a retired Israeli military official, emphasized the need to prepare for all scenarios during the release process. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office has received an initial list of those set to be freed and is keeping families informed. US President Joe Biden expressed hope that an American child abducted during the attacks would be among the first released.

Qatari foreign ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari confirmed that Palestinian prisoners will be released on Friday, with a list of names already approved. Under the deal, there will be a complete temporary ceasefire—including an end to aerial and ground operations—as well as a suspension of drone surveillance to ensure releases happen safely. Israel has published a list of 300 Palestinian detainees eligible for release if the truce extends, including 33 women, 267 minors (aged 19 or younger), and 49 Hamas members.

The armed wing of Hamas confirmed the cessation of hostilities would begin at 7:00 am, and that three Palestinian prisoners would be released for each Israeli hostage. Prisoners from three Israeli and West Bank facilities will be transported to Ofer military camp and are expected to be freed in the evening. Most are from the West Bank, with five from Gaza.

Governments worldwide have welcomed the agreement, hoping it could pave the way for an end to the war. Palestinian ambassador to the UN, Riyad Mansour, urged the truce not to be merely a pause before renewed violence. Israeli officials, however, warn that fighting may resume after the truce. Israeli Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi reiterated that hostilities will continue until victory is achieved.

Fighting persisted ahead of the truce, with rocket alerts in Israeli communities near Gaza and continued bombardment in northern Gaza, where large areas lie in ruins. Hamas health officials reported Israeli raids at the Indonesian Hospital, and Israeli forces detained the director of Gaza's largest hospital, Al-Shifa, and other staff. While Israel accuses Hamas of using hospitals for military operations, Hamas and medical staff deny these claims.

Bombardments continued in the southern city of Khan Yunis, with significant casualties reported in the Jabalia refugee camp, where a UN-run school sheltering civilians was hit. Tensions remain high on Israel’s northern border, as Hezbollah in Lebanon has intensified attacks, triggering deadly exchanges with Israeli forces and raising fears of wider conflict.

article_content: There are many ways to celebrate a sporting victory, but sleeping in the kit you competed in is unusual. Yet that is exactly what Jo Pavey did after winning the 10,000m gold medal at the European Championships in Zurich in 2014. The considerate runner did this because she didn’t want to wake her roommate, Goldie Sayers, when she returned. Pavey became the oldest-ever winner at the European Championships when she triumphed in Zurich, as reported by The Independent's athletics correspondent, Matt Majendie. On Tuesday, Pavey raced to gold in the women's 10,000m. Draped in the Union Jack flag, she celebrated her achievement on the track. Out of consideration, she slept in her running kit so as not to disturb Sayers. The mother of two also won a bronze medal in the 5,000m at the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. During her lap of honour, she hugged her 11-month-old daughter, Emily. Pavey has announced she will return to Portsmouth to compete in the Bupa Great South Run in October, aiming to secure another medal. 'The Great South Run means a lot to me,' said Pavey, who will join 25,000 runners at the world’s leading 10-mile event, celebrating its 25th year. 'I really like that it’s 10 miles, the course is fast and flat, and the competition is always strong. I enjoy the atmosphere and the finish along the Portsmouth seafront.' 'I’ve had a great year, and I’m excited to go back. It would be nice to try for a personal best. Even though I’m getting older, I’m still determined to run fast times.' Mo Farah will try to follow in Jo Pavey’s footsteps on Wednesday evening when he competes in the men’s 10,000m at the European Championships. Farah missed the Commonwealth Games but is participating in the European Championships.

Southampton and West Bromwich Albion played out a goalless draw at St Mary's Stadium, demonstrating the ongoing challenges both teams face after significant summer squad changes. Managers Ronald Koeman and Alan Irvine, both newly appointed at their respective clubs, highlighted the need for additional signings to strengthen their squads before the transfer window closes.

The match itself was marked by a lack of fluidity and few goal-scoring opportunities. The sides struggled to find attacking cohesion, reflecting their in-progress rebuilding efforts. Among the few notable moments, Southampton's Dusan Tadic forced a save from West Brom goalkeeper Ben Foster in the first half, while West Brom’s substitute Brown Ideye headed wide from close range and later tested Southampton’s new keeper Fraser Forster. Despite new additions like Graziano Pelle and Shane Long for Southampton, and Ideye for West Brom, neither side found a breakthrough.

Individual performances varied, with the game highlighting the work that remains for both teams to gel. Statistical data from the EA SPORTS Player Performance Index showed high work rates from players such as Morgan Schneiderlin and Dusan Tadic for Southampton, and Craig Gardner for West Brom. Yet, their efforts did not translate into goals.

Southampton fans were disappointed not to capitalize on their previous strong performance but were reminded that it took Koeman several games to secure his first league win in his former post in the Netherlands. Meanwhile, Irvine expressed satisfaction with a point away from home despite having limited time to work with his new squad. As the match ended 0-0, both managers acknowledged the importance of bringing in fresh talent to improve creativity and competition within their teams ahead of a demanding Premier League season.

article_content: A study analyzing over 4,000 cryptocurrencies from 2015 to 2022 has found that high-risk cryptocurrencies generally perform worse than their low-risk counterparts. The research reveals that cryptocurrencies with the most idiosyncratic (asset-specific) risks experienced an average annualized return of -9.36%, while those with the least idiosyncratic risks saw an average annualized return of 80.6%. For example, Bitcoin achieved a 53.5% return over the year ending June 2023, whereas Dogecoin underperformed with a return of -4.8%. Conducted by academics from the University of Sydney School of Economics, this study is one of the most comprehensive analyses of cryptocurrency pricing to date. Published in the Journal of Empirical Finance, the research challenges the traditional view that higher risk yields higher returns. Instead, the study highlights the low-volatility anomaly, where investors are penalized for making risky, lottery-like bets. Lead researcher Dr. Simon Kwok explains that possible explanations for this phenomenon include limits on leverage, constraints on short-selling, investors’ preference for lottery-type outcomes, and behavioral biases such as overconfidence. While the low-volatility anomaly suggests potential opportunities, Dr. Kwok notes that exploiting it is difficult. "We found that traders need significant leverage to capitalize on this anomaly effectively. However, borrowing to invest significantly increases the risk of insolvency," he says. The authors calculated that traders aiming to exploit the anomaly would need to borrow at least 50% of their investment, facing the possibility of losing up to 84% of their capital. Dr. Kwok also points out practical obstacles to trading cryptocurrencies, such as the limited number of brokers offering a wide range of cryptocurrencies, governance issues with unregulated assets, and large bid-ask spreads. Regarding the future, Dr. Kwok remains observant: “Our findings are based on about eight years of cryptocurrency trading data, whereas stock markets have matured over decades. We are keen to see how the cryptocurrency market evolves and how investor behavior changes through different market cycles.” For everyday investors, Dr. Kwok offers simple advice: “Do your research; don’t buy into the hype.”
translated_content: 一项针对2015年至2022年超4000种加密货币的研究发现，高风险加密货币的表现通常逊于低风险币种。 研究显示，资产特异性风险最高的加密货币，年化平均回报为-9.36%；而风险最低的年化回报高达80.6%。 例如，截止2023年6月，比特币的年回报率为53.5%，而狗狗币回报率为-4.8%。 这项由悉尼大学经济学院学者主导的研究，是目前关于加密货币定价最全面的分析之一。 研究发表于《实证金融期刊》，挑战了“高风险高回报”的传统观点。 相反，研究强调了“低波动率异常”现象，高风险、类似彩票的投资反而表现更差。 首席研究员郭博士解释，造成这一现象的原因包括杠杆受限、做空难度、投资者偏好彩票型收益，以及过度自信等行为偏差。 尽管“低波动异常”在理论上为投资者带来机会，郭博士强调利用该机会非常有挑战性。 他说：“我们发现，投资者需要大量杠杆资金才能把握这一异常，但借钱投资也极大增加了破产风险。” 作者指出，想要利用该异常的交易者需要至少借贷50%的本金，但有可能损失高达84%的资本。 郭博士还指出，加密货币交易面临实际障碍，比如可交易币种有限、监管缺失，以及买卖价差大。 对于加密货币的未来，郭博士表示持续关注：“我们的结论基于约八年加密货币市场数据，而股票市场经历了数十年发展。我们期待见证加密货币市场及投资者行为在不同周期下的演变。” 对于普通投资者，郭博士的建议是：“要做好调研，别盲目跟风。”

article_content: Hampton University in Hampton, Virginia, was placed on lockdown for several hours Sunday morning after a former student shot two people in a dormitory before shooting himself, according to university and police officials. The incident occurred shortly before 1 a.m., when the former student entered Harkness Hall by following a pizza delivery person, stated Dr. William Harvey, the university's president, during a news conference. The former student proceeded to shoot the delivery person and the dormitory's night manager, who went into the hall after hearing gunshots, Harvey said. He then shot himself. No one was killed, but the attack led to the dorm's evacuation and a campus-wide lockdown. The three injured individuals were taken to local hospitals, and the dormitory night manager was treated and released. Police said the shooter is in custody. The motive remains unknown. Dr. Harvey commended the first-responders for their quick actions, which he believes helped prevent further tragedy. He also praised the school's emergency notification system for alerting students and staff. Hampton University is located about 70 miles southeast of Richmond, Virginia.

After 22 years of trying to have a daughter, Michigan couple Kateri and Jay Schwandt have welcomed their 12th son. The Schwandts began their family while still in college, with their first son, Ty. Hoping to eventually have a girl, they decided to try for one more child, but instead, their newest son, Tucker, was born on August 4th, 2013.

"This is a pretty testosterone-filled house!" Mr. Schwandt told Today. The couple’s sons are Tyler (21), Zach (17), Drew (16), Brandon (14), Tommy (11), Vinny (10), Calvin (8), Gabe (6), Wesley (5), Charlie (3), Luke (almost 2), and now baby Tucker. 

Mrs. Schwandt, the only woman in the home, admits she was hopeful to welcome some feminine energy this time. "We thought maybe, maybe, you know, we’re going to have a girl. Number 12 could be the one," she said. However, the couple expressed excitement at their growing family. "We are confident that he is going to fit right in," said Mr. Schwandt, joking that they gave up on expecting a girl a long time ago.

Their family’s growth has been gradual, beginning with a four-year gap between the first two sons, Ty and Zach. After that, a new baby arrived nearly every year or two. The Schwandts describe their big family as a happy accident that has brought them joy, even if it means even more chaos at home.

article_content: ABUJA, Nigeria — Many impoverished African countries are experiencing the harshest effects of climate change including severe drought, extreme heat, barren land, as well as unpredictable rainfall and catastrophic flooding. These environmental shocks intensify conflicts and disrupt livelihoods, especially since much of the population relies on increasingly vulnerable agriculture. Experts highlight that climate challenges are fundamental to the vulnerabilities faced by conflict-prone countries in Africa's Sahel region, including Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Niger, and northern Nigeria. According to the Global Commission on Adaptation, adapting to these climate pressures could require up to $50 billion yearly. Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency estimates that the continent's clean energy transition could cost as much as $190 billion each year—an overwhelming burden for Africa's constrained budgets. Leaders point out that further borrowing to fund climate goals would only deepen existing debt crises. They suggest that recent meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank in Marrakech, Morocco, offer a timely opportunity to address Africa’s financial constraints and capacity to manage climate shocks. There has been criticism that these global lending institutions do not sufficiently consider climate change and the vulnerabilities of poorer countries in their funding decisions. Kenyan President William Ruto, African Development Bank President Akinwumi Adesina, African Union Commission Chairman Moussa Faki, and Patrick Verkooijen, chief executive of the Global Commission on Adaptation, criticized the current global financial system as 'outdated, dysfunctional and unjust' in a New York Times opinion column. According to them, international financial institutions are too limited to fulfill their mandates, respond too slowly to new challenges like climate change, and discriminate against poorer countries. In recent years, funding for climate action in Africa has increased, recognizing that while the continent contributes little to global emissions, it faces the highest risk due to insufficient resources and support. Major development banks now view climate change as a significant economic threat. IMF economist Daniel Lee reported at the Marrakech panel that the organization is integrating climate change into policy advice, development, and lending, but offered few details on funding size or allocation. One recent IMF program funded only Rwanda in Africa—providing $319 million over three years. Both African leaders and experts agree that climate financing has fallen short, especially for Sahel countries ruled by unstable or unrecognized governments. Carlos Lopes of the University of Cape Town points out that most funding emphasizes mitigation, while adaptation—a pressing need in Africa—receives less attention. In Niger, where the government was overthrown in August, and in northern Nigeria, vast tracts of arable land are vanishing due to soil erosion and drought. This puts farmers and herders in competition over dwindling resources and opens opportunities for armed group recruitment, according to Idayat Hassan from the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Although irrigation projects could help, ongoing violence prevents farmers from accessing their land and boosts food insecurity. Ibrahim Audi, a 58-year-old wheat farmer from northern Katsina state, Nigeria, explains, 'Apart from extreme heat and unpredictable rain, insecurity often stops us from reaching our farms.' Femi Mimiko, a professor of political economy at Nigeria’s Obafemi Awolowo University, described the level of climate finance for Africa as 'negligible,' noting the immense challenges posed by stringent IMF and World Bank funding requirements. Professor Lopes further notes that Africa’s debt repayments—estimated at $62 billion this year—outstrip the continent’s adaptation costs. African leaders continue to urge for a pause on international debt repayments to free up funds for climate action. Experts warn that governments underestimate the links between climate change, economic instability, and violence. Hassan observed, 'National climate policy is lax—there’s little focus on the conflict-climate nexus in the Sahel, which must be prioritized as a root cause.' In Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger, currently ruled by military juntas, 16 million people require humanitarian assistance—a 172 percent increase since 2016—and over five million face acute food insecurity, according to the International Rescue Committee. The organization cites conflict and climate impacts as driving a worsening crisis for agriculture, the main livelihood for most residents. As Mimiko notes, 'Illegitimate governments limit not only compliance with IMF and World Bank funding criteria, but also access to support itself.' He argues that persuading or pressuring juntas towards 'timely redemocratization' is essential. ___ Associated Press climate and environmental coverage receives support from multiple foundations. translated_content: 阿布贾，尼日利亚 —— 许多贫困的非洲国家正面临气候变化带来的最严峻影响，包括严重干旱、极端高温、土地荒漠化，以及不可预测的降雨和毁灭性的洪水。这些环境冲击加剧了冲突并扰乱了生计，特别是大量人口依赖于日益脆弱的农业谋生。 专家指出，气候问题是导致非洲萨赫勒地区（包括布基纳法索、乍得、马里、尼日尔和尼日利亚北部）冲突国家脆弱性的根本原因。根据全球适应委员会的数据，适应这些气候压力每年可能需要高达500亿美元。同时，国际能源署估计，非洲清洁能源转型每年可能花费高达1900亿美元——对预算有限的非洲来说，这是巨大的负担。 各国领导人强调，继续借债以实现气候目标只会加重现有债务危机。他们建议，最近在摩洛哥马拉喀什举行的国际货币基金组织（IMF）和世界银行会议，是解决非洲财政困境和气候冲击应对能力的契机。全球贷款机构在资助决策时未能充分考虑气候变化和贫困国家脆弱性的批评声不断。 肯尼亚总统鲁托、非洲开发银行行长阿金武米·阿德西纳、非洲联盟委员会主席穆萨·法基和全球适应委员会首席执行官帕特里克·弗科伊恩，在《纽约时报》专栏中批评全球金融体系“过时、失灵且不公”。他们表示，国际金融机构规模有限，无法履行使命，对气候变化等新挑战反应过慢，并对贫困国家存有歧视。 近年来，非洲气候行动资金逐渐增加，人们认识到非洲对全球排放贡献微小，但由于资源和支持不足而面临最大风险。各主要发展银行现在将气候变化视为重要的经济威胁。IMF经济学家丹尼尔·李在马拉喀什的讨论会上称，IMF正在将气候变化纳入政策建议、能力建设和贷款，不过未具体说明资金规模或分配情况。近期一个IMF项目，仅向非洲卢旺达提供了三年3.19亿美元的资金。 非洲领导人和专家一致认为，非洲获得气候资金远远不够，尤其是由不稳定甚至未获国际承认政府掌控的萨赫勒国家。洛佩斯教授（开普敦大学）指出，绝大多数资金投入在减缓气候变化上，而非洲急需的适应性建设则关注不够。 在尼日尔（政府于8月被推翻）和尼日利亚北部，大量耕地因土壤侵蚀和干旱正在消失。战略与国际研究中心的哈桑表示，这导致农民与牧民因资源减少而竞争，也让武装团体更易招募成员。虽然灌溉项目本可助力，但持续暴力令农民难以耕作，加剧粮食安全问题。 尼日利亚卡齐纳州北部的58岁小麦种植户易卜拉欣·奥迪说：“除了极端高温和不可预测的降雨，不安全局势常常让我们无法下田。” 尼日利亚奥巴费米·阿沃洛沃大学政治经济学教授米米科认为，非洲获得的气候资金“极其有限”，严格的IMF和世行资金条件让本就严峻的挑战雪上加霜。 洛佩斯教授还指出，非洲今年的债务偿还预计将达620亿美元，已超过气候适应支出。非洲领导人持续呼吁暂停国际债务偿还以腾出应对气候的资金。专家警告，许多政府低估了气候变化、经济不稳和暴力之间的联系。哈桑说：“国内气候政策薄弱，对萨赫勒地区气候与冲突间的关联关注很少，这才是亟须重视的根源问题。” 根据国际救援委员会的数据，如今由军政府执政的布基纳法索、马里和尼日尔，有1600万人需要人道援助，比2016年上升172%，而超过500万人正经历严重粮食不安全。该组织认为，冲突和气候影响正在不断加剧农业危机，而农业是这些国家多数人的主要生计手段。 米米科指出：“非法政府不仅使IMF和世行的资助标准难以达标，甚至让获得援助本身成为难事。”他呼吁，必须劝导或施压这些军政府尽快推进“及时的重新民主化”。 ___ 美联社气候与环境报道获得多家基金会支持。AP对报道内容独立负责。

article_content: JetSynthesys, a digital entertainment company based in Pune, has formed a strategic partnership with Digital Hearts Holdings (DHH), a Japanese firm. Through this agreement, DHH will invest in JetSynthesys Japan, and JetSynthesys Japan will leverage DHH's expertise in quality assurance, customer support, and marketing to develop gaming products for the global market. The financial details of this deal have not been disclosed. DHH, headquartered and publicly listed in Tokyo, offers comprehensive services—including debugging, game translation, linguistic quality assurance, development support, and marketing—to gaming companies. The partnership is expected to stimulate business expansion for both firms in Japan and India and to introduce innovative gaming experiences. A significant element of the partnership is the creation of a 50:50 joint venture in India, focused on advancing debugging services in India and internationally by combining resources from both JetSynthesys and DHH. JetSynthesys Japan will assist DHH in growing its business presence in Western regions, while DHH will support JetSynthesys Japan’s activities in Japan and other major East Asian markets. Executives from both companies have expressed excitement about the collaboration. Rajan Navani, CEO of JetSynthesys, views the partnership as a key move to expand the company’s international reach and develop innovative games by leveraging a joint understanding of gaming trends and player behavior. Toshiya Tsukushi, COO of DHH, highlighted how the partnership will enable DHH to boost its presence in India and utilize JetSynthesys’ reach in Western markets. Ryo Shima, the head of JetSynthesys Japan, noted that plans include collaborative game development, operations, and talent management, expressing confidence the partnership will bring benefit to both sides. DHH and its affiliated companies will also contribute development and support resources for joint projects with JetSynthesys Japan.

article_content: Specialists advise maintaining some distance between mobile phones and the body, using speakerphone or earphones, and carrying phones in bags to reduce exposure. The possible connection between mobile phone usage and male sperm health is being closely studied, especially since average sperm counts worldwide have fallen by more than 50% over the past 50 years. According to a recent study cited by CNN, men aged 18 to 22 who used their mobile phones over 20 times a day had a 21% higher risk of overall low sperm count and a 30% higher risk of reduced sperm concentration—the number of sperm per milliliter of semen. The study did not analyze differences between phone activities like calls versus texts. Researchers found that earlier generations of phones (2G/3G) had more pronounced negative effects on sperm measures compared to more modern 4G and 5G models. This suggests some improvement as technology has advanced, although the reasons remain unclear, as noted by Allan Pacey from the University of Manchester. Experts stress that sperm health involves several factors, such as motility, DNA integrity, and proper shape, not just count. Alison Campbell of Care Fertility emphasized that while the research is noteworthy, it should not cause undue concern or abrupt lifestyle changes. She recommends exercise, balanced eating, maintaining a healthy weight, avoiding smoking and excessive drinking, and seeking medical support if conception is challenging. Mobile phones emit low-level radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMF), a topic of ongoing debate regarding their role in male fertility. These emissions are highest during heavy data use—such as streaming or downloading—particularly when signal strength is low. RF-EMF levels drop during less demanding tasks like texting. Even in peak scenarios, tissue temperature change is minor, under one degree Celsius. The California Department of Public Health points out that phone use in moving vehicles like trains or cars can also boost exposure levels. Therefore, experts recommend reducing direct contact by using hands-free options and storing phones in bags. While uncertainty about the direct effects of electromagnetic fields on fertility continues, maintaining a healthy lifestyle remains key for reproductive well-being.

article_content: The US dollar fell sharply on Thursday, tracking a drop in US Treasury yields as investors grew increasingly confident that the Federal Reserve has ended its aggressive rate hike cycle. The Fed left interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, as expected, with policymakers debating whether current financial conditions are restrictive enough to curb inflation. Fed Chair Jerome Powell noted that elevated Treasury yields, higher mortgage rates, and increased borrowing costs could impact the economy if they persist. The Fed's decision improved market sentiment on Wall Street, which spilled over into Asian markets, supporting risk-sensitive currencies like the Australian and New Zealand dollars. The Australian dollar climbed 0.5% to a three-week high of $0.6426, while the New Zealand dollar rose over 0.5% to a two-week high of $0.58825. The dollar index slipped alongside Treasury yields, which touched multi-week lows in early Asian trade. Wells Fargo chief economist Jay Bryson commented, 'It seems the FOMC is now in hold mode, with less likelihood of further rate increases than a few months ago.' The two-year Treasury yield dropped to a two-month low of 4.9250%, and the benchmark 10-year yield fell to a two-week low of 4.7070%. The euro gained 0.18% to $1.0589 against the dollar, and the US dollar index fell 0.11% to 106.34. Fresh data showed US manufacturing contracted sharply in October, suggesting rates may have peaked, though a still-resilient labor market could keep rates higher for longer. Lon Erickson, portfolio manager at Thornburg Investment Management, said, 'We will likely need to see some labor market weakness before target inflation is reached. This could take time and is one reason we expect higher rates for longer.' According to CME FedWatch, market pricing now shows a nearly 15% chance of a rate cut as early as March, up from around 10% a week prior. The weaker dollar provided some relief for the yen, which stood at 150.44 per dollar after falling to a one-year low of 151.74 earlier in the week following the Bank of Japan's policy move. Investors are still assessing the impact of the BOJ's tweaks to its bond yield control policy, which have triggered volatility in Japan's bond and currency markets. Tom Kenny, senior international economist at ANZ, remarked, 'This feels like the end of the line for YCC, but the extent to which the BOJ will intervene if 10-year yields exceed 1% remains unclear.' Sterling rose 0.35% to $1.2192 ahead of the Bank of England's rate decision, where no change is expected. In business, Apple Inc. reported record quarterly revenue in India, with CEO Tim Cook highlighting strong double-digit growth and India's importance as a strategic market. Meanwhile, the Indian luxury car market is trending younger, with significant portions of Audi, Mercedes-Benz, and BMW buyers now under 40. Additionally, Sony is reportedly considering replacing Punit Goenka as CEO of the proposed Sony-Zee merged entity amid ongoing investigations by Indian regulators.

article_content: Following a healthcare reform town hall in Belgrade, Montana, President Obama plans to unwind with his family in the state’s picturesque landscape, where he’ll try his hand at fly-fishing for the first time. White House Chief of Staff Rahm Emanuel was spotted carrying fishing equipment onto Marine One to prepare for the trip. Fly-fishing—requiring focus and precision much like golf—mirrors the challenges of leadership. The adventure draws a clear parallel between learning a new outdoor skill and tackling the responsibilities of a presidency. Instructor Tony Derosier explains that as anglers progress, they shift from simply wanting to catch a fish, to catching many, then bigger ones, before ultimately rediscovering the pure enjoyment of fishing itself. At this point, Obama is focused on catching the 'big fish'—achieving health care reform. A victory here would be a standout accomplishment, with future successes being additional rewards. The techniques of fly-fishing offer metaphorical lessons for politics: mastering a good cast, reading the river to find fish, and reeling in the catch all align with political strategy. Derosier notes that proper timing during a cast is crucial, resembling Obama’s need to move reforms forward without exhausting momentum or losing support. Just like reading river currents to determine where fish gather, Obama needs to identify and persuade key political figures, particularly those who are difficult to win over, such as Blue Dog Democrats and Republicans in conservative Montana. Landing a fish, Derosier points out, involves a delicate balance of pressure—too much risks the line breaking, too little and the fish escapes. Achieving healthcare reform requires the same finesse with congressional negotiations. Out in Montana’s rivers, catch-and-release is the goal, but in Washington, bringing the 'big one'—healthcare legislation—home is what matters most to Obama.

article_content: After many years away from the spotlight, Caroline Kennedy is emerging as a possible candidate to replace Hillary Clinton in the U.S. Senate following Clinton’s nomination as Secretary of State. If Caroline is selected, the Kennedy family’s presence in the Senate would continue, a tradition that began with her father, John F. Kennedy, in 1952. Her uncle, Ted Kennedy, served Massachusetts for decades, and her late uncle, Robert Kennedy, once held the New York seat. Caroline has usually kept her distance from political office, but her recent public support for Barack Obama signaled a new level of political engagement. She has reportedly sought advice from close friends and advisers about the Senate position. According to New York Governor David Paterson, Kennedy has asked about the role, but hasn’t officially expressed her intent to seek the seat. Most of Caroline’s life and work are closely tied to New York City, where she grew up, attended college and law school, and worked in various civic and cultural organizations. She has edited books, overseen her father’s presidential library, and been involved with institutions like the Kennedy Center Honors and the American Ballet Theatre. Taking an elected office would represent a major change for Caroline, given her preference for privacy and her nonpartisan civic work. Her political inexperience has helped her avoid intense criticism so far, but those close to her say she is giving the Senate seat serious thought. There are several high-profile contenders for Clinton’s seat, including New York’s Attorney General Andrew Cuomo, but Caroline’s influential family background could be a decisive factor. At 51, Caroline Kennedy, a mother of three, has not made any public announcements about running. Earlier interviews show her interest in public issues, even as she previously avoided making political plans. Her significant involvement in Obama’s campaign is her most active participation in partisan politics so far. If appointed, Caroline Kennedy would enter a new phase in her public life, facing heightened political attention and new challenges.

article_content: I believed I was prepared for North Korea. Having spent much of my life studying, traveling to, and living in the former Soviet Union and other Communist or post-Communist countries, I expected similarities. When we arrived at Pyongyang airport, the emptiness reminded me of Leningrad in 1969—our flight being the only one scheduled that day. From our plane, a large color portrait of Kim Il Sung, North Korea's 'Great Leader,' looked down on us. Over the next nine days, portraits of Kim Il Sung and his son, Kim Jong Il, the current leader known as the 'Dear Leader,' were omnipresent—on buildings, monuments, bridges, and even on lapel pins worn by everyone, including our guides, Mr. Jang and Mr. Song. Their presence echoed my experiences in the Soviet Union, where Lenin’s image and slogans like 'Lenin lived, Lenin lives, Lenin will live' dominated the landscape. Kim Il Sung, who died in 1994, maintains a similar posthumous influence. The preserved bodies of both leaders, displayed in mausoleums, further parallel Soviet practices, reportedly with Russian expertise assisting North Korea in this political symbolism. Pyongyang’s streets, sparse in traffic except for official cars, recalled Moscow in the 1960s. Instead of Zils or Volgas, officials now ride mostly older Mercedes, some in conspicuous baby blue. Exploring local life often means visiting food stores and markets. For days, we asked to see markets where small-scale capitalism is emerging and citizens are allowed to sell produce—an effort to ease food shortages. One evening, without a guide, I viewed a state-owned store through a window. Like Russia decades earlier, shelves were sparse, with only a few cans, onions, and cucumbers. In Pyongyang, stores are better supplied than in the countryside, where hunger is more severe. Our interactions were carefully managed. In Russia, guides strictly controlled tourists’ exposure; Mr. Jang and Mr. Song behaved similarly, ensuring we saw nothing that might reflect poorly on the regime. Even requests to photograph the countryside were met with reluctance. Once, Mr. Jang stopped us from filming an elderly woman, possibly to avoid negative impressions. Mr. Song, a former diplomat, was somewhat more relaxed, sharing a smile when we recounted similar experiences from the Soviet era. Every encounter seemed orchestrated. When we requested to see everyday life, guides took us to a city park where elderly women, dressed in traditional hanbok, were singing and dancing. It was a charming scene, yet our guide reminded us, 'They knew you were coming,' highlighting the pervasive staging. North Korea projects a militarized image, with daily life organized around collective activities. Despite the regimented environment, there are touches of formality and even modest adornments—like occasional jewelry—hinting at slow social change. Young women in Pyongyang direct the sparse traffic in neat uniforms, reminiscent of Soviet-era schoolgirls. Understanding true public sentiment proved challenging. With our foreign appearance and journalist armbands, blending in was impossible. In the Soviet Union, dissent sometimes revealed itself under the surface; in North Korea, conformity is even more pronounced. At the Arirang Mass Games, thousands performed elaborate routines to mark historical events, with the audience responding rapturously to Kim Jong Il’s entrance. Mr. Jang tried to explain North Korean self-reliance using a rabbit metaphor, positioning Korea between major powers and advocating unity for survival. On a trip to a mountainside museum, we saw gifts from global leaders to Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, including a lavish train car from Stalin. A final room revealed a life-size, eerily lifelike figure of Kim Il Sung amid an artificial scene, with guides bowing reverently. Whether these displays reflect genuine reverence or are simply more theater remains impossible to confirm.
translated_content: 我曾以为自己已经为朝鲜做好了准备。毕竟，我曾大半生都在前苏联和其他共产主义或后共产主义国家学习、旅行和生活，期待能发现共同点。当我们抵达平壤机场时，那种空荡荡的场景让我想起1969年的列宁格勒——当天只有我们这一班航班。从飞机上望去，一幅朝鲜“伟大领袖”金日成的大幅彩色画像俯视着我们。 在接下来的九天里，金日成和他的儿子、现任领导人“亲爱的领袖”金正日的画像无处不在——高悬于建筑、纪念碑和桥梁上，甚至每个人胸前的胸针上，包括我们的向导张先生和宋先生。他们的存在让我想起在苏联的经历，那里列宁的形象和“列宁活着、列宁将永远活着”这样的口号随处可见。1994年去世的金日成也以类似的方式在朝鲜产生着身后影响力。 两位领导人的遗体都被保存、陈列在陵墓中，这种做法与苏联的传统相似，据说是在俄罗斯专家的帮助下完成的。平壤街头除了公务汽车，几乎没有其他车辆，和上世纪60年代的莫斯科颇为相似。不同的是，这里官员们多乘坐色彩醒目的老款梅赛德斯，比如婴儿蓝等颜色，而非苏联的Zil或Volga。 了解当地生活往往要从食品商店和市场开始。我们花了好几天才得以参观正在兴起的小型市场，公民可以出售自家农产品，这也是缓解朝鲜食品短缺的一种尝试。有一天晚上，我独自偷偷看了一家国营商店的橱窗，里面货架很空，只有几罐鱼罐头、几个洋葱和黄瓜。这是在供应相对充足的平壤，农村地区饥饿状况更为严重。 我们的接触都受到严格管理。在苏联，导游严密控制游客能见到的内容；朝鲜的张先生和宋先生也是如此，确保我们不会接触任何对政权不利的景象。就连拍摄乡村的请求也很难获准。有一次张先生阻止我们拍摄一位老人，或许是不想留下负面印象。相比之下，做过外交官的宋先生稍微宽容一些，听我们讲述苏联时期类似经历时也会露出微笑。 几乎每次接触都是被安排好的。当我们要求参观普通人的生活时，导游最终带我们去了市公园，那里一些身穿传统韩服的老妇人在唱歌跳舞，场面非常迷人。但导游仍特意提醒我们：“他们知道你们会来”，暗示这一切都经过预先安排。 朝鲜社会的日常生活充满军事化氛围，集体活动成为常态。尽管环境严谨，但偶尔能看到些许修饰，比如女士佩戴的简单饰品，说明社会正在缓慢变化。平壤年轻女性在街头穿着整齐制服，指挥稀少的交通，仿佛苏联时代的女学生。 真正了解民众内心想法非常困难。我们穿着西式服装，佩戴记者臂章，完全无法融入其中。在苏联，表面之下偶尔会遇到异见者；但在朝鲜，社会的统一程度更高。在“阿里郎”大型团体体操表演上，数千人一起庆祝历史事件，观众在金正日入场时反应非常热烈。 张先生曾用兔子的比喻来解释朝鲜的自力更生，把朝鲜比作夹在大国之间、只能依靠团结自救的小动物。 我们曾去山中的一座博物馆参观，那里陈列着世界各国领导人送给金日成和金正日的礼物，包括斯大林赠送的豪华火车车厢。参观尾声见到一尊金日成的真人大小模型，身处人工造景之中，导游们虔诚地鞠躬致意。这些景象究竟是真心敬仰还是精心设定的表演，我们也无从判断。
