article_content: During World War II, American pilot Roland 'Bud' Wolfe joined the Royal Air Force and crash-landed his Spitfire into an Irish peat bog. Surviving the incident, Wolfe was taken by Irish authorities to Curragh Camp, an internment facility where Allied and German prisoners coexisted and famously played football matches together. Wolfe lost his U.S. citizenship for enlisting with the British before the United States entered the war. Although he managed to escape to British territory at one point, he was returned to the camp to avoid diplomatic tensions. Nearly 70 years after Wolfe's Spitfire went down in County Donegal in 1941, archaeologists recovered significant portions of the aircraft from the peat bog. The Spitfire was one of 20 paid for by Canadian philanthropist Willard Garfield Weston. The BBC Northern Ireland’s program, with historian Dan Snow and archaeologist Simon Parry, led the recovery, unearthing not only the plane but also six Browning .303 machine guns and about 1,000 rounds of ammunition. Curragh Camp was noted for its lenient conditions, with prisoners sometimes allowed out for recreational activities, and even social gatherings with the opposing side. Despite these conditions, Wolfe was determined to keep fighting. After spending two years in the camp, he was finally released to return to active duty as the Allies began gaining momentum. The aircraft and recovered weaponry will be conserved and displayed at museums in Derry, highlighting a unique story in aviation and wartime history.

A leading academic has called for a broader inquiry into sexual abuse within UK music schools, following the conviction of a choirmaster and his ex-wife for abusing a former pupil. Michael Brewer and his former wife Kay (also known as Hillary), both aged 68, were found guilty of six counts of indecent assault. Their victim, Frances Andrade, 48, a former pupil at Chetham’s School of Music in Manchester, died by suicide shortly after testifying against them.

On the evening of the verdict, another academic and former Chetham’s pupil, Ian Pace, advocated for a comprehensive investigation into sexual abuse at music schools during the 1970s and 80s. Pace, a pianist and musicologist who lectures at City University in London, emphasized that classical music is controlled by a small group of powerful individuals, making it difficult for victims to come forward. He stated: ‘It is well known within the music world that there are many such stories involving influential staff at various music schools. Many survivors are afraid to speak out in an environment where careers are shaped by a few powerful figures. A full, independent inquiry into sexual and physical abuse in classical music education during this time is absolutely essential.’

The court heard that Michael Brewer, director of music at Chetham’s, began abusing Frances Andrade when she was 14, in 1978, and that his ex-wife joined in after Frances turned 18. The trial revealed that sexual abuse was widespread at the academy and that Andrade was not alone in her experiences. Greater Manchester Police have asked anyone who may have suffered abuse at the school to come forward and have defended the care provided to Frances Andrade during the trial at Manchester Crown Court.

Jurors were not informed of Mrs. Andrade’s death until after delivering their guilty verdict. Michael Brewer and his ex-wife have been remanded in custody and will be sentenced at a later date.

article_content: During an event marking the United Nations' World Disability Day in Istanbul, Altinok Oz, the Mayor of Kartal district, playfully tapped Ozgur Ugur, a visually impaired spokesman for the Republican People's Party, on the back of the head as Mr. Ugur addressed the crowd. Spectators were surprised by the gesture, which took place at a rally organized by the party. As Mr. Ugur turned to understand what happened, Mayor Oz, smiling, made a 'shhh' gesture before greeting Mr. Ugur with a friendly kiss on both cheeks. The act drew a mix of laughter and discomfort from the audience. Mr. Ugur, representing the municipality’s disabled people unit, attempted to locate his assailant by turning in the wrong direction before Mayor Oz stopped him and offered the cheek kisses. The incident sparked criticism online and offline, with some people accusing the mayor of insensitivity and calling for his resignation. One commenter, Selcuk Potuk, questioned whether the mayor understood the gravity of his actions. According to the United Nations, more than a billion people globally—about 15% of the population—have some form of disability. The UN notes that disabled individuals often face poorer health, lower education, fewer economic opportunities, and higher rates of poverty compared to those without disabilities. Observing the Day, UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon emphasized that barriers to inclusion and a lack of accessible services contribute to hardships for people with disabilities. He highlighted the potential for technology to empower them in society and the workforce. The mayor's spokesperson described the gesture as a joke between friends and compared it to a ritual greeting. Mr. Ugur was quoted defending Mayor Oz, calling the act a 'beautiful greeting' and expressing that people misunderstood the context.

article_content:
Animal rights group PETA is urging the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to return a $2.1 million research grant after reports of animal cruelty were made public. The call follows documentation of ongoing animal suffering at UCSF, which operates one of the largest medical research programs in the United States.

Recipients of National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants must follow strict animal welfare protocols. Previously, UCSF paid a $92,500 settlement after federal investigators found violations of the Animal Welfare Act. Recent NIH reports show that neglect and mistreatment of animals persist at the university.

Abuses noted include laboratory mice having toes removed without anesthesia, birds and a squirrel monkey receiving little or no pain relief after surgery, and some animals being denied adequate food or water. Animal rights advocates argue that small fines do little to promote higher welfare standards.

One case that has drawn significant attention involves Petra, a rhesus monkey. Petra participated in a Parkinson’s disease study involving the surgical implantation of a device in her skull. After the device was removed, screws were left in place, and Petra developed a chronic infection and suffered pain for two years. Inspectors later discovered acrylic left in her head. Following the removal of the foreign material, Petra was euthanized. Inspectors stated that the failure to minimize Petra’s suffering was not consistent with the Animal Welfare Act.

PETA is asking the NIH to demand the return of the $2.1 million grant connected to Petra’s study. UCSF states that animal testing is only used when necessary, with computer models and cell cultures prioritized as alternatives. The university asserts that it takes animal welfare seriously and strives to use the smallest number of animals possible, in line with regulatory requirements. The USDA also conducts unannounced annual inspections to enforce compliance with the Animal Welfare Act.

动物权益机构PETA在多起校园动物残忍对待事件曝光后，呼吁加州大学旧金山分校（UCSF）退还210万美元研究经费。作为美国最大医学研究机构之一，UCSF长期被指出存在动物受虐问题。

国家卫生研究院（NIH）要求受资助机构严格遵守动物福利政策。此前UCSF因联邦调查员查实其违反《动物福利法》，支付了9.25万美元和解金。最新NIH报告显示，该校动物忽视和虐待问题依旧突出。

具体问题包括实验鼠无麻醉切除脚趾，鸟类与松鼠猴手术后几乎未获止痛，部分动物长时间缺乏食物或水。动物保护人士认为，罚款金额过低，难以改善动物福利状况。

引发关注的典型案例为恒河猴Petra。她为帕金森病研究被植入装置，移除后螺钉残留导致长期感染，经历两年痛苦。调查后发现其头部还有丙烯异物，移除后Petra被实施安乐死。调查员认定该案例未按《动物福利法》保障动物权益。

PETA已要求NIH追回与Petra相关研究的210万美元经费。UCSF则称，动物实验仅在无替代方案时使用，并倾向于采用计算机模型和细胞培养。校方表示高度重视动物照护，努力减少实验动物数量，并依规定行事。美国农业部每年也会突击检查，确保研究机构遵守《动物福利法》。

article_content: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has unveiled a year-long infrastructure programme worth N100 billion to update the state’s public facilities. The comprehensive plan includes the renovation of 345 health centres, improved water access in 332 wards, upgrades to 31 schools, reconstruction of 45 kilometers of roads, and construction of five new flyovers at key points. While the announcement initially raised doubts among attendees regarding funding, Governor Adeleke assured that the projects would be financed entirely from Osun State's own revenue streams, without loans. He highlighted measures taken to stop financial leakages and boost internally generated revenue (IGR), explaining that the funds are kept in a special project account. Community members in areas slated for development have generally welcomed the move, noting the anticipated benefits for local traffic, health, and safety. Leaders from Ilesa, Ikirun, and Ile-Ife voiced strong support, encouraging residents to cooperate with the initiative. Not all stakeholders agree: the opposition, especially the APC, has raised alarms about possible debt risks and questioned whether the initiative is genuinely in the public interest. Conversely, some community leaders and civil society groups praised Adeleke’s ambitious response to Osun's infrastructure shortfall but called for continued transparency and financial prudence. Governor Adeleke has reaffirmed his commitment to transparency, vowing to follow due procurement processes and update the public on the management of the project fund. The government intends to start work immediately, using available resources, amid ongoing debate about the plan’s sustainability.

article_content: Over Roswell, New Mexico, massive supercell storms recently formed—remarkably shaped like the classic flying saucer—prompting a sense of awe not unlike scenes from “Independence Day.” Storm chaser Jody Miller from California traveled to capture these breathtaking weather events with his camera, undeterred by the risks involved in getting close to such volatile conditions. The dramatic clouds appeared near Roswell, not far from the famously secret military site Area 51, stirring reminders of the town’s long-standing associations with UFO tales. The sky was dominated by a vast, swirling storm system casting the landscape in deep gray, its rotating updraft—called a mesocyclone—reaching towards the ground where tornadoes sometimes form. Miller, 63, has chased severe storms for two years, often heading out with experienced meteorologists to ensure safety. He insists that while storm chasing can be dangerous, proper precautions can minimize the risk. His photographs, taken on June 7, show enormous storm clouds rolling over New Mexico’s desert, dwarfing everything beneath. Supercells are the most uncommon and severe type of thunderstorm, capable of producing hail, flooding, lightning, and tornadoes. They occur under the right conditions worldwide but are most frequent in the central US and certain South American plains. While these storms more often pass over unpopulated stretches, they can cause serious destruction when they sweep through towns and cities—sometimes with tragic consequences.

article_content: A man has been arrested and an American bully XL dog has been seized after a security guard was reportedly bitten. Police were called to Highcross Shopping Centre in Leicester at about 12:30 GMT on Saturday following reports that a security guard had been bitten by a dog when the owner was refused entry to a shop. Officers later arrested a man in Silver Street on suspicion of allowing a dog to be dangerously out of control in a public place and causing injury. Police said he has since been released on bail, and the dog has been taken to a place of safety. The security guard sustained injuries to his arm and leg, received hospital treatment, and has now been discharged. His injuries are not believed to be serious. It will be illegal to own an American bully XL in England and Wales from 1 February, with the ban being introduced after a series of attacks involving the breed.

article_content:
Forty-one men from diverse Indian states—including Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar, West Bengal, Uttarakhand, Assam, and Himachal Pradesh—are trapped inside the collapsed Uttarkashi tunnel. Despite coming from different parts of the country, these workers share the common goal of seeking better livelihoods due to limited job opportunities at home.

The workers are divided into skilled and unskilled categories, earning Rs 24,000 and Rs 18,000 per month respectively. They typically work 12 hours a day, seven days a week, with just two days off each month, as reported by their families.

The incident has left families waiting anxiously for over ten days, clinging to hope for the safe return of their loved ones. In Odisha, individuals like Bisweswar Nayak, with over two decades of experience and a family depending on him, are among those trapped. His wife found solace in his last voice message. Similarly, Dhiren Nayak promised his family a return in January for Makar Sankranti, reflecting the sacrifices these workers made.

Migration for employment is echoed across other regions. In Jharkhand’s Khirabera village, nine men went to work at the tunnel, three of whom remain inside. The lack of job opportunities locally continues to drive such migration. Uttar Pradesh’s trapped workers mostly come from Shravasti's Motipur Kala village and are members of the Tharu community. Many families are experiencing the separation of migration for the first time.

In Assam, two men from Ramphalbil village have spent months away, working to support their families. Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district shows villagers coming together for a trapped youth, Vishal, even as they skip festival celebrations out of concern.

West Bengal families, including those of Soubhik Pakhira and Manik Talukdar, cope with uncertainty and hope. Bihar’s workers have been away from their home state for years, illustrating the ongoing trend of migration for better income.

Despite their anxiety, the families express gratitude for rescue efforts and urge the government to create stable local job opportunities so that future generations might stay closer to home.

来自贾坎德邦、北方邦、奥里萨邦、比哈尔邦、西孟加拉邦、北阿坎德邦、阿萨姆邦和喜马偕尔邦等多个印度邦的41名工人，被困在乌塔尔卡什隧道坍塌事故中。尽管他们来自全国各地，这些工人都因家乡就业机会有限，被迫外出谋生。

这些工人分为熟练工和非熟练工，月薪分别为24,000卢比和18,000卢比。据家属称，他们通常每天工作12小时，每周七天，每月只有两天假期。

事故已过去十多天，家属们焦急等待着亲人平安归来，怀抱希望。在奥里萨邦，拥有二十多年经验、养家糊口的比斯韦斯瓦尔·纳亚克等工人被困隧道。他的妻子因收到他最后的语音留言而获得些许安慰。同样，德伦·纳亚克承诺家人1月的马卡尔·桑克兰提节回家，体现了工人的牺牲精神。

这种为生计而外出务工的情形在其他地区也屡见不鲜。在贾坎德邦克希拉贝拉村，九人赴隧道打工，其中三人被困。由于本地就业机会稀缺，外出务工成为普遍现象。北方邦的被困工人大多来自斯拉瓦斯提县莫蒂普尔卡拉村，属于塔鲁族社区，许多家庭首次经历亲人外出务工。

在阿萨姆邦，兰法尔比尔村的两名工人已外出数月，努力养家。喜马偕尔邦曼迪地区，村民们为被困青年维沙尔日夜祈祷，甚至放弃了节日庆祝。

西孟加拉邦索比克·帕基拉、曼尼克·塔卢克达等家庭正经历着焦虑和希望的煎熬。比哈尔邦工人多年在外，突出表现了长期劳动力迁徙的社会现实。

尽管承受巨大压力，家属们对救援工作表示感谢，并呼吁政府创造更多本地就业机会，让下一代能留在家乡。

article_content: A man who dumped a large pile of rubbish on a secluded country lane was fined £1,000 after authorities tracked him down using a McDonald’s receipt left in the trash. Patrick Lishman, 30, abandoned scraps of wood, plastic bags, and electrical fittings on Washingwell Lane in Whickham, Tyne and Wear, before driving off. Gateshead Council investigators discovered two crumpled McDonald’s receipts among the waste, which showed purchases made at the Shearlegs Road McDonald’s in Gateshead. By checking CCTV footage, officials saw Lishman’s white Ford Transit van at the drive-through, loaded with rubbish. The van’s license plate led them to Lishman’s home in Marian Court, Gateshead. In Gateshead Magistrates Court, Lishman admitted to fly-tipping and was fined £1,000, plus £100 in costs and a £100 victim surcharge. Colin Huntington of Gateshead Council praised the investigators, noting that even minor clues can help identify offenders and that there are serious penalties for illegal dumping. The dumping occurred on January 16, and some waste traced back to Durham Prison, where Lishman had worked as a subcontractor. The article also references previous offenders tracked via evidence left with their rubbish, such as Scott Hamilton and Mohammed Javad, illustrating authorities’ determination to catch fly-tippers by following up on any available clues.

article_content: Ed McMahon, the longtime television announcer and beloved sidekick to Johnny Carson on 'The Tonight Show,' has died at age 86. McMahon passed away peacefully shortly after midnight at Ronald Reagan/UCLA Medical Center, according to his publicist, Howard Bragman. He had faced several health challenges in recent years, including a neck injury from a 2007 fall and a hospitalization for pneumonia in February. Throughout his career, McMahon hosted shows such as 'Star Search' and 'TV's Bloopers and Practical Jokes,' but he achieved his greatest fame working alongside Johnny Carson from 1962 to 1992. The pair first met in 1957, shortly after Carson began hosting 'Who Do You Trust?'. Their partnership became legendary, with McMahon's jovial energy complementing Carson's reserved wit. McMahon's signature introduction, 'Heeeeeeerre's Johnny!', became part of television history, while his infectious laughter and supportive presence made him a favorite among viewers. He was also well known for his promotional work, endorsing brands like Budweiser, American Family Insurance, and Alpo dog food. He fondly recalled a humorous incident when Carson playfully interrupted one of his dog food commercials on air. Born in Detroit, Michigan, on March 6, 1923, McMahon frequently relocated during his childhood due to his father’s work as a promoter. He served in the Marines during World War II and the Korean War. Despite receiving a substantial salary at NBC, McMahon faced financial difficulties later in life due to multiple divorces and poor investments. In 2008, it was reported he risked foreclosure on his Beverly Hills home, though he ultimately made arrangements to keep it. McMahon was married three times and had six children, one of whom, Michael, died in 1995. He is survived by his wife, Pamela, and five children. Widely recognized as one of television's greatest sidekicks, McMahon left a lasting impact on American entertainment.

article_content: On Friday, SAG-AFTRA’s National Board voted overwhelmingly to approve a tentative agreement with studio CEOs and the AMPTP, signaling the end of the union’s 118-day strike. The union has since released details of the deal, describing it as 'valued at more than one billion dollars in new wages and benefit plan funding.' The SAG-AFTRA National Board approved the agreement with an 86% majority. Members will receive an 80-page summary of the agreement on November 13. The ratification vote starts November 14 and runs until early December for the union’s 160,000 eligible members. Union leaders called the tentative agreement 'a landmark achievement,' highlighting new protections and consent rights around artificial intelligence, which had been a major issue in negotiations. While details at today’s press conference were limited, the union did emphasize wage increases, improved casting guidelines, higher relocation allowances, and increased health and pension fund contributions. The contract sets a new wage pattern with two increases in the first year: 7% upon ratification and a further 4% in July 2024, compounding to 11.28%. An additional 3.5% increase is set for July 2025. Background actors’ wages will rise by 11% on November 12, 2023, then by 4% in July 2024 and 3.5% in July 2025. For the first time, background positions in the West Coast Zones will match those of the East Coast Zones, potentially adding 11,000 new background workdays annually. Contributions to Health and Pension/Retirement funds will rise, with caps increasing significantly—by 43% for one-hour productions and 67% for half-hour productions—helping more performers qualify for benefits. A notable feature is the creation of a new compensation stream for actors working in streaming, including a substantial bonus. Most compensation will go to actors in highly viewed programs, with the rest distributed through a jointly-managed fund. Stunt coordinators will now receive fixed residuals for TV and new media work. The deal includes progress on hair and makeup equity, diversity reporting, gender-neutral language, access to gender-affirming care, more comprehensive sexual harassment prevention, and use of intimacy coordinators. There are new standards for casting, including advance scripts, page limits for self-tapes, and guidelines around nudity and audition processes, with special provisions for minors and disabilities. Relocation allowances have improved, now offering $5,000 per month for up to six months, with no limit on eligible seasons—an effective 153% increase over previous rates. The cumulative wage increases, totaling about 14.8%, are higher than the WGA’s 13% in a recent deal. SAG-AFTRA’s criteria for streaming bonuses are similar to the WGA’s: bonuses apply only when a show is watched by at least 20% of a streamer’s domestic subscribers within 90 days of release. SAG-AFTRA expects the streaming bonus pool to distribute about $120 million over the contract term, or $40 million a year—less than the initial $500 million sought. President Fran Drescher acknowledged only a small portion of shows will qualify. She hopes to lower the bonus threshold to 10% in the next round of negotiations beginning before the contract expires in 2026. Both Drescher and Crabtree-Ireland described the deal as 'industry-breaking.' Whether this stands up compared to recent DGA and WGA agreements will become clearer once the full summary is public. Further negotiations are anticipated as the contract’s end date nears.

Several prominent female celebrities are threatening to sue Google for $100 million after personal, explicit photos were shared online due to an iCloud hack. Marty Singer, an attorney representing over a dozen women, has sent a letter to Google’s top executives—including Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Eric Schmidt—accusing the company of not acting quickly enough to remove the images from its services. The letter alleges Google has failed to protect the privacy of the victims and has profited from the incident instead. While the specific clients named in Singer’s representation are not clear, celebrities affected by the leak include Jennifer Lawrence, Kate Upton, Amber Heard, Rihanna, Ariana Grande, and Cara Delevingne.

Singer asserts that his firm, Lavely & Singer, has issued multiple takedown requests over several weeks, but many images remain accessible on sites like BlogSpot and YouTube. In his letter, Singer draws a comparison between Google’s response and the NFL’s handling of the Ray Rice scandal, implying that both organizations overlooked or enabled the mistreatment of women. Additional victims reportedly include Kim Kardashian, Hope Solo, Aubrey Plaza, Gabrielle Union, Vanessa Hudgens, and Kaley Cuoco. The letter criticizes Google for allegedly failing to adequately address these privacy violations and for profiting from the notoriety surrounding the scandal, sparking ongoing public criticism.

article_content: Since the Hamas attacks on October 7, Israel’s left is facing a crisis of identity amid a surge in nationalism. In cities like Ashkelon, the echoes of explosions from the nearby Gaza Strip serve as a constant reminder of the conflict. Danielle, a 22-year-old who identifies as left-wing, says the violence has shaken her beliefs. 'After that Saturday, many people who believed in peace lost that belief—it became personal,' she explains, recounting how attackers targeted and killed civilians in kibbutzim. Danielle notes that before October 7, there was greater empathy toward the people in Gaza, with the left championing understanding and dialogue. Now, she and her friends see things differently, feeling frustration that resources meant for Gaza's welfare are used by Hamas for attacks instead. This disillusionment is widespread as Israeli society grapples with trauma and heightened nationalist sentiment. National flags are now a common sight, and the political climate has become intensely charged. Some, like engineer Ohad Gur, remain steadfastly left-wing and advocate for negotiations rather than military escalation. He acknowledges, however, that peers on the left have grown more militant in response, a shift he attributes to emotional reactions that may ease over time. Amid ongoing anti-government protests in Tel Aviv, others illustrate the emotional complexity. Talia Keinan and Gai Sherf, mourning friends lost in the attacks and grappling with having a loved one captive in Gaza, describe how left-wing Israelis have become more defensive and patriotic, blurring the line between self-defense and revenge. Both express fears about where this new atmosphere may lead. Dennis, speaking from a café in East Jerusalem, observes that people on the far left are expressing unusually emotional or nationalistic views, but he chooses to avoid political arguments. Though personally affected by the attacks and wishing for an end to Hamas, he does not support a large ground operation in Gaza, instead seeking escape from the charged political climate. Nadav Hakham, a consultant with right-of-center views, observes broader unity in Israel amid a feeling of existential threat. He notes former left-leaning friends now engage actively in pro-Israel events and lament global criticism of Israel’s response. At a Palestinian-Israeli solidarity event in northern Israel, Aldema—a photographer from a kibbutz—shares how the violence has deeply traumatized communities known for left-wing, even pro-Palestinian, sentiments. While still advocating peace, he now believes the left must be realistic about the need for military action given recent events. Activists and leaders like Roee Aloni of B’tselem and Ofer Cassif of the Hadash coalition say it's too soon to know the long-term political consequences, as emotions are still raw. Historically, conflict has pushed Israeli leftists to the right, and some now voice right-wing ideas. Others feel disappointed by the international left’s response to Hamas’s actions. The heated atmosphere has made those who sympathize with Palestinians vulnerable to criticism, with Cassif himself suspended from the Knesset after condemning government policy, though he believes leftist opposition will eventually recover. Public frustration with government handling of hostages mixes with anti-Netanyahu protests, sometimes leading to tense confrontations between those urging unity and those demanding accountability. Some, like Rey Kanterewicz, insist that now is the time to focus on supporting hostages’ families rather than political disputes. Yet others, like Gideon Avaltal Eppstein, continue to protest government decisions despite facing public backlash. As political divisions blur in the face of national trauma, many Israelis are setting politics aside—at least for now—to prioritize unity and support for those most affected by the conflict.
translated_content: 自10月7日哈马斯袭击以来，以色列左派在民族主义高涨的氛围中面临身份危机。在如阿什克隆这样的城市，来自加沙地带的爆炸声成为冲突持续的提醒。22岁的Danielle自认为是左翼分子，她表示此次暴力事件动摇了自己的信念。她解释道：“在那天之后，许多原本相信和平的人失去了信念——一切都变得个人化了”，并回忆了袭击者在基布兹杀害平民的情景。 Danielle指出，10月7日之前，对于加沙民众拥有更多同情心，左派主张理解和对话。但现在，她和朋友们的看法已经改变，对用于加沙福利的资源被哈马斯用来发动袭击感到愤懑。这种失望在整个以色列社会中蔓延，人们正在应对创伤和高涨的民族主义情绪。国旗如今随处可见，政治氛围变得异常激烈。 一些人，如工程师Ohad Gur，依然坚持左翼立场，主张通过谈判而非军事升级来解决冲突。但他也承认，左派内部有许多人在回应中变得更具激进性，这种转变源于情绪反应，随着时间推移或许会逐步缓和。 在特拉维夫持续举行的反政府抗议活动中，其他人则展现了情感复杂性。Talia Keinan和Gai Sherf在哀悼在袭击中遇难的朋友并担忧亲人在加沙被俘后，描述了许多左翼以色列人变得更加防御和爱国，将自卫与复仇的界限变得模糊。他们都对当前氛围的发展表示担忧。 Dennis在东耶路撒冷的一家咖啡馆表示，很多极左的人表达出不同寻常的情绪或民族主义观点，但他选择不参与政治争论。虽然他本人也深受袭击影响并希望哈马斯消失，但他并不支持大规模地面攻势，而是希望摆脱这种高压政治氛围。 持更偏右翼观点的顾问Nadav Hakham表示，在存在感受到存亡威胁的情况下，以色列人表现出更大的团结。他注意到，曾经的左翼朋友现在积极参与亲以色列活动，并对全球对以色列反应的批评感到失望。 在以色列北部的一场巴以团结活动上，基布兹出身的摄影师Aldema讲述了暴力事件给以左翼甚至亲巴勒斯坦社区带来的深刻创伤。尽管仍然支持和平，但他现在认为，左派在近期事件后必须对军事行动的需要更为现实。 如B’tselem的Roee Aloni和Hadash联盟的Ofer Cassif等活动人士和领导人表示，现在判断长期政治影响还为时过早，因为大家的情绪仍然很激烈。历史上，冲突常令以色列左翼右倾，如今也有一些人发表右翼观点。还有人对国际左派对哈马斯行动反应感到失望。激烈的氛围让对巴勒斯坦持同情态度者更易受批评，Cassif本人因批评政府政策被暂停议员资格，但他相信左翼的反对声音最终会恢复。 政府对人质处理方式引发的不满与反内塔尼亚胡抗议交织，有时导致主张团结和要求问责之间的激烈对峙。有些人，如Rey Kanterewicz，认为此时应把重心放在人质家属身上而非政治争端；但也有人，如Gideon Avaltal Eppstein，继续在公众强烈反对下抗议政府决定。 在国家创伤面前，政治界限模糊，许多以色列人——至少在目前——选择搁置政治，优先支持受冲突影响最深的人群。

On Thursday, the Special Cell of Delhi Police dismantled an international drug cartel comprising three individuals—Paul Joy from Sierra Leone and Peace Ilobe and Stephen from Nigeria—who allegedly distributed banned substances throughout India. According to The Statesman, authorities seized 6kg of the hypnotic drug methaqualone and 2kg of heroin from the suspects.

Acting on a tipoff, a police team conducted a swift raid near Shiv Murti, Rangpuri, resulting in the arrest of Paul Joy and Peace Ilobe. Interrogation revealed that Stephen had supplied the methaqualone. He was apprehended later in Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar.

Investigations indicated that the three suspects had been involved in drug trafficking for two years while residing in India without valid legal documentation. They face charges including drug trafficking, cheating, impersonation, forgery, and possession of forged documents. The Delhi Police Special Cell stated that further investigations are underway.

article_content: On Tuesday, Kwara State experienced mixed responses to the nationwide strike called by the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress (TUC). Some state workers, including judiciary employees, initially reported to work and court sessions commenced in Ilorin. However, federal ministry staff, bank employees, and power distribution company workers did not report, leaving their offices locked. Commercial banks opened to customers at first but soon closed to observe the strike, causing disappointment as most ATMs were not dispensing cash. Teachers joined the strike later in the day, sending students back home. Electricity users felt the effects as the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company offices at Challenge and Baboko business centres were closed. Banners from the National Union of Electricity Employees were seen at the gates, and security staff informed people that the workers were on strike. Public transport operators in the state did not participate in the strike and continued business as usual. NLC state chairman Saheed Olayinka noted that although some workers turned up at the start of the day, they left after being informed about the strike. He added that the NLC set up a monitoring committee to ensure compliance and expects stronger enforcement, including picketing, in the following days. Efforts to reach TUC state chairman, Comrade Tunde Joseph, for comments were unsuccessful, as his phone was switched off during the period of reporting.

article_content: COPENHAGEN: What was the air like during the time of Caesar, the Prophet Mohammed, or Christopher Columbus? A giant freezer in Copenhagen holds the answers, storing blocks of ice that contain records of the atmosphere dating back thousands of years. The Ice Core Archive, mainly housing 25 kilometers (15 miles) of ice collected from Greenland, helps scientists study climate changes over millennia. According to glaciology professor Jorgen Peder Steffensen from the University of Copenhagen, this archive preserves a record of prehistoric climate change and human activity from the past 10,000 years. Steffensen, who has been passionate about ice cores for 43 years, met his wife Dorthe Dahl-Jensen – also a leading paleoclimatologist – while drilling into Greenland’s ice sheet. Since 1991, Steffensen has managed one of the world’s largest repositories of ice cores, storing 40,000 blocks of ice in large boxes stacked on long shelves. Unlike frozen water, these samples are made from compressed snow. The tiny air bubbles trapped within are the same age as the surrounding ice, providing snapshots of ancient atmospheres. Scientists examine the samples in an antechamber kept at -18°C (-0.4°F), much warmer than the main storage room’s -30°C (-22°F). Here, Steffensen holds up a block of ice containing bubbles visible to the naked eye, explaining that it might have fallen as snow during the year zero. Jokingly, he notes, 'We have the real Christmas snow,' wearing a warm winter hat with furry ear flaps. The first ice cores arrived in Denmark in the 1960s from Camp Century, a secret US military base in Greenland. Recently, scientists drilled to the bedrock in eastern Greenland at a depth of 2.6 kilometers, obtaining ice samples around 120,000 years old, dating to a warmer interglacial period when Greenland’s temperatures were 5°C higher than today. Steffensen notes, 'The globe has been much warmer before — but humans weren’t there yet.' These newly acquired ice cores will help researchers better understand factors contributing to rising sea levels, including the role of fast-moving ice streams. Steffensen hopes their work will allow more accurate sea level rise predictions for the next century, reducing the margin of error from today's 70 centimeters to 15 centimeters. Ice cores are the only way scientists can determine the pre-industrial atmosphere before man-made pollution. With this research, greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane have been tracked over long periods, highlighting the impact of fossil fuel burning in modern times. Parallel to this work, the Ice Memory foundation has collected ice cores from 20 sites around the world. They aim to store these samples in Antarctica’s Concordia research station, where the average annual temperature of -55°C (-67°F) provides excellent long-term preservation. Jerome Chappellaz, head of the foundation, praises Greenland’s efforts but warns of dangers like technical failures, funding issues, and unforeseen events, referencing an incident in 2017 when a freezer failure at the University of Alberta, Canada, damaged irreplaceable samples. Chappellaz appeals to Danish researchers to join the Concordia project, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding these 'treasures' as part of humanity’s world heritage.
translated_content: 哥本哈根：你是否好奇凯撒大帝、穆罕默德先知或哥伦布时代的空气是什么味道？哥本哈根一个巨大的冷冻库给出了答案，这里保存着能够追溯几千年大气历史的冰块。冰芯档案馆主要收藏了来自格陵兰的25公里（15英里）长的冰芯，为科学家研究气候变迁提供了宝贵资源。 哥本哈根大学的冰川学教授约根·皮德·斯特芬森表示，这个档案馆保存了过去一万年来史前气候变化和人类活动的纪录。斯特芬森已经从事实地冰芯研究43年，并在钻探格陵兰冰盖时结识了同为古气候学专家的妻子多尔特·达尔-延森。 自1991年以来，斯特芬森管理着世界最大的冰芯库之一，存有4万块冰芯样本，被整齐地装箱堆放在长长的货架上。这些样本不是简单的冻水，而是经过雪压实形成的冰，内部小气泡与冰同龄，为我们提供了古老大气的“快照”。 科学家们会在温度为-18°C（-0.4°F）的前室分析冰芯，这比主库房的-30°C（-22°F）要温暖。在这里，斯特芬森举起一块肉眼可见气泡的冰芯，解释说这可能是公元元年冬天积下的雪。他开玩笑说：“我们拥有真正的圣诞雪。” 头上戴着毛皮冬帽。 上世纪六十年代，第一批冰芯从格陵兰的“世纪营地”秘密美军基地被带到丹麦。最近科学家们在格陵兰东部钻探到2.6公里深的基岩，获得了大约12万年前的冰芯，那时格陵兰的温度比现在高5°C。斯特芬森说：“地球以前确实比现在更热，但那时还没有人类。” 这些新冰芯将帮助研究者更好地了解导致海平面上升的不同因素，包括快速移动正在融化的冰流。斯特芬森希望他们的工作能帮助提升未来百年海平面上升预测的准确度，将误差从现在的70厘米降至15厘米。 冰芯是科学家确定工业革命前大气状况的唯一手段。借助这些样品，科学家可以追踪二氧化碳、甲烷等温室气体的变化，直观展示现代化石燃料燃烧带来的影响。 像“冰记忆”基金会，也从全球20个站点收集冰芯，准备用南极 Concordia 研究站零下55°C（-67°F）的独特环境长期保存。该基金会负责人杰罗姆·沙佩拉兹肯定了格陵兰的工作，同时也提醒样本面临技术故障、资金风险和不可预见事件的威胁。2017年加拿大阿尔伯塔大学一台冰柜损坏，导致大量珍贵样本受损。 沙佩拉兹呼吁丹麦研究人员加入 Concordia 项目，强调这些“珍宝”应该成为全人类的世界遗产。

article_content: A mother whose son and his partner died in the Luxor balloon disaster described the couple as 'wonderfully creative and sensitive individuals.' Joe Bampton, 40, and his girlfriend Suzanna Gyetvai, 34, were among 19 tourists killed when their hot air balloon caught fire and crashed over Luxor, Egypt, on Tuesday. Maureen Bampton, Joe's mother, paid tribute to the couple, who died alongside fellow Briton Yvonne Rennie, 48. She said, 'Joe and Zsi were wonderfully creative and sensitive individuals who lived life to the fullest and enjoyed spending time in Clapham Common with their dog Ollie.' Joe worked at Lots Road Auctions in Chelsea as a valuer and cataloguer for rugs and carpets since graduating from the Slade School of Art in the mid-1990s. Zsi met Joe at Lots Road Auctions after graduating from Kingston College of Art. She exhibited her silk screen prints and etchings under the name Zsi Chimera, with her latest exhibition at the Smokehouse Gallery in Hackney. Maureen added that both would be deeply missed by their families, colleagues, and many friends. Michael Rennie, husband of Yvonne, survived by jumping from the burning basket but was forced to watch as his wife fell to her death. He issued a statement: 'Yvonne was my rock, my friend, my shoulder to cry on. She was my world. My heartfelt condolences go out to the other families who lost loved ones in this terrible disaster.' He is currently being treated in Cairo for burns. The Egyptian pilot, named Momen Morad (also referred to as Moaman Abdo), whose clothes caught fire, also jumped and was the only other survivor. Mr. Rennie reportedly ran 250 yards after the balloon, calling for his wife as the balloon rose rapidly and exploded at around 1,000 feet above Luxor. Yvonne's father, Michael Harris, described Mr. Rennie as distraught and said he broke down during their conversation. He believed Yvonne, who enjoyed adventure, persuaded Michael to take the balloon ride. As the investigation continues, Egypt's Civil Aviation Minister revealed that the pilot jumped without shutting off the gas valve, which contributed to the disaster. Tour operator Thomas Cook defended its arrangements, asserting that all local companies, including Sky Cruises, were fully licensed by Egypt's aviation authority, and that Sky Cruises had been verified and approved. However, local balloon operators accused Bright Sky Travel, the ground agent, of cost-cutting that may have affected safety. Ala Mahmoud, head of Magic Horizon, criticized the financial arrangements between Thomas Cook and Bright Sky. The same balloon experienced a near-miss incident in October 2011 when it nearly hit a hotel roof and landed in the Nile, but no major injuries occurred. This week's tragedy reportedly happened after a landing rope became entangled with a gas tube, severing it and causing a fire. Witnesses described the pilot and British survivor jumping out before the balloon rose to about 70 meters; several passengers then fell as the fire intensified. Egyptian authorities are investigating the cause of the accident and have suspended all balloon flights in Luxor. Ahmed Mohamed Al Yemeni, Luxor's deputy public prosecutor, reported that a technical malfunction of a gas canister is being considered. The tragedy has deeply affected the victims' families and colleagues. Yvonne Rennie worked in the radiology department at Perth Royal Infirmary, where colleagues described her as much loved. In total, at least 19 foreign tourists died. At the crash site, investigators examined the remains of the burned balloon basket, and the investigation is ongoing.
translated_content: 一位母亲形容在卢克索热气球事故中去世的儿子和其伴侣为“极具创造力和感性的人”。40岁的乔·班普顿和34岁的女友苏珊娜·盖特维是周二在埃及卢克索热气球起火并坠毁造成19名游客遇难者之一。 乔的母亲莫琳·班普顿悼念了两人，他们与另一位英国人伊冯·雷尼（48岁）一同遇难。她说：“乔和兹西都是极富创造力和感性的，他们充实地生活，喜欢和狗狗Ollie一起在Clapham Common散步。” 乔自1990年代中期毕业于斯莱德艺术学院后，一直在切尔西的Lots Road Auctions担任地毯和挂毯鉴定与编目。兹西毕业于金斯顿艺术学院后，在Lots Road Auctions认识了乔。她以Zsi Chimera之名展出丝网印和蚀刻作品，最近一次展览于哈克尼的Smokehouse画廊举行。 莫琳补充说，两人将被家人、同事和众多朋友深切怀念。 伊冯的丈夫迈克尔·雷尼跳下燃烧的吊篮幸存，却不得不目睹妻子坠亡。他表示：“伊冯是我的支柱、朋友，也是我倾诉的对象，她就是我的全部。对于在这场灾难中失去亲人的家庭，我深表哀悼。”他目前正在开罗接受烧伤治疗。 埃及飞行员穆蒙·莫拉德（又称穆阿曼·阿卜杜）衣服起火后也跳下，是唯一另一位幸存者。据报道，雷尼先生追着气球跑了250码，呼喊妻子的名字，热气球迅速升到卢克索约300米高空后爆炸。 伊冯的父亲迈克尔·哈里斯称雷尼先生十分悲痛，两人通话时泣不成声。他认为喜欢冒险的伊冯劝说迈克尔参加了这次热气球之旅。 埃及民航部长透露，飞行员跳伞时未关闭燃烧器气阀，可能导致事故，调查仍在进行。 旅行社托马斯·库克为其安排进行辩护，称所有当地公司（包括Sky Cruises）均已获得埃及民航局许可和认证。 而部分当地热气球公司则指责Bright Sky Travel在地接方面为降成本而影响安全。Magic Horizon负责人阿拉·马哈茂德批评托马斯·库克与Bright Sky的价格安排。 同一只热气球在2011年10月也曾险些出事，几乎撞上酒店屋顶后落入尼罗河，所幸无重大伤亡。 据报本次惨剧发生于着陆绳绕住气罐并被切断后引发火灾。目击者称，飞行员与英国幸存者在气球升至约70米时跳下，随后火势加剧，几位乘客也坠落。 埃及当局正对事故进行调查，目前已暂停卢克索所有热气球飞行。卢克索副检察官艾哈迈德·穆罕默德·叶梅尼称，事故或与气罐技术故障有关。 这场悲剧对遇难者家属和同事造成了巨大影响。伊冯·雷尼曾在珀斯皇家医院放射科工作，是备受同事尊敬的成员。 该事故共造成至少19名外国游客遇难。事故现场调查人员检查了烧毁的气球吊篮残骸，调查仍在持续。

The IRS has informed Microsoft that it owes nearly $29 billion in back taxes, putting a spotlight on the tax practices of major technology companies. The case focuses on whether Microsoft moved profits through a factory in Puerto Rico, where software CDs were produced, by selling intellectual property to this subsidiary. Under a Puerto Rican tax arrangement, these profits were taxed at nearly 0%, a practice the IRS considers a form of tax avoidance since it bypassed standard U.S. taxes. 

This $28.9 billion assessment follows a lengthy audit of Microsoft’s taxes from 2004 to 2013. Microsoft expects further appeals and discussions to determine the final amount owed. The company maintains that it disagrees with the IRS's proposed adjustments, noting that taxes paid under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act could reduce the bill by as much as $10 billion. 

Daniel Goff, Microsoft’s corporate vice president for worldwide tax and customs, stated in a blog post: “We believe we have always followed the IRS' rules and paid the taxes we owe in the U.S. and around the world. Microsoft historically has been one of the top U.S. corporate income taxpayers. Since 2004, we have paid over $67 billion in taxes to the U.S.”

Microsoft is not alone in these practices. Accurately measuring the prevalence of profit shifting — moving revenue to lower-tax regions — is challenging, but according to Yale law professor and former Treasury official Natasha Sarin, the IRS is signaling that such practices are widespread, particularly among major U.S. corporations. Sarin explains that efforts to narrow the gap between taxes paid and taxes owed are crucial, as large corporations have advantages in minimizing taxes. 

Research from Ludvig Wier of the Danish Ministry of Finance and Gabriel Zucman of UC Berkeley found that the proportion of corporate profits reported in countries without company headquarters has quadrupled since 1975. For example, foreign firms have registered 16 times more profits in Puerto Rico than the wages they pay employees there. In 2019 alone, an estimated $969 billion in profits globally, and $165 billion in the U.S., were shifted to tax havens, resulting in a 16% loss of U.S. corporate tax revenue.

Sarin argues that these tax advantages for large corporations undermine fairness in the economy. She estimates the corporate tax gap — the difference between what corporations owe and what they actually pay — at around $40 billion annually. Sarin notes that distinguishing between tax avoidance and tax evasion is difficult until enforcement efforts increase, which has begun under the Inflation Reduction Act, allocating more resources to the IRS for enforcement.

According to Sarin, improved tax administration is key to addressing these inequities. She concludes that the solution is adequately resourcing tax authorities to ensure major corporations are held accountable.

美国国税局（IRS）已告知微软，要求其补缴近290亿美元税款，这一消息让大型科技公司的税务问题受到更多关注。本案核心在于微软是否通过波多黎各一家工厂（该厂生产微软软件光盘），通过将知识产权出售给该子公司，将利润转移到税率几乎为零的地区。国税局认为，这种做法属于避税行为，规避了美国本土的正常税收。

这项289亿美元的追缴要求源于对微软2004年至2013年税务状况的多年审计。微软预计未来还将继续上诉，并协商最终应付金额。微软坚持反对国税局的调整方案，并指出2017年《减税与就业法案》下已缴纳的税款可能使最终账单减少约100亿美元。

微软全球税务与海关企业副总裁丹尼尔·高夫（Daniel Goff）在博客中表示：“我们一直遵守国税局的规定，按照美国及全球的要求依法纳税。微软一直是美国公司所得税的主要纳税企业之一，自2004年以来已向美国缴纳超过670亿美元税款。”

而采取类似做法的企业并不只微软一家。尽管很难准确统计利润转移——即将收入转至低税区的行为——有多普遍，耶鲁大学法学院教授、前财政部官员纳塔莎·萨林（Natasha Sarin）指出，国税局的态度表明，这种行为在美国大型企业中十分常见。萨林表示，缩小实际纳税与应纳税额之间差距至关重要，因为大型企业更有能力将税负最小化。

丹麦财政部秘书处负责人卢德维格·维尔（Ludvig Wier）和加州大学伯克利分校经济学家加布里埃尔·苏克曼（Gabriel Zucman）的研究显示，企业在总部不在本国的情况下申报利润的比例自1975年以来已增长四倍。例如，外国公司在波多黎各申报的利润是当地工资总额的16倍。仅2019年，全球约有9690亿美元利润被转移到避税天堂，美国则为1650亿美元，导致美国公司税收损失达16%。

萨林认为，大型公司享受的税收优势削弱了经济公平。她估计，美国企业税收缺口——即应缴与实缴的差额——约为每年400亿美元。萨林指出，避税与逃税的界限并不总是清晰，只有加强执法后才能更好区分。目前，由于《通货膨胀削减法案》的资金，国税局执法力度有所提升。

萨林认为，改善税务管理是解决税收不公平的关键。她总结：“解决办法就是为税务机关提供足够资源，确保大型企业公平纳税。”

article_content: Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers has dismissed rumors about Raheem Sterling potentially leaving the club, pointing out that Sterling's talent will always attract attention from other teams. Despite a slow start to their Premier League campaign, with Liverpool currently 11th before facing Everton in the Merseyside derby, Sterling has been a bright spot, scoring three goals so far this season. Rodgers said he is comfortable with speculation about Sterling's future, noting that the 19-year-old and his representatives know how settled he is at Anfield, where he has three years left on his contract. There is no rush to address his contract at this time. At the pre-match press conference, Rodgers remarked, 'It shows how well he's playing. You could link him with every club in the world. I am at ease with the speculation. He and his representatives know how comfortable he is here. At some point, he will be rewarded for his performances, but there’s no rush.' Rodgers confirmed that Sterling, who is 'super-fit,' will play against Everton after getting a rest against Aston Villa. Liverpool heads into the Everton match following back-to-back league defeats to Aston Villa and West Ham. In last season's corresponding fixture, Liverpool beat Everton 4-0, with two goals from Daniel Sturridge and goals from Steven Gerrard and Luis Suarez. Mario Balotelli, who joined the club from AC Milan for £16 million in August, seems to have settled in well and is looking forward to adding to his goal tally against Everton. Goalkeeper Simon Mignolet, along with teammates like Martin Skrtel, Suso, and Fabio Borini, have been preparing for the derby, with some light-hearted moments observed in training. Rodgers cautioned against expecting a repeat of last season's emphatic result, given the number of new players in the squad this year. He also revealed that Daniel Sturridge, who has recently been out with a thigh injury, could return, praising his speed and movement. However, he said they will not rush Sturridge's comeback. Rodgers praised Everton manager Roberto Martinez and acknowledged the special atmosphere of the Merseyside derby, emphasizing the team's efforts to maintain the principles that brought success in the previous 18 months, despite integrating many new players. He dismissed the idea that Champions League commitments are responsible for Liverpool's poor league results, noting the difference in points from the same fixtures last season is minimal. Rodgers expressed confidence that Liverpool will improve as the squad returns to full strength after the next international break. Philippe Coutinho is expected to play a leading role in attack, while captain Steven Gerrard could partner Joe Allen in midfield as Liverpool aims to improve their league position.

article_content: A leading NHS executive, Professor Sir Roger Boyle, has said he would not want his own child to be treated at the Leeds General Infirmary's children's heart surgery unit, citing worries about its safety standards. His remarks came after the unit reopened following a temporary shutdown based on data—leaked by Boyle—that suggested its mortality rates were potentially double the national average. Sir Roger, currently in charge of NHS death rate monitoring and formerly national director for heart disease, described care at Leeds as 'on the edge of acceptability.' He remarked that if his ten-year-old daughter needed heart surgery, he would choose another hospital, such as Newcastle. Parents and supporters of the Leeds unit were alarmed, accusing Boyle of holding a personal vendetta. The center’s surgical services were suspended briefly after disclosed data indicated above-average death rates, a concern echoed by some external surgeons. Nevertheless, opponents of the closure claimed it was politically charged, since it happened just after a High Court reversal of plans to shut the facility as part of a national streamlining effort. Leeds hospital officials maintained that the data in question was incomplete and insisted a comprehensive review confirmed the unit's safety. Surgery has since resumed, and NHS England stated that immediate risks have been addressed. Still, Boyle’s comments on BBC radio revived the controversy, as he pressed for ongoing supervision, noting the unit's performance was just within acceptable limits. A representative from Leeds Teaching Hospitals highlighted that independent reviews had confirmed the heart unit's safety, which was reaffirmed by NHS England's deputy medical director. The Save Our Surgery (SOS) campaign group and Leeds MP Greg Mulholland have called for Boyle’s removal, saying his statements distressed families and hurt the hospital’s reputation. NHS medical director Sir Bruce Keogh, who initially suspended the unit’s surgery, later disagreed with Boyle, confirming he would be content for his own child to have surgery in Leeds. This dispute arises as the NHS reshapes children’s heart services, proposing closures of several smaller centers, including Leeds—a move that would make local patients travel considerable distances for treatment. Nearly 600,000 people signed a petition opposing these changes. Recently, Justice Mrs Justice Davies ruled the NHS process for deciding closures was unfair due to secrecy around expert panel scoring. Nonetheless, officials closed the Leeds unit temporarily after new data highlighted elevated death rates. Disagreements between NHS leaders mean families and patients face continued uncertainty.

The Google Pixel 8 Pro is an outstanding smartphone, arguably the best Pixel Google has ever released and one of the top Android phones of 2023. In my review last October, I praised it as the best Pixel I’ve ever used—a bold statement, but after over a month of daily use, it still holds true.

The Pixel 8 Pro's design continues to impress, especially the more rounded shape, which greatly enhances comfort in hand. Even with the notable design improvements to the iPhone 15 Pro Max, I prefer the feel of the Pixel 8 Pro, especially with its striking Bay blue color. The only downside so far is that the stainless steel frame around the camera lenses has gathered some small, cosmetic scratches, echoing a similar issue seen on last year's Pixel 7 Pro. Switching to a material like titanium could be a welcome change in future models.

The camera setup on the Pixel 8 Pro is excellent, living up to Google’s reputation for outstanding smartphone photography. The phone consistently delivers impressive shots in various environments, from dimly-lit concert halls to nature trails. Video performance is equally strong, with smooth stabilization, vibrant colors, and crisp details. The camera’s quality has even prompted me to move my cloud photo library from Apple Photos to Google Photos to continue using the Pixel 8 Pro as my primary camera.

Beyond design and cameras, the 6.7-inch OLED display stands out for its vibrant, punchy colors and smooth 120Hz refresh rate. The slightly curved edges add to the premium feel. Android 14 on the Pixel 8 Pro is fast and enjoyable, offering customizable lock screens and innovative features like the AI wallpaper generator. Other hardware aspects, such as the reliable in-display fingerprint sensor, Face Unlock for app logins, responsive buttons, and clear speakers, contribute to an overall great user experience.

Performance-wise, the new Tensor G3 chip marks a substantial improvement over previous Pixels. Earlier Pixel models suffered from issues like overheating and poor efficiency, but the Pixel 8 Pro runs swiftly and remains cool, even during heavy multitasking or gaming sessions. While the phone can get warm with extensive gaming, this is common across smartphones.

Unlike the Pixel 7 Pro, which was plagued by bugs and performance problems, the Pixel 8 Pro has been nearly flawless so far. Over the past month, I’ve had no issues with app crashes or UI glitches. Only once did the always-on display stop working, which was quickly fixed through the settings.

However, two areas need improvement: battery life and charging speed. While the Pixel 8 Pro can last a full day with normal use, it doesn’t match the battery longevity of competitors like the Motorola Edge Plus or OnePlus 11, which can go two days between charges. Charging is also slower than some rivals, taking up to an hour and a half to reach 100%. This might not matter to those who charge overnight, but it’s less ideal for quick top-ups.

Overall, my first month with the Pixel 8 Pro has been a dramatic improvement over previous generations. While some reservations remain given the Pixel line’s history, the 8 Pro’s performance and reliability are winning me over. If the phone maintains its current quality, I expect it to remain my daily driver well into 2024.

article_content: During a Veterans Day address on Saturday, former President Donald Trump referred to his political opponents as 'vermin' and suggested they represent a more significant threat to the United States than countries such as Russia, China, or North Korea. This language quickly drew comparisons to rhetoric used by past dictators like Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini. In response, The Lincoln Project released a video comparing Trump's remarks to those of authoritarian figures, while Meidas Touch shared a list of similar statements from both Trump and Hitler, highlighting the parallels. Ammar Moussa, spokesperson for the Biden-Harris campaign, sharply criticized Trump's comments, arguing that, rather than honoring veterans, Trump echoed the language of leaders whom American soldiers fought to defeat, and accused him of disregarding the sacrifices of the military and American democratic principles. Trump, for his part, reiterated on Truth Social his intention to remove elements he labeled as Communists, Marxists, Fascists, and Radical Left figures, referring to them as 'vermin' inside the country. He argued that internal threats surpass external ones in danger, and reaffirmed his commitment to 'Make America Great Again,' despite objections from his opponents.

Pat Rogers, a leader in the Republican National Committee (RNC), is facing calls to resign after sending an email containing remarks that many have deemed offensive to Native Americans. Rogers criticized New Mexico Governor Susana Martinez for meeting with Native American leaders and accused her of dishonoring the memory of General George Armstrong Custer, a controversial figure known for his involvement in the Indian Wars and his death at the Battle of Little Bighorn in 1876.

In his June 8 email to members of Governor Martinez’s staff, Rogers wrote, “The state is going to hell,” and suggested that Allen Weh, a former Republican candidate who lost to Martinez in 2010, would not have disrespected Custer in this way. The email was obtained by Independent Source PAC and released by ProgressNow New Mexico, a liberal advocacy group, which has called for Rogers to step down. Pat Davis, executive director of ProgressNow New Mexico, condemned the comments as “blatantly racist and indefensible.”

The controversy comes as Rogers attends the Republican National Convention in Tampa, Florida, which was postponed by a day due to Tropical Storm Isaac. Governor Martinez is scheduled to speak at the convention, following Condoleezza Rice and before vice presidential nominee Paul Ryan.

State law requires Governor Martinez to meet annually with tribal leaders at a state-tribal summit. ProgressNow New Mexico has posted an online tool for the public to contact RNC leaders and Rogers’ law firm, Modrall Sperling, to call for his removal.

Rogers has previously faced criticism for his use of personal email accounts to conduct government business, which led to his resignation from the board of the New Mexico Foundation for Open Government in July. He was appointed to the RNC executive committee by former Chairman Michael Steele, who also drew backlash in 2010 for using racially insensitive language. Neither Rogers nor the RNC responded to requests for comment.

article_content: Karnataka secured a 52-run victory over Uttarakhand in the Vijay Hazare Trophy in Ahmedabad on Saturday, marking their second straight win. Devdutt Padikkal top-scored with an impressive 117 off 122 balls (13 fours, 5 sixes), while V Koushik's four-wicket haul played a crucial role. After being asked to bat first, Karnataka lost captain Mayank Agarwal in the opening over. Padikkal and SJ Nikin Jose (72 off 82 balls, 3 fours, 3 sixes) put together a key 131-run partnership for the third wicket after the fall of R Samarth. Manish Pandey added a quickfire 56, with four boundaries and three sixes, helping Karnataka post 284/7 in 50 overs. Uttarakhand’s batting order struggled to find momentum. Jiwanjot Singh (46) and D Negi (21) made starts but could not convert them into big scores. Kunal Chandela's determined 98 was not enough, as Uttarakhand finished at 232/9 in their 50 overs. Brief scores: Karnataka: 284/7 in 50 overs (Devdutt Padikkal 117, SJ Nikin Jose 72, Manish Pandey 56; Agrim Tiwari 3-45, Rajan 2-71) beat Uttarakhand: 232/9 in 50 overs (Jiwanjot Singh 46, Kunal Chandela 98; V Koushik 4-30, Vidwath Kaverappa 2-51). Other matches: Mizoram: 128 all out in 42.1 overs (Jehu Anderson 38; Divij Mehra 2-20, Suyash Sharma 4-25) lost to Delhi: 131/2 in 16.5 overs (Anuj Rawat 28, Himmat Singh 52 not out, Ayush Badoni 45 not out; KC Cariappa 2-41). Bihar: 112 all out in 30.4 overs (Pratap 46 not out; HV Patel 4-49, Anshul Kamboj 2-17, SP Kumar 3-25) lost to Haryana: 117/0 in 19.1 overs (Yuvraj Singh 50 not out, Ankit Kumar 61 not out). J&K: 138 all out in 37.4 overs (Henan Nazir 23, Abdul Samad 40, Lone Nasir 27; Sandeep Sharma 2-9, Rajangad Bawa 4-25) lost to Chandigarh: 142/2 in 25.1 overs (Arslan Khan 76 not out, Gaurav Puri 34 not out). Recent related articles: Rajasthan Royals have traded Devdutt Padikkal to Lucknow Super Giants in exchange for fast bowler Avesh Khan ahead of IPL 2024. Delhi Capitals have released Sarfaraz Khan and Manish Pandey, creating a Rs 2.6 crore purse for the upcoming IPL auction. In Karnataka politics, former BJP MLA Aravind Limbavali has raised concerns about the appointment of BY Vijayendra as state BJP president and R Ashoka as leader of the opposition, alleging 'adjustment politics' over merit. Limbavali, a Dalit community leader in the BJP, questioned Vijayendra’s qualifications and suggested the appointments aim to boost seats in the Lok Sabha elections. In Bihar, two people died and two others were injured after being hit by a car owned by the Madhepura district magistrate in the Phulparas area of Madhubani district on National Highway 57. The car collided with a railing after hitting the victims. Eyewitnesses claimed the vehicle was speeding and swerved to avoid people. Local residents protested and blocked the road, later reopened. Authorities plan to file an FIR and pursue action.

A small mixed-breed dog named Foxy is being praised as a hero after alerting her family to a house fire in Santa Ana, California. Vera Mendez, 52, said her two-year-old pup began barking loudly around 2 a.m. on Wednesday as smoke entered the home. Thanks to Foxy's warning, Mendez’s son was able to wake up the rest of the family and ensure everyone evacuated safely.

The family of eight—seven adults and a nine-year-old boy, spanning three generations—managed to escape without serious injury. Only one man suffered minor smoke inhalation, but he did not need to be hospitalized. "By the time I woke up, almost three rooms were involved. We were lucky we got out. All of us barely escaped," Mendez recounted to City News Service.

Nearly 50 firefighters responded to the fire at 1200 South Garnsey Street, managing to control it within about 30 minutes. However, the house was destroyed, with officials estimating $200,000 in structural damage and an additional $100,000 in lost contents. The American Red Cross is providing assistance to the family with temporary accommodation, while the cause of the fire remains under investigation. Mendez was seen affectionately comforting Foxy at the scene during clean-up efforts.

这个三代同堂的家庭共八人——七位成人和一名九岁男孩——都没有受到严重伤害。只有一名男子吸入了少量烟雾，但不需要住院治疗。Mendez向City News Service回忆道：“我醒来时，房子里已有三个房间着火了。我们真的很幸运能逃出来，大家都是勉强逃脱。”

article_content: By Stephanie Linning. Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it's Superman — or rather, two Supermen — pulled over in a customized super car while driving down the M42 near Solihull, West Midlands. Officers from the Central Motorway Policing Group, consisting of staff from West Midlands, West Mercia, and Staffordshire police forces, stopped the vehicle on suspicion of driving without insurance. The car was missing its rear window, which had been replaced by a piece of red fabric tied across the opening — adding a superhero touch as the fabric fluttered like Superman's cape in the wind. The two men, both dressed in matching Superman costumes complete with the iconic 'S' logo on their chests, stood next to their customized car after being stopped. Central Motorway Police Group tweeted after the stop on Saturday night: 'Even Superman needs insurance. We don't work for Lex Luthor, but we had to remove Superman's wheels from the road.' Images of the two 'not-so superheroes' quickly spread online. The Oklahoma County Sheriff later tweeted to his West Midlands counterparts: 'Nice work! Not even Superman has a chance against police Kryptonite. He's much better at flying than driving, anyway. Stay safe.' article_content: A Spanish family who lost a memory card while on holiday in Scotland have been reunited with more than 500 photos from their trip, thanks to a Facebook campaign started by a Scottish student. Barry Carruthers, a 22-year-old drama student, discovered the memory card and found it still contained hundreds of pictures from the family's visit to various Scottish landmarks. Carruthers selected several images and posted them on Facebook, showing the family's adventures at famous locations across Scotland, hoping that someone would recognize them. The family of four, from Barcelona, lost their camera during their travels in Scotland. The appeal quickly gained traction online, spreading from Shetland to Hong Kong. People even contacted American talk-show host Ellen DeGeneres via Twitter to help spread the word. Carruthers said: 'This family had seen everything, from the Military Tattoo at Edinburgh Castle to the Fringe, the Royal Mile, Knockhill Circuit, and Ayr.' The student posted the photos online in an attempt to find the family, and the campaign soon went viral. Carruthers noted that he had lived in Scotland his whole life and that some places in the photos were unfamiliar even to him. After reviewing the family's extensive trip through Scotland, Carruthers felt compelled to help return the lost pictures. The pictures appeared to show a family of four—two parents, a son, and a daughter—from Barcelona. Spanish media confirmed the family had contacted Carruthers to claim their photos. Carruthers found over 500 remarkable photos on the family's memory card, documenting their travels. Eventually, the manager of the Ibis hotel in Edinburgh where the family stayed reached out to Barry to offer help. The son then directly contacted Carruthers to arrange for the memory card’s return. The Spanish newspaper La Vanguardia reported the family's identification was aided by details in the photos, such as a reference to a Catalan beer brand and an image next to a car driven by Barcelona pilot Pepe Massot. These clues helped the Ibis hotel manager confirm the family's identity and contact Barry. Carruthers said: 'I have only spoken with the son, who studies in Barcelona. He said they are from Catalonia and he was completely shocked.' 'The manager, Jamie, contacted the mother after seeing the photos on Facebook, and she was delighted.' The family had apparently lost their camera, and someone may have discarded the memory card, which was later found by the student near a multi-storey car park in Glasgow.

Jaycee Chan, the 32-year-old son of martial arts icon Jackie Chan, has been officially charged with a drug offense in China that could lead to a prison sentence of up to three years. According to a statement from the Supreme People’s Procuratorate shared on Sina Weibo, Jaycee is being prosecuted for 'sheltering others to use drugs.'

Jaycee, a Hong Kong native, and Taiwanese actor Kai Ko, age 23, were apprehended in August during a police raid in the Dongcheng district of Beijing. Authorities reportedly found more than 100 grams of marijuana in Jaycee’s apartment after both men tested positive for cannabis use. Ko was released after serving 14 days in administrative detention, but Jaycee has been held in custody since his arrest.

Beijing’s intensified war on drugs has resulted in the detention of more than 7,000 people over the past year—a 72% increase according to China Daily. High-profile celebrities have been a focus of the crackdown, with recent cases involving actor Zhang Mo and singer Li Daimo, the latter of whom was sentenced to nine months in jail for hosting a drug party.

In an effort to clean up the entertainment industry, dozens of talent agencies in Beijing have agreed to terminate contracts with artists implicated in drug offenses and to enforce industry-wide drug bans.

Jackie Chan addressed his son’s arrest by expressing his anger and disappointment on Sina Weibo, taking some responsibility as a parent and urging young people to steer clear of drugs. Jackie Chan, who was named China’s anti-drug ambassador in 2009, has been vocal in supporting drug prevention efforts.

The article concludes by briefly noting that Indio Downey, the son of actor Robert Downey Jr., faces a similar felony drug charge in another case.

成龙在微博上就儿子被捕事件公开表示愤怒和自责，坦言作为父亲未尽到责任，并呼吁年轻人引以为戒，远离毒品。成龙自2009年起担任中国禁毒形象大使，并积极宣传禁毒。

article_content: James Gibbon, 62, the former head of finance at Benenden Healthcare Society, has been sentenced to six years in prison for embezzling more than £1.2 million to fund a lavish lifestyle including private school fees for his children, a BMW for his wife, luxury holidays, property investments, and over £667,000 in credit card spending. Gibbon began working at Benenden Healthcare just six months after being released from a four-year sentence for a previous £300,000 fraud at a road construction company. Benenden Healthcare expressed deep disappointment at the significant breach of trust, emphasizing that the crime affected its 900,000 members and violated the organization's values. Prosecutor Andrew Haslam told York Crown Court that Gibbon had been declared bankrupt so none of the stolen money could be recovered. Recorder Simon Myerson QC described the case as a grave breach of trust, highlighting that the funds belonged to the members who relied on the society, and that Gibbon used the money for his own benefit. Gibbon, from York, pleaded guilty to stealing £1,207,417 from Benenden Healthcare Society between January 2003 and April 2012. He earned between £48,000 and £55,000 per year during his tenure from March 1998 to April 2012 and had control over the society’s corporate accounts, which he exploited for personal use, including forging cheques. Gibbon falsified internal records to cover his theft and was eventually discovered after an internal audit exposed discrepancies going back to 2006. He was dismissed in 2012 following unauthorized payments to two female staff members; a subsequent audit revealed the full extent of his fraud. Defense lawyer Glenn Parsons stated that Gibbon had intended to reform after his previous prison term but ultimately took advantage of weak oversight. A Benenden spokesperson said the theft did not threaten the society’s financial stability but reduced its assets. The organization has since taken steps to strengthen internal controls. The spokesperson did not disclose whether Benenden was aware of Gibbon’s previous conviction when hiring him.

article_content: The outbreak of fighting in Iraq's Anbar Province has sparked renewed concern and debate in U.S. foreign policy circles. Prominent conservative voices, including Senators John McCain and Lindsey Graham, have criticized the Obama administration's policy on Iraq, asserting that its inaction allowed al Qaeda to regain ground, with the group's flag now flying over parts of Falluja and Ramadi—two cities secured at significant cost during the Bush administration. Critics argue that if President Obama had not withdrawn the remaining U.S. troops at the end of 2011, Washington would have more leverage to prevent the present turmoil. However, important context is often overlooked. It was President Bush, not Obama, who negotiated the original withdrawal agreement with Iraqi Prime Minister Nuri al-Maliki, requiring all U.S. forces to leave by the end of 2011. The Obama administration faced the choice of either breaking this agreement, thus undermining the sovereignty of a democratic Iraq, or persuading the al-Maliki government to accept a new arrangement. Administration officials did attempt to broker a new 'status of forces' agreement to retain some U.S. troops, but al-Maliki insisted that any remaining personnel would be subject to Iraqi law. Given longstanding U.S. reluctance to accept such terms—especially in countries with less stable legal systems—the request was declined. It's important to consider whether subjecting American service members to Iraq's legal system would have been advisable. If not, then refusing the concession was likely the correct decision. Moreover, U.S. troop presence had become widely unpopular with both the American and Iraqi publics by 2011. Opinion polls reflected that most Americans viewed the war as a mistake, and both Sunni and Shiite Iraqis agreed, often by large margins, that all foreign troops should depart. The main exception was the Kurdish region, which viewed a continued U.S. presence as protection against actions from Baghdad. Keeping U.S. forces in Iraq would have placed American personnel amid escalating tensions—between Baghdad and the Kurds, and between the Shiite-led government and Sunni insurgents. U.S. troops would now be involved in increasingly severe sectarian violence, as the death toll from political conflict reached a five-year high in 2013. With Kurdistan's growing autonomy and a direct Sunni challenge to central authority, Iraq is showing clear signs of instability and potential fragmentation. Critics who blame Obama for withdrawing troops often overlook these complex dynamics. The belief that the U.S. occupation was successful until later missteps is, according to the article, an oversimplification. The conclusion is that it is safer for the United States not to be re-engaged militarily in Iraq.
translated_content: 伊拉克安巴尔省爆发的战斗，引发了美国外交政策圈的新一轮关注和讨论。包括约翰·麦凯恩与林赛·格雷厄姆在内的知名保守派人士批评奥巴马政府的伊拉克政策，认为其不作为让基地组织重新崛起，如今该组织的旗帜再次飘扬在费卢杰和拉马迪部分地区——这两座城市曾在布什政府时期付出巨大代价才得以收复。 一些批评者认为，如果奥巴马没有在2011年底撤出剩余美军，美国现在本可以更有效地防止伊拉克陷入动荡。然而，这一观点忽略了一些重要背景。事实上，是布什总统（而非奥巴马）与伊拉克总理马利基谈判并签署了美军必须在2011年底前全部撤离的最初协议。 奥巴马政府面临的选择是，要么违约破坏一个民主伊拉克的主权，要么说服马利基政府接受新安排。奥巴马团队曾试图通过新的“驻军地位协议”让部分美军留在伊拉克，但马利基坚持任何留驻的美军都必须遵守伊拉克法律。美国长期以来不愿接受类似条件，尤其是在法律体系不稳定的国家，因此最终拒绝了这一请求。 值得思考的是，将美军置于伊拉克法律体系下是否明智。如果答案是否定的，那当时拒绝做出让步很可能是正确决定。此外，到2011年，无论是在美国还是在伊拉克，美军的驻扎已广受反对。民调显示多数学美国人认为伊拉克战争是个错误，伊拉克的逊尼派和什叶派居民也都大多希望外国军队全部撤离。唯一的例外是库尔德地区，他们希望美军留守，以防范巴格达方面的压制。 如果继续驻军，美国士兵将被卷入不断升级的紧张局势——包括巴格达与库尔德之间的纷争，以及什叶派主导政府与逊尼派激进分子的对抗。如今如果有驻军，他们将面临更为激烈的教派冲突，因为2013年伊拉克政治暴力致死人数已创五年新高。 随着库尔德斯坦地区自治权的加强，以及逊尼派对中央政府的直接挑战，伊拉克显现出极大的不稳定甚至分裂迹象。那些批评奥巴马撤军决定的人，往往忽视了这些复杂因素。认为美军占领一度成功，而后仅因操作失误才被破坏，这种观点是过于简化的。综上，作者认为，美国不再涉足伊拉克冲突更为明智和安全。

article_content: Patrick Smith, 62, from Texas, has been charged with bigamy after his second wife contacted his first wife using his cellphone. Smith is accused of marrying Janet Mills Maun while still legally married to his wife of 34 years, Toni Marie Zimmerman, who lives in Washington. Zimmerman discovered the second marriage in November 2012 when Maun called her from Smith’s phone. It is unclear why Maun called. Zimmerman recounted, according to the Houston Chronicle: 'A woman asked for my husband. I said, 'He's at work in Texas.' She didn't answer, but said, 'Who is this?' I replied, 'This is his wife.' She responded, 'No! This is his wife!' Zimmerman then reported Smith to authorities. She also goes by the name Toni Smith and told News 92 FM she separated from her husband in 2006. She said she’s Catholic and does not believe in divorce but chose separation to avoid responsibility for her husband’s credit card debts. Smith allegedly believed legal separation allowed him to remarry, and he moved to Texas, marrying Maun in 2009. Smith was indicted by a Fort Bend Grand Jury on February 10, 2014. If convicted, he could face up to 10 years in prison, although under Texas law, an individual who 'reasonably believes they are divorced' can use that as a defense in bigamy cases. Smith’s attorney, John Venza Jr, hopes the court will dismiss the case, describing it as a family law matter rather than a criminal issue. When Smith’s second marriage ended last year, Maun was initially awarded a portion of Smith’s retirement in the settlement. However, lawyers for Zimmerman argued that Maun’s marriage to Smith was invalid, and a judge agreed, invalidating Maun’s right to Smith’s retirement benefits. Zimmerman said, 'People need to stand up for themselves and speak out because it’s a lot like identity theft and fraud.' Smith’s attorney claims Zimmerman’s actions are driven by money, while Zimmerman insists her motive is to combat bigamy. The case’s next court date is scheduled for April.

article_content: The Canadian High Commission in Nigeria has temporarily suspended its operations until further notice. This suspension appears to follow a fire incident at the High Commission on Monday. The announcement was made late Monday night via the Commission's official X (formerly Twitter) account. During this period, visa and immigration services for those seeking to visit or emigrate to Canada are unavailable. Additionally, services for Canadians residing in or visiting Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea, and Sao Tome and Principe will not be provided. The Commission stated: 'The High Commission of Canada to Nigeria, in Abuja, has temporarily suspended operations until further notice. For consular assistance, contact our 24/7 Emergency Watch and Response Centre.' Furthermore, on November 6, 2023, the Canadian government updated its travel advisory, warning citizens to avoid non-essential travel to Nigeria, including Abuja, due to unpredictable security conditions and risks such as terrorism, crime, inter-communal clashes, armed attacks, and kidnappings. This warning followed a similar travel advisory issued by the United States to its citizens on November 3, 2023. Canada specifically advised its citizens to avoid certain regions of Nigeria, including Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Sokoto, Zamfara, Plateau, Kogi, Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Yobe, and the Niger Delta states of Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bayelsa, Delta, Imo, and Rivers (except for the capital city, Port Harcourt), due to risks of terrorism, armed attacks, kidnapping, and violence. When contacted by phone, Canadian High Commission official Demilade Kosemani did not respond to calls or messages.

article_content:
House Speaker Kevin McCarthy announced he will bring Rep. Matt Gaetz’s motion to remove him as Speaker to a vote on Tuesday, confirming to reporters after a closed-door Republican meeting that the vote would take place during the day’s first series of votes, expected around 1:30 p.m. ET. McCarthy acknowledged ongoing efforts to unseat him, saying, “If I counted how many times someone wanted to knock me out, I would’ve been gone a long time ago.”

During a caucus meeting on Tuesday, Democratic leaders reportedly urged their members not to back McCarthy. This comes as Gaetz and four other Republicans have voiced their intention to remove McCarthy, primarily criticizing his handling of funding and budget negotiations, particularly the short-term deal reached over the weekend to prevent a government shutdown. 

McCarthy received a standing ovation during the GOP meeting and defended his choice to work with Democrats, expressing disappointment at having no alternative for keeping the government running. He emphasized the importance of continuing to pass individual spending bills to fund the government beyond November 17. “At the end of the day, if you throw a speaker out that has 99% of their conference that kept government open and paid the troops, I think we're in a really bad place for how we're going to run Congress,” McCarthy told reporters.

Because at least five Republicans may vote against him, McCarthy would need Democratic support to keep the Speaker’s chair—a prospect he said he was not expecting. “If five Republicans go with Democrats, then I'm out,” he noted, acknowledging that outcome was likely. ABC News also reported that McCarthy reached out to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Monday night as he worked to secure his position.

After the Democratic caucus meeting, Jeffries said, “House Democrats are going to continue to put people over politics and to fight to make life better for everyday Americans…We encourage our Republican colleagues who claim to be more traditional to break from the extremists, end the chaos, end the dysfunction, end the extremism.” He added, “We are ready, willing and able to work together with our Republican colleagues, but it is on them to join us to move the Congress and the country forward.”

Democrats remained steadfast in their opposition, with Rep. Adam Schiff stating, “Kevin McCarthy is not trustworthy. We don’t trust him. Their own conference doesn’t trust him. We’ve just lurched from crisis to crisis with him as speaker and they need to choose someone that has the ability to govern because it’s not him.” Rep. Pramila Jayapal echoed this, saying, “We’re not voting in any way that would help save Speaker McCarthy.”

The Republicans backing Gaetz’s motion are Matt Gaetz, Bob Good of Virginia, Andy Biggs of Arizona, Eli Crane of Arizona, and Tim Burchett of Tennessee. Rep. Nancy Mace of South Carolina remains undecided, expressing frustration but leaving the door open to conversation. During a GOP meeting, Rep. Carlos Gimenez confirmed widespread support for McCarthy, who received a show of hands from most present. Gaetz, however, remained resolute, saying McCarthy no longer had his support or the necessary Republican backing to continue as Speaker. He suggested McCarthy could only remain with Democratic votes, but would no longer lead because of Republican support.

Reporting by ABC's Lauren Peller, Lalee Ibssa, and Alexandra Hutzler.

报道：ABC的劳伦·佩勒、拉莉·伊布萨与亚历山德拉·胡茨勒。
