Treasury yields and inflation data are deeply connected, each influencing the other. The yield on the 10-Year Treasury Note has returned to levels seen late last week. After Tuesday’s consumer price index (CPI) showed lower-than-expected inflation, buyers came back to Treasuries, hoping this means the Federal Reserve may be finished raising rates and could soon consider cuts. Stock market enthusiasm followed, with the Nasdaq 100 rebounding to summer highs before pulling back as Treasury bond selling resumed.

For longer-term Treasuries, the 30-Year yield peaked near 5% in mid-October, then dropped as low as 4.6% after the recent CPI release, before climbing back to almost 4.7% as some investors grew cautious. The 10-Year Note followed a similar trend, approaching 5% last month and now down to 4.535%, which is typical given its shorter term compared to the 30-Year.

On the short end, the 3-month Treasury bill yield reached 5.35% in early October but now stands at 5.255%. This causes the yield curve to invert, with short-term rates higher than long-term ones, signaling uncertainty about inflation and interest rates ahead.

Bond funds like the iShares 20+ Year U.S. Treasury Bond ETF have also seen renewed interest, recently rising above the 50-day moving average but remaining below the 200-day moving average. Beyond economic data, political factors—particularly the approaching 2024 U.S. election—are adding to market unease and affecting the bond market.

article_content: Matthew Cordle, a 22-year-old from Ohio, admitted in an online video to causing a fatal wrong-way crash after drinking heavily. Despite his confession, he initially pleaded not guilty in court—a procedural move to ensure random judge assignment before he plans to plead guilty and accept responsibility for the June accident that killed Vincent Canzani, 61. Judge Julie Lynch suggested the not guilty plea was a legal tactic. Cordle faces charges of aggravated vehicular homicide and drunk driving. In his three-and-a-half-minute video, Cordle confesses, expresses remorse, and urges others not to drink and drive. The victim’s daughter criticized Cordle's public confession as an attempt to lessen his sentence, while Canzani's ex-wife supported his coming forward. Canzani was a former Navy missile technician and photographer. The confession video was created with 'Because I Said I Would,' a non-profit founded by Alex Sheen to promote personal commitments. Sheen said Cordle wanted to raise awareness of drunk driving’s consequences. The organization is also active in other causes, such as anti-sexual abuse campaigns following the Cleveland kidnappings.

Sun Africa LLC, an international organization focused on Africa’s energy sector, is committing approximately $2.2 billion to develop Nigeria’s power infrastructure. The announcement was made by Nigeria’s Minister of Power, Adebayo Adelabu, after meeting with Sun Africa’s team led by Chairman Goran Rajsic. According to the Federal Ministry of Power’s statement in Abuja on Sunday, the company will help the Nigerian government build essential energy facilities.

The project’s initial phase involves constructing 961 megawatts peak (MWp) of solar photovoltaic (PV) infrastructure and 455 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery energy storage. The ministry stated that Sun Africa and its partners will launch this transformative initiative soon.

Minister Adelabu underlined the pressing need for new power infrastructure to promote economic development and sustainability in Africa’s largest economy. All stakeholders have pledged to collaborate closely on expanding renewable energy infrastructure to meet Nigeria’s electricity needs.

Chairman Rajsic voiced enthusiasm for the project and expressed gratitude to partners who supported the design, emphasizing the use of advanced solar PV and battery storage technologies, financed through cost-effective, long-term loans under OECD principles.

Sun Africa is also collaborating with its EPC partner, Sterling & Wilson Renewable Energy Limited, which will play a crucial role in executing the project’s first phase. The ministry described this joint effort as a significant milestone in advancing sustainable and reliable energy solutions for Nigeria, reaffirming their dedication to innovation and positive change in renewable energy.

article_content: During its ongoing review of the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and the Fiscal Strategy Paper, the House of Representatives on Monday issued a 48-hour deadline to the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) to account for the whereabouts of N3 billion, as highlighted in the Auditor General for the Federation’s 2022 report. The Chairman of the Committee on Finance, who led an interactive session with several Federal Government agency heads at the National Assembly Complex, made this demand. article_content: Jesse 'LJ' Matthew, currently charged in connection with the disappearance of University of Virginia student Hannah Graham, has a history involving past serious allegations. In 2002, while studying and playing football at Liberty University, Matthew was accused by a fellow student of sexual assault. Police named him as a suspect, but he was not prosecuted due to insufficient evidence. Following the accusation, Matthew lost his football scholarship and was expelled from the university. Recently, authorities announced Matthew’s arrest in Galveston, Texas, after he fled Virginia. He has appeared in court in Texas for the charge of abduction with intent to defile, and will be extradited to Virginia for further legal proceedings. Matthew, previously recognized as a talented athlete, had received a football scholarship to Liberty after being named Charlottesville’s Athlete of the Year in 1999. His tenure at the university ended abruptly after the assault allegation, with both the school and former teammates confirming his removal from the team and expulsion. Liberty University, known as the United States’ largest private Christian university, stated that Matthew attended and played football there from 2000 to 2002, but cited student privacy laws as the reason for not disclosing additional details. After leaving Liberty, Matthew held several jobs, including driving a taxi and working as a hospital porter at UVA Hospital. He also assisted as a football coach at a local private school. Matthew previously faced other legal issues, such as a 2009 arrest for attempted larceny and assault, though those charges were dismissed, along with history of minor driving violations. The search for Hannah Graham, involving local and federal authorities, began after she was last seen with Matthew according to investigators and verified by surveillance video. Authorities are reviewing past allegations against Matthew during their investigation. Hannah Graham’s family, visibly distressed, appealed for help at a press conference, emphasizing how much she means to them. A reward of $100,000 is being offered for information leading to her discovery. As the investigation and search for Hannah Graham continue, law enforcement works to extradite Matthew back to Virginia.

article_content:
Formula One magnate Bernie Ecclestone is facing possible extradition after being indicted by a German court on bribery charges. The 82-year-old billionaire could face up to five years in prison if convicted.

Prosecutors allege Ecclestone paid £26 million to German banker Gerhard Gribkowsky to ensure that a significant stake in Formula One was sold in 2006 to Ecclestone’s preferred bidder at a reduced price. Gribkowsky, who was a key figure in arranging the sale while working for the state-owned Bayerisches Landesbank, has already been convicted of corruption related to the payments and is serving an eight-and-a-half year sentence.

Ecclestone denies the payment was a bribe; he claims that Gribkowsky was blackmailing him with unfounded allegations about his taxes, which could have cost him billions. During Gribkowsky’s trial, Ecclestone admitted to making the payments but denied any illegal intent.

A German judge has now issued an indictment against Ecclestone, who must decide whether to respond to the charges voluntarily or risk extradition. His legal team plans to send a response to the judge in the coming weeks. After considering the defense and prosecution, the judge will determine whether Ecclestone should stand trial.

The proceedings have raised questions about Ecclestone’s ongoing role as Formula One’s chief executive while the charges remain. Ecclestone told the Financial Times: "I have just spoken to my lawyers and they have received an indictment. It’s being translated into English. We are defending it properly. It will be an interesting case. It’s a pity it’s happened."

He added that he considered the indictment "inevitable," saying, "If someone wants to sue you, they can do it and you have to defend it."

Ecclestone has stated that the payments were made under pressure from Gribkowsky, who allegedly threatened to report false information to UK tax authorities regarding Ecclestone family trusts in Liechtenstein. Ecclestone maintains he had no control over the trust and was not evading tax.

Comments on the case are unavailable for legal reasons.

一级方程式大亨伯尼·埃克莱斯通因被德国法院以贿赂罪起诉，正面临可能的引渡。这位82岁的亿万富翁如果被判有罪，可能面临最高五年监禁。

检察官指控埃克莱斯通向德国银行家格哈德·格里布科夫斯基支付了2600万英镑，确保2006年以较低价格将一级方程式的大量股份出售给他指定的买家。格里布科夫斯基当时在德国国有的巴伐利亚州银行任职，是此次股份出售的重要人物，目前因腐败受贿被定罪，正在服八年半的刑期。

埃克莱斯通否认该款项是贿赂；他称自己被格里布科夫斯基以无根据的税务指控勒索，否则可能损失数十亿。在格里布科夫斯基受审期间，埃克莱斯通承认支付了巨款，但坚称没有非法意图。

现有一名德国法官向埃克莱斯通发出起诉书，他必须决定是否自愿应诉，否则可能面临引渡。他的律师团队计划在接下来几周内提交回复。法官将在权衡控辩双方陈述后，决定是否传唤埃克莱斯通出庭受审。

案件引发外界对埃克莱斯通在被指控期间，能否继续担任一级方程式首席执行官的质疑。埃克莱斯通在接受《金融时报》采访时表示：“我刚与律师沟通，他们已收到起诉书，正在把内容翻译成英文。我们会妥善应对。这将是一个有趣的案件。很遗憾会发生这样的事。”

他还表示，自己被起诉是“不可避免”的，并说：“如果有人想告你，他们就会行动，你只能应对。”

埃克莱斯通称，支付巨款是因被格里布科夫斯基威胁，否则后者会向英国税务部门举报关于其家族信托的虚假信息。他坚称自己并不掌控该信托，也没有逃税。

因法律原因，暂不接受对此案的评论。

article_content: Google has launched a new line called 'Chromebook Plus,' designed to simplify the process of picking a Chromebook. Each Chromebook Plus comes with core features, including at least a 1080p webcam, and starts at $399. These Chromebooks enhance video call experiences with controls for lighting adjustment, noise cancellation, and live captions. There are also several background blur options, and these settings work with any video conferencing app. Photo editing also gets an upgrade. Users will find Google's Magic Eraser in the Photos app and can now access Adobe Photoshop on the web. New Chromebook Plus buyers receive three months of free Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Express. AI is at the center of this release. A no-cost trial of Duet AI is available, which integrates into apps such as Gmail, Docs, and Meet. Google is also adding generative AI features, like drafting short content or generating custom wallpapers based on text prompts. Acer, ASUS, HP, and Lenovo will begin selling Chromebook Plus laptops on October 8, 2023. Existing eligible Chromebooks will start receiving these new features through a free OS update from October 17, 2023. By offering upgraded specs, improved features, and extended support, Google aims to make Chromebook Plus a trustworthy and sustainable choice for users.

article_content: On Friday, President Droupadi Murmu called upon civil servants to respond swiftly to public grievances and to adopt innovative methods that benefit citizens. Speaking to officer trainees at Rashtrapati Bhavan, she highlighted the importance of public feedback on government schemes, stating it is now a critical factor for efficient and accountable governance. President Murmu noted that with the rise of social media, people can instantly share their concerns, increasing the need for advanced tools and technology in public service delivery. 'As dynamic and aware civil servants, it is your duty to address the grievances and issues of the common people promptly. You must implement innovative measures that serve the immediate and long-term interests of both the citizens and the nation,' she said. The officer trainees are attending the 98th special foundation course focused on good governance at the Haryana Institute of Public Administration (HIPA) in Gurugram. The president observed that with new technological advancements, concepts like electronic, smart, and effective governance have become essential for fast and efficient service delivery. She commented that good governance signifies a citizen-centric approach and that public feedback is increasingly vital for accountable administration. President Murmu also reminded the trainees that civil servants play a key role in strengthening national unity and integration. 'It is your duty to contribute to the country’s inclusive development. The citizens of India are active participants in its progress. Promoting jan bhagidari, or people's partnership, is essential to achieve various program objectives,' she added. She further said that through collaboration with stakeholders, including the private sector, NGOs, and dedicated citizens, India can achieve its development goals. 'Remember, you were chosen to serve the nation. Align your personal goals with those of the country. Be prepared to face challenges and turn them into opportunities as you contribute to the development journey,' the president concluded.

article_content: Stockholm has witnessed a third consecutive night of unrest in its economically disadvantaged, immigrant-heavy neighborhoods, with rioting now spreading to at least ten districts. In the past two days, groups of mostly young people have set hundreds of cars on fire and clashed with police. This represents Sweden’s most serious wave of civil disturbance in recent years, triggering a nationwide debate over how the country handles youth unemployment and rising immigration. Despite calls for calm from Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt, the violence has intensified: rioters attacked a police station in Jakosberg, burned about 30 vehicles, smashed shop windows, and destroyed a 19th-century cultural center. Gangs also set fire to a school and a nursery, hurling stones at police and firefighters as they tried to respond. The immediate catalyst appears to be the fatal police shooting of a 69-year-old man wielding a machete in the Husby neighborhood. This incident has led to accusations of police brutality and heightened tensions between residents and authorities. The riots have brought renewed focus to Sweden’s deep-rooted social challenges. Critics argue that years of government policy have created isolated ‘ghetto’ areas with high unemployment rates and limited opportunities. The left-leaning Aftonbladet newspaper and opposition politicians have called the unrest a severe failure of social policy. Public unease over integration and immigration is reflected in the rising support for the anti-immigration Sweden Democrats party ahead of upcoming elections. Official statistics show that the unemployment rate among Sweden’s foreign-born residents is 16%, compared to 6% among native Swedes. Sweden is also among the European countries with the highest intake of asylum seekers. Although the nation is still lauded for its high standard of living, many immigrant communities continue to struggle with poverty and chronic joblessness. As the cleanup begins and burned vehicles are removed, Sweden must now confront challenging questions about integration, economic policy, and its evolving welfare system.

article_content: The Obama administration has defended its decision to exchange five Taliban detainees held at Guantanamo Bay for U.S. Army Sergeant Bowe Bergdahl, stating that notifying Congress in advance could have endangered Bergdahl’s life. This explanation was provided to senators during a classified briefing, amid a broader controversy surrounding the circumstances of Bergdahl’s capture, the prisoner swap, and the process by which it was conducted. Officials emphasized intelligence indicating that any leak about the negotiations could have resulted in Bergdahl’s death. At a press conference following the G7 summit in Belgium, President Barack Obama reiterated the American principle of not leaving service members behind, stating, “We do not leave anybody wearing the American uniform behind.” He rejected criticism for acting unilaterally, insisting that ensuring Bergdahl's safe return was a priority. Some lawmakers remain critical of the administration for bypassing the requirement to inform Congress in advance, as stipulated by the National Defense Authorization Act. Critics, particularly among Republicans, argue that the release of five Taliban members for one soldier—who some say abandoned his post—sets a concerning precedent. During the classified briefing, senators viewed a ‘proof of life’ video that showed Bergdahl in significantly deteriorated health. Reports from the meeting described the atmosphere as tense and somber, with several senators noting the seriousness of Bergdahl’s condition. Debate continues over accusations that Bergdahl deserted his unit. An Army investigation concluded he left his outpost deliberately but did not find definitive evidence of desertion, as intent could not be determined without Bergdahl’s statement. Claims that soldiers died attempting to rescue Bergdahl remain unsubstantiated, according to U.S. officials, though some former colleagues hold personal beliefs to the contrary. The prospect of such a prisoner swap had been considered for years but only gained traction as U.S. combat operations in Afghanistan neared their end. Some legal arguments assert that under the law of war, the Taliban detainees would have had to be released soon regardless. Sen. Angus King and other officials acknowledge mistakes were made in not keeping Congress sufficiently informed, but emphasize the urgency and threat to Bergdahl’s life influenced operational decisions. Bergdahl is recovering at Landstuhl Regional Medical Center in Germany and is showing signs of improvement, according to Pentagon officials. He has not yet spoken with his parents.

article_content: Katie Hill discovered a large cyst weighing more than two stone while pregnant, putting both her and her unborn son, Alfie, at serious risk. Doctors initially worried the cyst could be cancerous, warning that it could be fatal for both mother and baby if it ruptured. Katie and her partner, Ricky Collier, had been trying for a baby for 18 months and were delighted when she became pregnant last July. A few weeks after her 12-week scan in September, Katie experienced sharp, cramping pain on her left side. Doctors detected a small cyst and drained four liters of fluid, but after her 20-week scan, they found a much larger second cyst. Her consultant explained that the cyst contained debris and could potentially be cancerous, advising surgery at 25 weeks to maximize the baby's survival chances. The cyst continued to grow, causing severe pain and making Katie's abdomen as large as if she were carrying twins at 30 weeks. Doctors cautioned that a rupture could be life-threatening. In December, Katie was rushed to Royal Preston Hospital with breathing difficulties and a high temperature. She was found to be bleeding internally, received an emergency blood transfusion, and underwent emergency surgery. The three-and-a-half-hour operation removed 12 liters of fluid from the cyst, and thankfully, no cancer was detected. The cyst had developed in her left fallopian tube, which had expanded significantly. Surgeons also removed her left fallopian tube during the procedure. Katie had regular scans afterward to monitor Alfie's health, and despite concerns, he developed normally. Three months later, Katie delivered Alfie slightly prematurely at Royal Preston Hospital. He spent several days in intensive care but recovered well, and both mother and son were able to return home after a week. Katie expressed her relief and happiness, describing Alfie as an 'absolute joy.' Both parents felt grateful and amazed at their family's outcome. During the pregnancy, the couple faced additional worry when a scan suggested some abnormality in Alfie's brain, but chose not to pursue further testing. Sanjeev Prashar, clinical director of women's health at Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, said that removing such a large cyst during pregnancy is rare and complex, and sent his best wishes to the family.

article_content: Gary Coleman's funeral plans remain on pause as a Utah court decides who will inherit his estate, shares attorney Robert Jeffs. Although cremation is planned, Coleman's ashes will be held until a dispute between ex-wife Shannon Price and former business associate Anna Gray is settled. Coleman divorced Price in 2008, but they lived together in Santaquin, Utah, when he suffered a fatal fall last month. Price claims she was still his common-law wife and has filed a handwritten note from 2007 supporting her claim. Meanwhile, a 2005 will names Gray as executor and sole heir. Judge James Taylor is expected to spend several months reviewing which document is Coleman's legal will. In the interim, Jeffs—the court-appointed special administrator—will keep Coleman's ashes secure in a vault. There is consensus that Coleman wanted to be cremated, as stated in his 2005 will, which also requested no funeral or memorial. A 1999 will outlined even stricter criteria for services and attendees. Coleman's remains are now at a Utah mortuary, with final arrangements on hold. The judge allowed time for Gray to view the body before cremation proceeds. Coleman was best known for his iconic role on 'Diff'rent Strokes.'

article_content:
For decades, California maintained a level of political influence that was the envy of lawmakers in Washington. Nancy Pelosi, who led the House Democratic Caucus for 20 years—including eight years as Speaker—was the party's foremost fundraiser and one of the most skilled legislative tacticians. Kevin McCarthy, a Bakersfield native who rose through the ranks to become Speaker, was also among the most prolific Republican fundraisers nationwide. The late Dianne Feinstein, a trailblazing politician who began in San Francisco city government and chaired the Senate Intelligence Committee, was long respected for her expertise on intelligence issues.

Recently, however, California's political dominance has shifted. McCarthy was removed as Speaker last week in a historic vote. Pelosi remains in Congress but is no longer part of the Democratic leadership. Following Feinstein’s passing, both California senators are now among the most junior members of the chamber. This dramatic change could have major implications for the state.

Both parties have had to adapt to significant changes in California politics in recent years. Republicans—once competitive statewide—have not won a major statewide race since 2006, when Arnold Schwarzenegger was re-elected Governor and Steve Poizner won Insurance Commissioner. McCarthy’s leadership provided a rare GOP foothold for California in Congress, allowing him to recruit diverse candidates and connect with significant conservative donors. Although McCarthy has pledged to help maintain the GOP’s slim 221-212 House majority, the next Speaker, whether Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana or Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, faces major challenges ahead.

On the Democratic side, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York—who succeeded Pelosi—is working to regain a House majority, partially by strengthening relationships in California. Pelosi’s extensive California network, including leaders such as Governor Gavin Newsom and the late Senator Feinstein, was a significant asset for the party.

California’s House races in 2024 are especially important, as the balance of power could hinge on their outcomes. The San Francisco Bay Area has traditionally been California’s political center, producing leaders like Vice President Kamala Harris (former San Francisco District Attorney), Governor Gavin Newsom (former San Francisco Mayor), former Governor Jerry Brown (ex-Oakland Mayor), former Senator Barbara Boxer, and the late Rep. Ron Dellums (former Oakland Mayor). Pelosi has represented her San Francisco-based district since 1987, and Feinstein, a former San Francisco Mayor, served in the Senate from 1992 until her recent death.

Despite the Bay Area’s influence, power is now shifting toward Southern California. Senator Alex Padilla, who succeeded Harris in 2021, is from Los Angeles. Newly appointed Senator Laphonza Butler—closely connected to Newsom and Harris—has not previously held elective office. Some of the leading Democratic Senate candidates, such as Reps. Katie Porter and Adam Schiff, represent Southern California districts. Rep. Barbara Lee is the only prominent Bay Area Democrat currently running. Most of next year’s competitive House races are also in Los Angeles and Orange counties.

While Harris and Newsom are key party leaders and possible 2028 presidential candidates, the 2024 elections could dramatically reshape California’s longstanding political landscape.

几十年来，加利福尼亚一直是华盛顿政坛羡慕的政治风向标。南希·佩洛西曾担任众院民主党领袖20年，其中8年担任议长，是党内筹款和策略的顶尖人物。凯文·麦卡锡出身贝克斯菲尔德，升任众院议长，也成为全国知名的共和党筹款高手。已故的戴安娜·范斯坦作为旧金山本地政治家，后来担任参议院情报委员会主席，多年来因其在情报领域的权威获得尊敬。

然而，近期加州的政治影响力发生了巨大变化。上周，麦卡锡在一场历史性投票中被罢免议长职务。佩洛西虽然还在国会，但不再担任民主党领导。范斯坦去世后，加州两位参议员现在都是参院中最资浅的成员。这一剧变可能对加州带来深远影响。

近年来，两党都不得不适应加州政治的重大变迁。共和党曾在全州选举中具竞争力，但自2006年以来再未获胜。当时施瓦辛格连任州长，波伊茨纳赢得保险专员。麦卡锡的领导让加州成为国会少有的共和党根据地，帮助吸引不同候选人并联结重要保守派金主。尽管麦卡锡承诺要协助维持221-212微弱多数，但无论是路易斯安那的斯蒂夫·斯卡利斯，或俄亥俄的吉姆·乔丹接任议长，都将面临艰巨挑战。

民主党方面，来自纽约的少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯——佩洛西的继任者——正努力通过与加州关系争取众院多数席位。佩洛西在加州的人脉，包括州长纽森及已故范斯坦，都是民主党宝贵资产。

2024年加州众议院争夺格外关键，胜负将左右国会平衡。湾区历来是加州政治中心，孕育了副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯（前旧金山地区检察官）、州长加文·纽森（前旧金山市长）、前州长杰瑞·布朗（前奥克兰市长）、前参议员芭芭拉·鲍克瑟，以及已故众议员罗恩·德卢姆斯（前奥克兰市长）。佩洛西自1987年起一直代表旧金山选区，而范斯坦则自1992年至上月去世始终担任参议员。

尽管湾区依旧有影响力，政治重心正逐渐南移。2021年接替哈里斯的参议员亚历克斯·帕迪利亚来自洛杉矶。新任参议员拉方扎·巴特勒与纽森、哈里斯关系密切，但未有民选公职经历。主要民主党参议员候选人如凯蒂·波特、亚当·希夫都代表南加州，湾区仅芭芭拉·李竞选。2024年最激烈的国会选战大多在洛杉矶和橙县。

哈里斯和纽森仍是党内核心人物，也有望于2028年竞选总统。明年大选有可能彻底重塑加州长期的政治格局。

article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — Some Democrats are increasingly concerned about President Obama's $787 billion plan to revitalize the struggling economy and are demanding more transparency regarding future spending. Rep. Earl Pomeroy (D-North Dakota) expressed significant worry about the possibility of a second stimulus package. With the White House often comparing the nation's economy to a house on fire, some congressional Democrats are questioning where the aid is. Rep. Carol Shea-Porter (D-New Hampshire) recently told Treasury Secretary Tim Geithner in Congress, 'Hurry, please hurry, because people are waiting and they are hurting, and they need the help now.' She is among a growing number of Democrats uncomfortable or at odds with some of the administration’s economic approaches. Some Democrats also take issue with aspects of the president's budget plan, particularly proposals to reduce popular tax deductions for wealthier Americans. White House Press Secretary Robert Gibbs commented, 'I don't think ultimately the criticism is surprising. That certainly happens and is all part of the process.' To address moderate concerns, President Obama included in his budget items that former President George W. Bush had kept separate in recent years, such as war funding for Iraq and Afghanistan, an annual multibillion-dollar fix for Medicare physician payments, and relief from the Alternative Minimum Tax for the middle class, to provide greater transparency. Sen. Evan Bayh (D-Indiana), part of a group of moderate Democratic senators known as the 'Gang of 15,' said messaging on the rationale for economic reforms is vital. He stressed that controlling health care costs, developing sustainable energy sources, and tackling the financial crisis are all important for the economy. Bayh added, 'Obama's got to move on all these fronts but also keep them tied to strengthening the economy, getting people to work, growing businesses, and improving our standard of living.' Rep. John Tanner (D-Tennessee), a member of the fiscally conservative 'Blue Dog' Democrats, noted that while Obama’s budget is large and the deficit is significant, 'it’s honest and truthful' about the country’s economic status. Steve Murphy, a Democratic media consultant, explained that Blue Dogs are 'deficit hawks' who are skeptical about further bank bailouts without accountability, want to target wasteful spending, and believe reducing the deficit was key to economic success in the 1990s. He added that, despite misgivings, these Democrats accept more funding may be necessary and will push for accountability and fairness for taxpayers. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi shared that leading economists have indicated a second stimulus package might be necessary. In a closed meeting with House Democrats, economists reportedly predicted that Obama’s stimulus plan would fall short of saving or creating the promised three to four million jobs. Economist Allen Sinai estimated, 'Over the first two years, about two and a half million jobs will be saved or created—a bit fewer than the administration and Speaker Pelosi have projected.' Sinai suggested the jobs goal could be met over time, but patience is required. Some budget hawks within the party remain skeptical. Rep. Earl Pomeroy said, 'If we were to vote this afternoon, the stimulus package would probably fail. If more funds are to be committed, a precise plan is needed.' Rep. Shea-Porter says her concerns reflect what she hears from constituents, as well as some in the media, commenting, 'It’s terrifying people. Previously, leaders and the public were optimistic, but now the media is often frightening people without presenting both sides.' For now, the White House maintains there are no current plans for another stimulus, insisting that the original plan needs time to work. In other words, the fire is not out yet. CNN’s Dana Bash and Time.com’s Jay Newton-Small contributed to this report.
translated_content: 华盛顿（CNN）——部分民主党人日益关注奥巴马总统7870亿美元振兴疲弱经济的计划，并要求未来支出更加透明。 北达科他州众议员厄尔·波默罗伊（Earl Pomeroy）对可能出台第二轮经济刺激方案表达了严重担忧。白宫常将美国经济比作失火的房屋，一些国会民主党人因此质问救火车去了哪里。 新罕布什尔州众议员卡罗尔·谢伊-波特（Carol Shea-Porter）近日在国会告诉财政部长盖特纳：“请快一点，真的请快一点，因为大家都在等待，他们很痛苦，他们现在真的需要帮助。”她是越来越多对政府经济措施感到不安的民主党人之一。 一些民主党人还对总统预算案中的部分内容表示异议，尤其是减少高收入者流行税收减免的提议。 白宫新闻秘书罗伯特·吉布斯表示：“我认为，批评本身并不令人惊讶。这种情况的确会发生，是整个过程的一部分。” 为回应温和派的关切，奥巴马总统在预算中加入了前总统布什过去几年单独列支的项目，包括伊拉克和阿富汗战争经费、每年数十亿美元的医疗保险医生费用补贴，以及为中产阶级提供的替代性最低税减免，以增强透明度。 印第安纳州参议员埃文·拜伊（Evan Bayh）是被称为“十五人帮”的温和派民主党参议员团体成员，他表示，围绕经济改革的宣传方式至关重要。他强调，控制医疗支出、发展可持续能源以及应对金融危机，对经济都很重要。拜伊补充称：“奥巴马需要在这些方面同时推进，并把它们都联系回持续壮大经济、增加就业、促进企业成长，提高生活标准的核心主题。” 田纳西州众议员约翰·坦纳（John Tanner），作为财政保守派‘蓝狗’民主党人的一员指出，尽管奥巴马的预算规模巨大，赤字严重，但‘它如实、坦率地反映了国家的经济状况’。 民主党媒体顾问史蒂夫·墨菲（Steve Murphy）解释说，蓝狗都是“赤字鹰派”，对没有问责机制的银行救助持怀疑态度，主张打击浪费性支出，并坚信上世纪90年代经济成功的基础是缩减赤字。他补充称，尽管存疑，这些民主党人也明白可能还需要更多资金，并将推动加强对纳税人的问责与公平。 众议长南希·佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）透露，主要经济学家表示可能需要第二轮刺激计划。在与众议院民主党人的闭门会上，据称经济学家们预测奥巴马的刺激方案将无法达到承诺的三四百万新增/保住岗位目标。经济学家艾伦·西奈（Allen Sinai）估算：“前两年，大约会有250万个岗位被保住或新创造出来，比政府和佩洛西预期的略低。”西奈表示，长期来看总统的就业目标可能达成，但需要公众耐心等待。 党内部分“赤字鹰派”依然持怀疑态度。厄尔·波默罗伊众议员称：“如果我们现在投票，刺激计划可能会被否决。如果要投入更多资金，就必须详细说明怎么操作。” 谢伊-波特还说，她的担忧反映了她在家乡听到的选民声音，媒体上也有关切。“这让人害怕。以前大家和领导人都很乐观，但如今媒体常常只讲消极吓人的话，而没有给出全面观点。” 目前，白宫表示没有推出新刺激方案的计划，强调原有计划还需时间显现成效。换句话说，火还没灭。 本报道由CNN的Dana Bash与Time.com的Jay Newton-Small共同贡献。

article_content: Political associates of the late Dr. Olusola Saraki, along with former government officials, political office holders, and supporters of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kwara State, gathered on Tuesday to offer special prayers in his memory. The event, which marked the 11th annual prayer session for the late politician and philanthropist, was led by the Chief Imam of Ilorin, Sheikh Mohammed Bashir-Saliu, and attended by other Islamic clerics from across the state. Participants, who gathered in large numbers, called on both the federal and state governments to address the current socio-economic hardships faced by Nigerians, especially residents of Kwara State, following the example set by Saraki during his lifetime. Speaking to journalists, PDP State Chairman Babatunde Mohammed reflected on Dr. Saraki’s commitment to public welfare, remarking, “For nearly 40 years, he brought happiness to many through his philanthropic efforts. He always prioritized helping others, and would return home to assist people in all 16 local government areas whenever hardship arose. His son, our leader, continues this legacy today.” Mohammed emphasized that the governor and all elected officials in Kwara should take immediate, lawful measures to alleviate the current economic challenges, regardless of political affiliation, as hardships are affecting everyone in the state. He also urged members of the State Assembly, the House of Representatives, and the Senate to empower their constituents to help reduce widespread suffering. Expressing gratitude, Mohammed acknowledged Saraki’s profound impact on his own career, saying, “Baba Saraki mentored me and enabled my political journey. May God grant him eternal rest.” He concluded by encouraging leaders to emulate Saraki’s dedication to the welfare of Kwara and Nigeria, describing him as a role model in political life.

article_content:
Sydney, known for top Japanese venues like Tetsuya’s and Sokyo, is about to experience a new kind of Japanese dining. This February, for two nights only, the famed Robot Restaurant from Shinjuku, Tokyo, will pop up in Australia. Organized by travel experts Contiki, the event—called Robots Unrivalled—aims to deliver an unforgettable mix of Japanese culture and futuristic entertainment.

Attendees can expect a dazzling spectacle: glowing neon lights, shimmering robot tanks, and cabaret dancers in metallic costumes. Direct from Japan’s cult-favorite sci-fi restaurant, performances will include robot battles, synchronised drumming, and techno-inspired dance routines, all set to high-energy J-Pop beats. Waitstaff dressed in LED-lit outfits will serve cocktails, adding to the immersive and surreal experience.

The original Robot Restaurant, opened in Tokyo’s Kabukicho district in 2012 at a reported cost of over $10 million, is celebrated for its extravaganza of lights, mirrors, and digital displays. While officially a restaurant, its focus is entertainment—the regular menu consists mainly of a simple bento box, similar to options found in Japanese convenience stores. The food menu for the Sydney event is not confirmed but may include authentic Japanese street food.

The sensory-heavy show is not recommended for people with epilepsy due to flashing lights and intense visual effects. Diners will receive glow sticks to join in the fun, waving them along with the performers. Robots Unrivalled will take place on February 23 and 24. Tickets are limited, with early access available to those who register in advance at www.contiki.com/robotsunrivalled.

article_content:
Teachers at Fair Oak Academy in Rugeley, Staffordshire, have created a humorous parody video of 2014’s biggest pop hits, aiming to raise funds for the Teenage Cancer Trust in memory of former student Stephen Sutton. In the video, staff dress up as famous musicians and celebrities, recreating scenes from iconic music videos and adverts such as Pharrell Williams’ ‘Happy’, Miley Cyrus’s ‘Wrecking Ball’, the original Band Aid’s ‘Do They Know It’s Christmas?’, Taylor Swift’s ‘Shake It Off’, and the John Lewis Christmas advert.

The project, produced by Rachael Sandham, the school’s director of design, involved teachers volunteering their time after school, as well as the support of students and the wider school community. Notably, teacher Phil Yeomans swings from gym ropes as Miley Cyrus in ‘Wrecking Ball’, and school principal David Powell stars in several scenes, even wearing a tutu for comedic effect. 

The video, uploaded on Friday evening, has already received over 2,500 views on YouTube. Eleven-year-old student Cole Parker features as the young boy in the John Lewis parody, recognized for his outstanding performance this year. The staff and Stephen Sutton’s family have enthusiastically supported the effort, with the Sutton family giving their blessing for the tribute.

Principal Powell, retiring at the end of the term, shared his delight in participating and described the project as a fun and meaningful way to support a worthy cause, even if it meant donning unusual costumes. Miss Sandham expressed hopes that the video will lift spirits and raise significant awareness and funds for the Teenage Cancer Trust, serving as a heartfelt tribute to Stephen Sutton’s legacy of resilience and positivity.

Fair Oak Academy, which serves over 800 students aged 11 to 18, was rated ‘Good’ by Ofsted in 2013. The staff intend to continue the annual video tradition, featuring student participation in future projects.

article_content: Ted Beston, a former BBC Radio 1 producer, was arrested as part of Operation Yewtree, the police investigation into sexual abuse allegations involving Jimmy Savile and others within the entertainment industry. Beston, now 76, has strongly denied claims that he molested young women or helped procure girls for abuse during the 1960s and 1970s. Authorities searched Beston's Bromley, south London residence, removing several items as evidence. Having worked closely with Savile on programs like 'Savile’s Travels,' 'Jimmy Savile Old Record Club,' and 'Double Top Ten Show,' Beston maintains he was unaware of any criminal activity, asserting he had no knowledge of underage victims. Known on air as 'Uncle Ted,' Beston was arrested early in the morning and later released on bail pending further inquiries, scheduled to return in February 2013. He is the eighth person arrested in the scope of Operation Yewtree, an extensive investigation managed by a 30-officer Metropolitan Police team and reportedly costing around £2 million. The inquiry is divided into three strands: allegations directly concerning Savile, accusations involving Savile’s associates, and cases targeting others in the entertainment field. To date, police have received 199 complaints of sexual assaults and 31 allegations of rape against Savile, with over 589 individuals coming forward—most reported to be underage females at the time. Other notable figures arrested and bailed include PR consultant Max Clifford, DJ Dave Lee Travis, entertainer Gary Glitter, and producer Wilfred De'ath. More than two dozen celebrities fitting Savile's generational profile have reportedly been named to the police. Investigators believe there is sufficient evidence for arrests in at least a dozen instances, though not every complainant may press charges or be publicly identified. Beston’s legal team continues to insist on his innocence and request privacy as investigations continue into allegations of historical abuse in the U.K.’s broadcasting world. The Metropolitan Police are leading efforts to establish the scale and specifics of the long-standing misconduct.

article_content: Travelers renting cars should watch out for additional charges, including cancellation penalties, energy surcharges, and various fees. With the industry facing significant financial losses amid the recession, many car rental companies have quietly introduced these new surcharges to recoup revenues, leaving some customers confused by unexpected costs at checkout. For instance, Jim Swofford recently noticed a $5 cancellation fee on his Hertz bill—a type of charge usually not associated with cancellations. When he considered skipping his reservation instead, he learned the no-show fee would be $50. Similarly, photographer Eric Hegwer from Austin, Texas, was surprised by a $1 'energy surcharge' he hadn’t seen before. Hertz spokeswoman Paula Rivera explained that since late 2008, the cancellation fee applies to prepaid reservations to cover processing and holding vehicles, while the energy surcharge offsets rising operating costs. These and other fees reflect the industry’s mounting financial pressures. Hertz recently reported a $73 million quarterly loss, Avis lost $121 million, and Advantage Rent A Car declared bankruptcy before Hertz purchased its assets. While industry leaders argue that such surcharges are necessary for survival, critics say car rental firms should provide more transparent explanations of all charges. Robert Barton, president of the American Car Rental Association and U-Save COO, stresses the importance of clear disclosure. Customers should remain alert for several types of fees: 1. Duplicate charges, such as being billed twice for gas, as Sid Savara experienced. 2. Fees for standard car features, including the $2 'tire fee' from Enterprise in Florida, or additional oil surcharges. 3. Stacked surcharges, like Scott Lerman’s 'privilege fee', often added to other 'concession recovery' fees. 4. Stadium taxes, where cities impose rental car taxes to fund venues—as Seth Mendelsohn saw with a $4 'downtown arena' fee. 5. Extra driver fees, now more strictly enforced, such as those Carol Stevenson faced at Payless in Phoenix. Some of these extra fees may be avoided by booking through certain travel sites that guarantee all-inclusive rates, but rental companies continue to find new ways to add charges—even for prepaid bookings. Given the proliferation of such fees, experts advise travelers to carefully review rental agreements in order to avoid unwelcome surprises. The addition of new surcharges shows no sign of slowing.

article_content: SpaceX has released impressive images from its second integrated test flight of the Starship rocket, conducted on Saturday. The photos display the 33 Raptor engines of the first-stage Super Heavy booster as the world’s most powerful space vehicle lifts off from SpaceX’s Starbase facility in Texas, generating approximately 17 million pounds of thrust. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also shared dramatic aerial footage of the 400-foot-tall Starship rocket at the start of its test flight. Unlike the first test flight in April, during this flight, the second-stage Starship spacecraft successfully separated from the Super Heavy booster about 2 minutes and 50 seconds after liftoff. However, about 30 seconds later, the first-stage booster experienced what SpaceX described as a 'rapid unscheduled disassembly'—meaning it exploded. The Starship spacecraft also did not complete its planned flight. Despite these setbacks, SpaceX regarded the test as a success for achieving stage separation and lasting longer than the April test. Engineers will now analyze all aspects of the flight to improve the system for future missions. NASA is closely following SpaceX’s Starship program since it plans to use a modified Starship to land astronauts on the Moon for the Artemis III mission, which is scheduled for 2025. Shortly after the test flight, NASA Administrator Bill Nelson congratulated the SpaceX team on their progress, stating: 'Spaceflight is a bold adventure demanding a can-do spirit and daring innovation. Today’s test is an opportunity to learn—then fly again. Together, NASA and SpaceX will return humanity to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.'
translated_content: SpaceX发布了第二次星舰火箭综合测试飞行的精彩图片，该测试于周六进行。照片展示了由33台猛禽发动机驱动的一级重型助推器，这款被称为全球最强大的太空发射载具，在SpaceX德克萨斯Starbase基地点火升空，产生了大约1700万磅的推力。 SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克还分享了星舰火箭起飞初期的震撼高空拍摄画面，这枚火箭高达400英尺。 与四月份的首次试飞不同，这次二级星舰飞船在发射约2分50秒后成功与重型助推器分离。不过，大约30秒后，一级助推器发生了SpaceX所说的“快速非计划性解体”——也就是爆炸。星舰飞船最终也未能完成既定飞行。 尽管出现这些挫折，SpaceX仍然认为测试取得了重要进展，因为实现了成功分离并且飞行持续时间超过了上一次。工程师们将全面分析本次飞行所有细节，以改进系统，为后续任务做准备。 NASA正在密切关注SpaceX的星舰项目，计划在2025年阿尔忒弥斯3号任务中，利用改进版星舰把宇航员送上月球。 测试飞行结束后不久，NASA署长比尔·纳尔逊向SpaceX团队表示祝贺并表示：“太空飞行是一场大胆冒险，需要敢为和创新精神。今天的测试是一次学习机会——然后再次起飞。NASA与SpaceX将携手，把人类送回月球、前往火星与更远的地方。”

article_content: Delhi’s persistent air quality crisis has attracted the attention of India’s Supreme Court for almost four decades. Through various landmark judgments and ongoing oversight, the court has played a central role in shaping how the city confronts pollution. Most recently, as pollution levels soared in November, the Supreme Court pressed officials for swift action. The court examined strategies like alternating vehicle usage by license plate numbers and cracking down on stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana. Although implementation was officially left to the government, the court strongly rebuked authorities for failing to allocate funds for a rapid rail project intended to cut emissions, calling it a serious breach of commitment. The court also faulted Punjab’s government for inadequate stubble management, arguing that their handling unfairly shifted blame onto farmers. Over the years, court orders have changed life in Delhi: setting standards for which vehicles can operate, shutting down highly polluting factories, and requiring some businesses to close to reduce emissions. On several occasions, the judiciary spurred government action that might not otherwise have happened. Still, critics question the court’s activist stance, warning that it sometimes encroaches on policy roles better left to elected officials. They also point out that pollution has continued to worsen, despite decades of court-mandated reforms. Senior lawyer Shyam Divan has described the Supreme Court as acting as policymaker, legislator, and administrator—filling roles that in other countries belong to government agencies. The court’s engagement with environmental issues can be traced to petitions brought in 1984 by MC Mehta concerning vehicle emissions, the deterioration of the Taj Mahal, and river pollution. To this day, the court continues appending new concerns—such as folding air quality challenges into broader pollution litigation. Some interventions have been dramatic. In 1998, the court required all public transport vehicles to switch from diesel to compressed natural gas (CNG) within three years, despite government resistance. Enforcement, including fines and contempt threats, ensured compliance. Study findings show these changes yielded only short-term improvements. Air quality did improve with the CNG move, but the benefits were soon offset by surging private vehicle ownership. Lawyer Anuj Bhuwania has noted that some reforms harmed public transport workers, especially tuk-tuk drivers, who rarely had input in the court process. Bhuwania argues that India’s public interest litigation, once a tool for empowerment, now often serves elite interests and leaves poorer workers unheard. Nonetheless, some former chief justices have defended the court’s involvement. PN Bhagwati called 'judicial activism' inevitable, while KG Balakrishnan said the CNG mandate showed courts are sometimes willing to make unpopular but necessary choices for environmental protection. However, others point to questionable initiatives, like smog towers mandated by the court despite little scientific backing. Years after installation, authorities found these towers had minimal effect on city pollution. Lawyer Shibani Ghosh credits the court with positive steps but stresses the need for stronger government leadership in making and enforcing environmental policy. Environmental law expert Ritwick Dutta suggests specialized tribunals could better enforce India’s many environmental laws, which are not always implemented. Dutta notes Supreme Court urgency usually spikes only when pollution peaks; once the air temporarily clears, these cases are often deprioritized.
translated_content: 德里长期的空气质量危机已持续近四十年，并引起了印度最高法院的高度关注。通过一系列标志性判决和持续监督，最高法院在该市治理污染的过程中发挥了关键作用。 最近，随着德里污染水平在十一月急剧上升，最高法院敦促相关官员迅速采取行动。法院讨论了如按车牌号单双日限行和打击旁遮普邦与哈里亚纳邦秸秆焚烧等措施。尽管实际执行权仍归政府，但法院因未拨款用于减少车流量的快速轨道项目而严厉批评了相关部门，称这是严重违背承诺。 法院还批评旁遮普邦政府未能有效应对秸秆焚烧问题，认为其管理不善导致农民遭受指责。多年来，法院的命令已改变德里的生活，如为经营车辆制定环保标准、关闭污染严重的工厂、部分企业停业以减少排放。法院屡次推动了政府本可能不会主动推进的环保措施。 不过，有批评认为，法院的积极介入有时逾越本应由民选政府负责的政策领域。同时，尽管法院几十年来做出多项改革，德里的污染问题依旧严峻。知名律师沙亚姆·迪万（Shyam Divan）形容，最高法院成了政策制定者、立法者和管理者，这些职能在其他国家通常由政府机构担当。 最高法院最早在1984年就通过环境活动家MC Mehta针对机动车尾气、泰姬陵损毁以及河流污染的请愿介入环境问题。时至今日，法院还常将新的空气质量议题并入现有的污染案件中处理。 有些判决影响重大。1998年，法院要求全部公共交通工具三年内由柴油改为压缩天然气（CNG）。虽遭到政府反对，但通过罚款和蔑视法庭威胁，规定最终得以执行。 相关研究显示，这一措施确曾短暂改善空气，但随着私家车数量飙升，成效逐渐被削弱。律师阿努吉·布瓦尼亚（Anuj Bhuwania）指出，这些改革影响了很多公共交通工作者，尤其三轮车司机，而他们未能在法庭上为自己发声。他认为，公益诉讼制度原为推动变革的利器，现在却更多服务于精英群体，忽略了底层工人的利益。 即便如此，许多前首席大法官为法院介入辩护。PN·巴格瓦蒂（PN Bhagwati）称“司法能动主义”不可避免，KG·巴拉克里希南（KG Balakrishnan）表示CNG推行说明法院有时会为环保作出不得人心但必要的决策。但也有质疑声音，批评法院强制安装“雾霾塔”的举措缺乏科学依据，事实证明作用有限。 律师席巴尼·高希（Shibani Ghosh）肯定法院的某些改革成就，但强调更应让政府主导政策落实。环境法专家里特维克·杜塔（Ritwick Dutta）建议由专业法庭更好贯彻印度众多但执行不到位的环保法律。他指出，最高法院通常只在污染高峰期紧急介入，而一旦空气略有好转，相关案件又被忽略。

article_content: Leo Ortega began planting spiky blue agave plants on the dry hillsides around his home in Murrieta, Southern California, because his wife liked their appearance. Ten years later, his property features thousands of agave plants, a crop he and others see as a promising alternative for the state amid years of severe drought and efforts to reduce groundwater use. The 49-year-old mechanical engineer is among a growing group of Californians cultivating agave to produce spirits similar to Mexico’s tequila and mezcal. This trend is driven by the search for resilient, low-water crops and rising demand for premium spirits following the COVID-19 pandemic. Entrepreneurs like Ortega, along with California farmers, are turning to water-efficient crops and irrigation methods as water restrictions and climate change make traditional farming more challenging. Unlike most crops, agave thrives with minimal water. “When we watered them, they didn’t grow much, but the ones we didn’t water actually grew better,” Ortega said, walking among rows of the succulent plants. Following the success of his initial spirits made from Agave americana—which sold for $160 a bottle—Ortega is now investing in his own distillery. According to agave spirits expert Erlinda A. Doherty, consumers began spending more on high-quality spirits during the pandemic, leading to a rise in premium beverage sales. In 2022, tequila and mezcal were the second-fastest-growing spirit category in the U.S., as reported by the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States. Both beverages are protected by Mexican law and U.S. trade agreements: tequila must consist of at least 51% blue Weber agave and be produced in specific Mexican regions, while mezcal is made from various agave types but also must be produced in certain Mexican states. Despite these rules, agave growers and distillers in California, Texas, and Arizona are betting on the potential for agave-based spirits produced outside of Mexico—even if they can’t be called tequila or mezcal. “We seem to have this insatiable thirst for agave, so why not have a domestically grown supply?” Doherty said. Alfonso Mojica Navarro, director of the Mexican Chamber of the Tequila Industry, emphasized tequila’s long heritage, global reputation, and deep ties to Mexican culture. While he did not comment directly on California’s efforts, he noted that the tequila industry is concerned about more producers trying to benefit from tequila’s popularity by making agave spirits that mimic the renowned Mexican drink. Large-scale commercial agave cultivation has yet to take off in California, and expansion will take time. Still, spirits made from the cooked, fermented core of the plant are gaining popularity, according to Henry Tarmy, owner of Ventura Spirits, who began distilling agave five years ago. “We’ve sold everything we’ve made,” he said. California has introduced measures to protect its fledgling industry. Legislation passed last year requires that “California agave spirits” be made only from agave grown in the state and without additives. Additionally, a group of growers and distillers formed the California Agave Council, which has tripled in size since its 2023 founding, said director Craig Reynolds, who grows agave near Davis, Northern California. “We have about 45 member growers. All of them want more plants,” Reynolds noted, adding that many makers of agave spirits deeply respect Mexican tequila traditions. Agave needs very little water but brings other challenges: it takes at least seven years to mature, is difficult to harvest—mature plants can weigh hundreds of pounds—and must be replanted after harvesting. Yet, many see agave as a practical alternative as California, a major supplier of U.S. produce, seeks ways to reduce water use. Drought conditions may return, despite heavy rain and snow in the past winter that eased a three-year drought. California also started regulating groundwater nearly a decade ago after excessive pumping depleted wells and caused the land to sink. Scientists predict that extreme weather will become even more frequent as the planet warms, leading to more drought. Central Valley farmer Stuart Woolf began considering agave after determining he could farm only 60% of his land over the next 20 years due to water constraints, despite investments in renewable energy and groundwater projects. Woolf went on to plant about 200,000 agave on land he would have otherwise left fallow. Each acre uses just 3 inches (7.6 cm) of water annually—one-tenth of what most row crops need, and even less than pistachio or almond trees. Woolf and his wife Lisa donated $100,000 to UC Davis to support research into drought-tolerant agave varieties. “I’ve been trying to find a crop that’s climate-resilient and drought-tolerant so I can use our land effectively,” said Woolf. “The amount of water I’m using is so low, I don’t think I’ll ever have a problem.”
translated_content: Leo Ortega因为妻子喜欢蓝色带刺龙舌兰的外形，十年前在南加州穆列塔家附近干燥的山坡上种下了第一批龙舌兰。如今，随着加州多年来遭受严重干旱、地下水受限，他的家园已经种满了数千株龙舌兰——这种作物被越来越多人视作该州农业的新希望。这位49岁的机械工程师，正和越来越多的加州人一起种植龙舌兰，生产类似墨西哥龙舌兰酒与梅斯卡尔的烈酒。新趋势背后，是大家在水资源受限和气候变化的大环境下，寻找更耐旱低耗水农作物；同时，自新冠疫情后，对高端酒类的需求也在猛增。像Ortega这样的创客及农民，正尝试节水型作物和新灌溉方式，以应对水资源紧缩和极端天气。与多数作物不同，龙舌兰几乎不用灌溉就能生长。“灌溉过的反而长得慢，没浇水的更旺盛，”Ortega边走边说。凭借首批每瓶160美元的Agave americana烈酒热销，Ortega更决定投资开设自家酒厂。龙舌兰酒专家Erlinda A. Doherty指出，疫情期间消费者更多地倾向高端酒类，带动了高端饮品销量。2022年，美国烈酒协会数据显示，龙舌兰酒与梅斯卡尔成为美国第二快增长的烈酒品类。受墨西哥法律与美国贸易协议保护，“tequila”需含至少51%蓝色韦伯龙舌兰，并仅可在特定墨西哥州生产；而“mezcal”虽然原料种类更丰富，但也有指定产区。尽管如此，加州、德州和亚利桑那州的种植者和酿酒师仍看好本土龙舌兰酒（虽不能叫tequila/mezcal）的市场潜力。Doherty说：“大家对龙舌兰的热情不断，为什么不支持美国本土供应？”墨西哥龙舌兰工业协会总监Alfonso Mojica Navarro强调，tequila传承悠久，享誉全球，与墨西哥文化密不可分。虽然对加州的探索未明确表态，但他也指出业内担忧，越来越多厂商试图利用tequila的知名度，生产类似却不能称作tequila的产品。当前加州龙舌兰还未大规模商业种植，发展尚需时日。但Ventura Spirits酒厂主Henry Tarmy五年前开始蒸馏龙舌兰酒，市场反应不错：“我们酿的全都卖光了。”为保护新兴产业，加州去年立法，规定“加州龙舌兰酒”须全部采用本地种植龙舌兰且不得加添加剂。加州龙舌兰理事会也于2023年由一批种植者和酿造者创立，创会理事Craig Reynolds介绍，如今成员已翻三倍，“目前有约45位种植者，都希望种更多。”他补充，大多数酒厂也很尊重墨西哥龙舌兰传统。龙舌兰极省水，却有其它考验：需生长7年以上，收割困难，一株成熟植株重达数百斤，砍掉还要重新种。尽管如此，由于加州是全美农产品重要供应地，减少用水压力下，龙舌兰被越来越多人视作切实可行的替代品。尽管今冬加州降雨降雪丰沛，终结三年旱情，但专家普遍预计干旱仍会周期性出现。十年前，加州立法开始管制地下水，因过量抽取曾导致水井干涸、土地下沉。科学家认为气候变暖将令极端天气增加、旱情加剧。中谷农民Stuart Woolf因水源受限，哪怕投入太阳能、地下水回灌等还原工程，预测未来20年只能利用原有农田的六成。因此他几年前试种后，已在原本要休耕的地块上种下约20万株龙舌兰。据介绍，每英亩龙舌兰年需水仅7.6厘米，仅为一般行作物用水量的十分之一，甚至低于开心果和杏仁。他与妻子Lisa还向加州大学戴维斯分校捐赠10万美元，用于龙舌兰耐旱性科研。Woolf说：“我一直在找气候适应性、抗旱强的作物，用好土地。以我现在浇的水量，很难遇到水不够的问题。”
